As a long-time domestic and international traveler, , staying for three nights at Hotel Grano de Oro was a simply fabulous experience. The hotel has luxurious old world charm. Our room had a private garden with incredibly lush plants and the dining room and courtyard were absolutely beautiful combining elegance and European style with contemporary appointments . The entire staff including Carlos the dining room manager, were extremely attentive and engaging. If you’re in San Jose, this would be my top choice to places to stay. We definitely will be returning.
David Hagerty and Louise Cadigan
April 18 2026

review_title: Great Boutique Hotel in San Jose
review_text: On our tour to Costa Rica we spent our first and last nights in San Jose at the Hotel Grano de Oro. It was an excellent choice. Instead of the sterile could-be-anywhere typical downtown hotel we were treated to a small boutique hotel built in and around a historic 19th century mansion. Super friendly, helpful staff, a delightful in-house restaurant and lovely rooms rounded out a great experience. If you are traveling on your own stay here. If you are booking a private tour ask if they can lodge you at the Hotel Grano de Oro.

review_text: The décor is tasteful. We stayed in their Standard Room as nothing else was available at the time of booking. The room was neat, but really small. Hardly enough room to open our travel bags. It overlooked a portion of the roof of the neighbouring dwelling, and was easily visible from neighbouring windows unless the curtains were drawn. No bedroom slippers, no iron or ironing board. It did have a coffee-maker and a choice of coffees. The bathroom was roomy enough, clean and with necessary amenities. The shower cubicle, however, was extremely slippery, although they do provide an anti-slip shower mat. My husband had a bad fall while in the shower. Thankfully, he was only slightly bruised, and we were able to carry on with our travel plans. The restaurant had good ambience, and also offered good vegetarian food on the menu. The staff at the front desk was especially courteous and helpful. We stayed in Room 2. Perhaps, a different room may have offered a better experience.

review_text:
Hotel Grano de Oro is a very charming place and an excellent starting point for a Costa Rica round trip. It’s not an anonymous chain hotel, but a place with real character. The courtyard in particular (with its restaurant) conveys a true Central American ambi-ance. The dinner menu is diverse and locally inspired. Breakfast is outstanding, gener-ous, and easily keeps you satisfied well into the afternoon.
Our room was a bit dark (both sides facing the courtyard, with large plants in front of the windows). But in the end we weren’t staying at Grano de Oro to spend time in the room.

review_text:

I had a massage which was fab after a 13 hour flight.
Hotel decor is wonderful

review_title: Beautiful hotel and facilities, quiet location.
review_text:
Beautiful old colonial building with stunning furnishings and grounds (would have been nice to have a couple of benches to sit on in the courtyard gardens). Very good breakfast, though we did not eat dinner here. Pleasant roof terrace and jacuzzi (if you like that sort of thing) alongside a small gym. The location is quiet - close to Sandana Park, with a restaurant just opposite. We ate in the city - downtown is approx ten mins by Uber or 45 minutes to walk.
Efficient check in and desk service, they very kindly looked after our suitcase for a couple of days. These are the things you remember: when a hotel goes out of its way to help you. Also, with an early check out, they gave us breakfast in doggy bags to eat at the airport. Many thanks.

review_text:
Lovely 19th C architectural gem with gorgeous decor and loads of character. Large rooms with all amenities, though ours was a little dark. This was probably due to it being in the quiet courtyard with huge palms and foliage. Pity that the owners did not think to place a bench or two in the courtyard to read on or just relax.
Instead the relaxation area is a fairly bare, and out of character rooftop terrace with jacuzzis. There are a couple of sunbeds and tables with parasols but it's unwelcoming, and uncomfortable with no cushions.
Service for breakfast is in the pretty courtyard adjacent to the restaurant. Breakfast has excellent options though service is a little variable. They will provide breakfast to go if you need a early checkout.
30 minute walk to town, ten mins or so to the sabana park. We used uber a few times. A haven of charm in a not so charming city. We spent 3 nights here at the start of a 3 week tour. Saw a couple of museums and did an informative free walking tour. We'd recommend this hotel but you can probably get by with 2 nights in San Jose.

Beautiful Victorian hotel outside of downtown San Jose. staff is very friendly and the food is very good. They have a great wine list. It was decorated beautiful for Christmas. The rooms are solid and comfortable. We stayed here for our first two and a half days over Xmas before heading out to the rest of our journey in Costa Rica. Would definitely recommend staying here for a classy overnight while traveling through the country before heading to your next area of interest.
We didn’t like the downtown area. We only visited Central market, which was OK, but pretty dirty and we did not walk anywhere from the hotel.

review_title: Amazing stay at Hotel Grano de Oro
review_text: My best friend and I stayed at Hotel Grano de Oro in San Jose Costa Rica from Dec 5-Dec 8 2025. We were in town for the Bad Bunny concert which was a birthday present for me from my husband and my best friend. We had the most incredible time and we loved the hotel. The service was extremely personalized and they made us feel very special. One of the concierge contacts, Brandon provided all of the options for excursions, helped us book reservations, and helped us book massages. He answered all of my questions (there were many!) and was so kind, professional and patient. They had a birthday message and fruit plate in the room for us when we arrived which was also very sweet. We got a massage at the hotel which was amazing. Best massage I’ve ever had. The masseuse was incredible! My favorite employee at the hotel was Roman who was a bartender and server at the restaurant. He gave us amazing recommendations for night life and even found us a gym outside of the hotel as my friend and I wanted to try a more intense work out. Roman was so kind and thoughtful. He always greeted us with a smile and he really made our stay unforgettable. I fell in love with the beautiful people of Costa Rica and with this hotel. What an amazing experience!

review_title: A hotel with charm and a great location
review_text:
We stayed two nights in this lovely hotel in San Jose. Architecture and decoration emulated a historic and cultural feel to our stay, which was the main reason for choosing this hotel.
This being said, there are a couple of room amenities that could be improved for a better experience. We booked a Deluxe King Room and the room was spacious enough but not huge.
Breakfast was a bit of a disappointment since it’s a La Carte but you can choose only one option. Coffee, tea and juice are complementary, everything else will be charged extra. For the prices this hotel charges, included breakfast options should be more generous.
Main restaurant is ok, but again, prices are on the high end considering quality provided. Buts still a worthwhile experience.
Locations is very convenient and if you don’t mind walking, city Center with main attractions, is a 30 minutes walk away.
Reception team is helpful and we reached out to them previously to our stay, for transfer and tour reservations. Response was always swift and adequate.
Overall I recommend Hotel Grano de Oro

review_title: Charming hotel without soul = hotel without charm
review_text: This hotel has everything to do well but... that is not enough you have to do. The place is beautiful and the location very pleasant. The staff is competent and kind but not enough. This hotel lacks a soul and a master or mistress who makes it warm. It’s just a stopover for the moment that wants to be a bit high-end on the road to a circuit in Costa Rica without more. In addition, the facilities are beginning to become old and deserve a refreshment apart from the bedding. Amenities are strict minimum and we ask you to use the glasses of the mini bar as tooth glasses... Finally and this is the biggest problem some rooms (especially with patio) are unlivable because of the noise of machines or compressors that alternate all night. When you also have a time difference to take it is horror. I think if you have to stop in San José apart from the historical aspect of the hotel it is better to look for something else and that is a shame.

review_title: Beauty and Comfort in this Crowded City
review_text:
We spent our last night in Costa at this lovely hotel! Checking ln was very easy and welcoming.
Our room was so sweet, with its own patio garden that even had a fountain. We had just come from whitewater rafting after 4 nights, and 5 days in the Rainforest, during the dry season. Yet, we were deluged by rain our last three nights there, so none of our clothes had dried! Once in this darling room, I draped our wet clothes all over thest patio, to dry. Success. We loved our room, it was very practical, pretty and comfortable.
We met friends for dinner in their beautiful dining room. Delicious food, great cocktails, nice wines by the glass, lovely service!
Because we were headed to the airport at 5 the next morning, breakfast wasn’t yet served. But the c made nice croissant sandwiches to take, then went into bar brought us lattes to take with us!
What service, all around!

review_title: An oasis for us in the heart of the city
review_text:
We arrived in the dark on our first trip ever to Costa Rica and our tour company booked us into this hotel for our first two nights. We arrived later in the evening and had no idea what to expect. But we needn't have worried at all about our lodging. Our first impression of Hotel Grano de Oro was very positive. We arrived at the elegant front entrance and were met by friendly staff who helped with our bags. The gentleman who checked us in was kind and informative and made us feel immediately welcome, to the hotel and to Costa Rica. We were shown to our Deluxe Patio Room which we found to be comfortable, clean and inviting. We really enjoyed our little enclosed patio with live plants and bubbling water. We slept well in a comfortable queen bed. In spite of being near a busy street, we were not disturbed by the traffic noise or city sounds. In the morning we went to the hotel restaurant to have breakfast and were taken aback by the elegance of the place. We sat outside in a beautiful atrium and were treated to a really nice meal and excellent service. We were so impressed that we went back that evening and had a terrific dinner, this time seated inside in the stately dining room. The next day we enjoyed the rooftop hot tubs and seating area as well. While they are not large, they were perfectly enjoyable and comfortable.
Our stay at Grano de Oro got our inaugural trip to Costa Rica off on the right foot.

review_title: Most Charming, Historic & Character-laden Hotel in San Jose
review_text:
Most of the hotels in San Jose are modern and rather generic in style. We love a bit of history and local character, without sacrificing comfort and sophistication. Hotel Grano de Oro was definitely the right choice!
The exterior of the hotel is rather understated, but the elegance and grandeur is obvious as soon as you enter. There are many surprises including a modern, stunning entrance, a grand historic dining area and many vintage San Jose moments memorialized along it’s higgledy-piggledy, but charming hallways. The rooftop jacuzzi is also both magnetic and impressive. Our room was comfortable, bright (even the budget-friendly option with a courtyard view) and had all the amenities one could ask for. Even the mini-bar options were complimentary.
The unparalleled service was probably the biggest plus. Our flight was delayed for hours, so we arrived more than 2 hours after final check-in time. Despite this, a gentleman met us at 2:00am providing an ideal parking spot right out front, they speedily helped us with our not-so-light luggage upstairs and checked us in very efficiently. The morning’s breakfast was completed with similar white glove service and it was delicious ta-boot! Our only regret was not having time on our itinerary to enjoy dinner here, but we have no doubt it would impress. When we departed and wanted to explore town without worry of theft, they stored our luggage after check-out. We couldn’t have been better taken care of.
Finally, the location of the hotel is in a safe area and perfectly situated to take in all of the city sights. All-in-all our stay was just as we’d hoped and it’s definitely a place we’d recommend to anyone sojourning in this lovely city.

review_title: Lovely hotel about 20 minute walk to the national theatre
review_text:
An oasis of calm in a beautiful building. Our room in the old building was beautiful, spacious, clean and comfortable. The restaurant was good too and we found the waiters polite and efficient but not overly friendly but all gave us a smile at the end of the evening or as we entered the restaurant. You can eat at the bar area if a table if unavailable in the main restaurant. Booking a dining table in advance is advisable as it was busy with locals as well as hotel guests for the 2 nights we stayed.
It is about a 20 minute walk to the National Theatre on a busy road. Some sections of pavement are broken with large holes in places so beware in the dark or you have poor eye sight. We did a city 1/2 day tour which was well worth it as there are only a few buildings of note and good to know the history of San Jose.

The property is beautiful. The staff in the reception were very kind on arrival. They helped us to arrange transport from the airport in advance, which was reliable and professional. The driver was on time and was so helpful.
However, in preparation for our trip we tried to contact the hotel multiple times to explore possibilities to help us to arrange an excursion to the volcanoes. All of our emails were ignored. We also tried to ask for help and recommendations while there and the staff would just tell us to google options. Not very helpful.
The bar at the hotel is really pretty. However, the staff at the bar at night are EXTREMELY rude. They act as if you are making them waste their time even though the price of the drinks is not cheap.
Funnily enough the waiters working the breakfast shift were incredible.
Make plans for excursions independently, do not count on the hotel. And either ignore the rude and snobbish waiters or get yourself to one of the many great bars around (Azotea 7 , Apocadero, etc) for better service.
But the property is nice and the breakfast was incredible.

review_text: This is one of the best hotels I've ever stayed in and I have traveled the world and stayed in palaces. Super attentive and helpful staff and the front desk. It was a scary process of having surgery alone in a foreign country but staying here before and after made me feel safe like family and I made a good recovery. I highly recommend the rooftop hot tubs.. I did those the night before the surgery!

review_title: A good stay, with small changes it could have been great
review_text: I only stayed for two nights but I was impressed with what I experienced. Check in with Joseph was excellent. He quickly realised we would be going out early on the days we were staying with the hotel and arranged a good boxed breakfast for us with a croissant, juice, fruit and a cookie. The room was a little small but very comfortable. The bed was excellent, the TV has international channels, a safe, good toiletries in the bathroom, large wardrobe, and excellent Wifi. There is a free minibar with some snacks and soft drinks but the range is a little limited. I asked for the regular coke to be swapped for Coke Zero but this didn’t happen. The bathroom had a shower bath and plenty of towels. All the staff we met were friendly and most had excellent English. We had dinner in the restaurant one night, the food and service was really good, attentive but not overpowering, but the atmosphere in the restaurant is quite formal which may put off some diners. There were some shortcomings to the hotel, the room didn’t have a full length mirror in it which would be useful when getting ready, the location is not near much apart from another restaurant. Breakfast times are too late, 7am until 10 am. We were on trips at 6-45am both days so could not have breakfast which was a real shame. The air conditioning I found to be underwhelming meaning the room got quite stuffy and warm at times. The mini bar was not restocked during our stay, we were told it would be, and there are lots of stairs, so if you have heavy luggage or mobility issues, this may need to be mentioned at the time of booking to ensure you get a room that will meet your needs. The hotel does have some nice period features, particularly the restaurant/bar area and some nice small gardens. Overall a good stay but with some small changes it could have been special.

review_text: I cannot recommend Hotel Grano de Oro enough. For starters, it is such a charming and unique hotel. We stayed there for a few days on our way to Quepos, and we stayed in a big family group. Diana Torres at the front desk was AMAZING to work with. She emailed me many times to be sure that our reservations were correct and to ensure that we had enough rooms for our group of 23 travelers (11 adults and 12 kids). While that is no easy feat, she managed it and had it organized with ease. We loved eating the delicious breakfast in the courtyard every morning--it was so beautiful and magical. It felt like a little oasis in a big city. We loved our rooms, they were very clean and well maintained. We also used the fitness center and hot tubs. I would hands down recommend this establishment to any group--big or small--and especially families. It is very family friendly and all of the staff are so kind and patient and efficient. We loved this hotel and would stay here again in a heartbeat if we visit San Jose.

review_text:
My wife and I stayed at Grano De Oro for 2 nights when heading home from Costa Rica.
Firstly, a warning to anyone thinking of spending a day or two exploring San Jose. DONT! Unless you love a visit or two to museums, there are no redeeming factors. The city is what can only be described as the worst we have ever visited on our travels. I won't go into detail as this is a hotel review.
Based on the above, we would have only stayed one night at The Grano De Oro. The hotel is stunning with a level of service to match. We only stayed in a basic room (number 1) due to this being the end of a long trip and we assumed that most of the day would be spent exploring. Instead we spent most of our time on the premises.
The food served in the restaurant was some of the best we had experienced (again with a service to match) during our trip. My wife and I dined here for both nights of our stay. An unsolicited shout out to Alberto our waiter who was just amazing. I can't remember having better service in any of London's Michelin restaurants. Both professional and engaging.
The only criticism of the hotel is the noise. The rooms aren't particularly well acoustically insulated. By the very nature of the hotel primarily used by travellers in transit, there is a lot of movement early in the morning due to people heading for the airport.
We would both return to The Grano Oro if we were passing thru again but would make sure we packed earplugs.

review_text: My husband and I stayed here for three nights in mid-January. It’s a beautiful historic hotel just outside of downtown San Jose. We had fresh fruit in our double room when we arrived and the room was large and clean. It was on the ground floor, off a beautiful garden courtyard. Breakfast was included and one ordered off a menu with lots of choice; there was no buffet. Over the three breakfasts the food was well presented and quite decent, though not spectacular. Service was also variable and quite “relaxed”. Dinner was offered in the same dining room which was very attractive with both an open-air terrace and covered spaces. It was about a 10-15 minute taxi ride from the hotel to the Teatro Nacional because of traffic and cost about US$5-$7, well worth it. The neighbourhood seemed safe and is largely residential but there were a number of restaurants within walking distance, and we had a superb meal of premium beef tenderloin at the Tierra Gaucha Parrilla Argentina (Argentinian Grill) across the street. We would stay here again.

review_title: NICE TRADITIONAL HOTEL, NOT SO GOOD SERVICE
review_text:
Stayed here on our last night as we needed to be close to San Jose airport.
It is a nice building, traditional in style and was already decorated for Christmas. Our room was very nice and clean, with 2 queen beds and had a small outside area with lights and a fountain (not running).
The cons: A very poorly equipped gym. I always try to stay in hotels with a fitness center, and this one had one. However, there were just 2 elliptical & 1 rower machine, and no weights. There was no treadmill. I was unable to use the rower or elliptical at that time because of an injury, and was looking forward to a good power walk on the treadmill, as I had just got off a long bus ride.
We had dinner at the hotel restaurant which was beautifully decorated. And had breakfast at the same restaurant. Dinner was OK, but breakfast was not. Omelet was overcooked and dry. We were also not impressed by the service. The servers were not very friendly or welcoming. We had been in Monteverde & La Fortuna before coming here and our servers were so friendly and helpful there, so we were expecting the same here. Maybe it's different in San Jose?

Their cocktails with fresh fruits and juices were extraordinary!

My husband had to received a phone call one morning so I enjoyed the jacuzzi by myself on the top floor, quiet and relaxing space., clean and tidy aswell.
We definitely will visit grano de oro again in our next trip to San Jose !

review_title: A beautiful hotel with comfy rooms. A slightly disappointing experience with a staff member on reception.
review_text:
Grano de Oro Hotel is a beautiful hotel. The architecture and interior design is unique and sophisticated. We drove past and were immediately greeted by someone wanting to help us park (which we really appreciated!). He helped us carry our bags up and was very helpful and polite.
The check in (and check out) was easy and they let us check in a little early which we appreciated.
The room was comfy and there was a complimentary mini bar with drinks and snacks which was a nice touch.
The restaurant is beautiful and the food and drinks were good (although we would have liked to see more vegetarian options on the menu).
It is an easy walk into the town from the hotel and the hotel has a secure car park.
My husband was unwell whilst we stayed at Grano de Oro and at about 8:30pm we were in our room and this extremely loud music began playing (with a really heavy bass). We waited for about an hour and began to panic that it would go on all night so we called reception. We felt the reception were very unhelpful. I explained that my husband was unwell and that he really needed a good night's sleep and they essentially responded saying 'this music is from another property, it is not our problem' and so when I suggested we get moved to another room to help him sleep, the man on reception scoffed and said 'it would be the same everywhere in the hotel'. He then went on to say that it should be finished soon (which suggested it happened regularly) and luckily it did stop shortly after this but we felt the experience let the service down and not something you would expect from a 'luxury hotel'.

review_text:
We loved our 5 day stay at Hotel Grano de Oro. It had a charming, historical feel, with hallways filled with black and white photos of San Jose in the olden days. There were lush green plants, tropical flowers and even a fountain to admire along our way to our room.
Our room had a ceiling fan plus airco. It had a table and chairs along with a desk that was tucked in an alcove. It had 2 windows that looked onto a private garden with plants, flowers and a water feature.
The dining area had a lovely open-air courtyard with umbrellas and heaters for any time of the day, if you didn't want to eat indoors. The food was delicious. The service was great.
The staff was friendly and very helpful.
We would definitely return!

review_text: Grano De Oro Hotel - we found this hotel comfortable and acceptable. The first night we spent there on our arrival in Costa Rica we had a nice bedroom with a large king size bed. The room was quite noisy as it is near a main highway and the traffic noise started at 4 am. There is a very good restaurant and I think has a reputation locally for its food. The inclusive breakfast is a bit mean. This was the only hotel where food allergies are not accommodated. The hotel is situated within walking distance of the town centre and there are other restaurants nearby which we only found on our last morning walking around the area.. For our last 2 nights we were told we had been upgraded but I question that as we had a ‘double size’ bed which is very small. This room was quieter than the first but I think it is important to find out when booking for your clients what size the bed is.

review_text:
Hotel Grano de Oro is a wonderful boutique hotel in San Jose, Costa Rica that is charming, relaxing, and providing superb service. When we had to leave too early in the morning to have breakfast, they packed a wonderful box lunch for us. A nice and unexpected touch that demonstrates their desire to make our stay the best it can be.
There is also no need to go anywhere else for dinner. The restaurant was wonderful in quality of food and service. The best we dined at during our entire vacation.
There may be other fine hotels in San Jose, but none better than Hotel Grano de Oro. We recommend them highly.
Mike B, Upper Saddle River, NJ

review_title: An unexpected and welcomed refuge for a quick stop
review_text: I had a last minute business trip and needed to coordinate transportation from the airport to outside of the city and then to the hotel for a one night stay. I emailed and called several hotels and Grano de Oro was by far the most responsive and accommodating. In addition, I needed a Covid test done the next morning and the reception arranged for me to have a rapid test in the hotel, it took fifteen minutes for me to get the results, this was super convenient and the price was the same as me having to go to the clinic to get the test done. That one night I also arranged for a massage (booked upon check in) with Yendry, and it was by far one of the BEST massages, she was super knowledgeable, caring and intuitive. Special thanks to the restaurant where they accommodated my vegan diet both during dinner and breakfast. Also, thank you to Marco who was super welcoming at the front desk and helpful as well. Can't wait to come back with more time to enjoy Grano de Oro to it's fullest.

review_title: Above average food below average service
review_text:
We came here on the first night of our honeymoon and were very excited after reading all the reviews. The food was excellent unfortunately even though the service started well it declined quickly as the meal progressed.
By halfway through our mains the waiters were loudly clearing the tables around us, even though I was told a 2030 reservation was fine when I booked 2 weeks before.
After finishing our mains the bill was obviously left on the table next to us and our wine glasses were topped up everytime we had a sip.
The final disappointment was when paying, the $100 bill used as part of the payment was brought back and I was told it could not be taken as it had a tiny rip in the top. I would not be exaggerating to say the rip was 3-5mm and the rest of the note was pristine having received it as travel money 2 days before.
Even after pointing out we did not have other notes that would make up the total I was told that it was unacceptable and I must pay by card.
All in all a pleasant eating experience soured by employees that clearly wanted to get off early.

review_text:
I spent 2 and later 1 night here during my round trip. It is a beautiful old building and it was really nicely decorated for Christmas. The rooms vary. I had room 8 first and room 4 the second time. Room 4 had a nicer view out into a courtyard but a smaller bathroom, room 8 looked out onto a busy street but had a huge bathroom. What I did not find in either room was an iron, even though one was supposed to been supplied. The rooms are very nicely furnished and clean, the bed was very comfortable. Both my rooms had a coffee machine, which was nice to have.
The food in the restaurant is excellent, the courtyard really nice. Service is also very friendly and helpful. I was able to keep my large suitcase in the hotel during my Tortuguero trip, which was very helpful. All in all a wonderful hotel with comfortable rooms, great food and service. Highly recommended!

review_title: Pretty mansion, bed full of ants
review_text:
A charming Victorian mansion made into a hotel. The public areas are very beautiful, lots of dark wood and green plants, wooden carvings and a fountain.
You can use the two jacuzzis and the gym, just remember to book them (for free). Breakfast is served to tables and is nice (not included), and the dinner at the same restaurant was exactly what I needed after the long flight.
The location isn’t too bad, if not ideal, some 1.5 kilometres from the centre. You can walk or take a taxi.
The best part was the personnel - everyone was very polite and flexible, a late check out was arranged as all the info and service (like taxis) I needed.
The worst part was my room (number 15).
The size was ok for one person (if you’re used to the European size hotel rooms rather than the US size). It was somewhat dim, the only window was to a tiny inner yard, and since the room was on the ground floor, no daylight ever reached it.
The worst part about the ground floor room were the ants. I spotted a few on my arrival but didn’t think anything of it, you’ll always have some insects in the tropics.
On my second day I woke up to find my bed full of ants. (See photo and video.)
Perhaps they had been there the previous night as well, but I’d been so dead tired I hadn’t noticed them. They didn’t bite but still a bad experience. When I informed the personnel I was told it means I’m sweet.
If you decide to stay here, I would recommend to ask a room from somewhere else than the ground floor.

review_text: Stayed here for a night before and after our exploration of Costa Rica - it appears many guests do this to make flying in and out less hectic. The hotel is beautiful, the beds are very comfortable, and our sleep was undisturbed. The staff were very welcoming - for example, they were kind enough to store some gear for us between our stays. On our return, I had suffered a bit of a zip lining injury and they made sure I had plenty of ice packs to aid my recovery! The restaurant is high end - dinner may seem expensive to some. Our rate included breakfast (which had a fine selection and modest prices). I will gladly look forward to staying here again. The only downside, if I looked hard for one, is the rooms are a bit “New York City’ sized and the neighborhood is not terribly walkable - but again, if you are just crashing here to relax before your international flight after a week of hiking the Osa Peninsula or similar, these are not problems. The calm, quiet, professional care more than make up for it!

review_title: The charm wasnt enough for us
review_text:
My husband and I spent 1 night there when we arrived to San Jose and were supposed to stay another night in San Jose before returning home.
The hotel has a lot of charm, beautiful central terrace, good restaurant and smiling staff but that was it.
The moment we entered the room I felt it was not up to the standards of what we thought would be. We stayed in room 4. Room very dated, the coverlet in the bed didnt look tidy, the bathroom was very small and towels also need to be updated. We closed the window and there was a gap between them and the a/c was in a position that the air went direct into the bed. The sheets and blanket need to be updated urgently. We were cold and couldn’t find another blanket in the closet. Old bathrobes and no slippers. No turndown service either. Not a single special detail in spite of being a “boutique hotel”.
Since we arrived early we payed for an early check in and breakfast was include, I ordered a ham & cheese omelette and what I received was a totally dry and over cooked egg tortilla folded in the middle. Not an omelette anywhere in the world, my husband ordered something like huevos rancheros and they were ok, nothing special. We had dinner there and it was very good. We couldn’t understand why so much difference being the same kitchen. The central terrace is really beautiful.
The following day we left at 8 am to go to the jungle ang again, breakfast wasn’t nice or good. We both ordered granola and it was not good at all, something didnt taste good for us.
We cancelled our return night there. We didnt like the bed linens, towels, breakfast…nothing to do around the area for us.
We have decided to stay in a hotel in Escazu near restaurants.
Again, the building looks nice and the service and food for dinner was good but nothing else. Stay somewhere else and go there for dinner.

review_text: This hotel is top notch. It's beautiful and impeccably clean. What truly makes it special is the staff. Every single person, from Danel at reception who checked us in, to Pablo at reception who gave us information on the history of the hotel and helped with directions, to the bellman who also helped with directions, to the waitstaff and housekeeping staff, these employees are true gems. In a country filled with the most amiable people, this hotel stands out. Though tap water in Costa Rica is fine to drink, this hotel has filtered water. There is also hand sanitizer everywhere for guests to use and, though it may sound minor, the only one of our 5 hotels that had conditioner as well as shampoo in the bathroom. We so appreciated our request for early check in being accommodated, though obviously this cannot always work out, as well as our request for a quiet room. The food is delicious. You can stay at less expensive places, but a stay here is absolutely worthwhile and very special. A fabulous way for us to end our 2.5 week stay in this exceptionally beautiful country. Pure Vida!

review_text:
We went for a deluxe room which had a small planted area outside a pair of doors - a nice touch. The room was of reasonable size but the bathroom was small.
Decor is a little old fashioned but everywhere was clean. The room was quiet and we slept well.
The restaurant is good but don’t expect European standards. Service is fine without being good. Both food and wine were far too expensive for what is on offer. However, it is a very pleasant looking restaurant and you will enjoy your meal.
There is a small enclosed “deck” on the roof with a few sun loungers and a couple of hot tubs. This is the only outside space on offer.
There are a couple of non dining tables at the entrance to the restaurant, but there is no “bar” as such.
This was our first hotel in Costa Rica and we thought it overpriced. We have now experienced three hotels and they were all overpriced! I think one has simply got to accept this as the norm.

review_text:
We spent one night here on our way out of the country. Initially, we'd planned to park our things and see a bit of the city, but we arrived tired, and there didn't seem to be much near the hotel, so we decided to stay put.
We enjoyed a beverage and snack at the charming bar while we waited for our room (we were a little bit early) then we settled in, had a good workout in the clean, attractive little gym area (sheltered, but open to the sky and the view- water and towels provided, and a sweet herb wall) and went downstairs for a delicious dinner with excellent service.
Our top floor suite was a delightfully eccentric pastiche of Victorian and Spanish influences, altogether a great space, with a very comfortable king bed, dark panelling, vintage tiling, plants, a city view, a coffee cart, a safe, snacks, a jacuzzi, everything you could want for a restful, luxurious night (the shower stall could stand an update at some point, but not terrible.) The cleaning staff must be excellent- the room was impeccable.
The next morning, after a delicious breakfast in the courtyard, we wandered the hotel taking pictures. The eccentric, rambling decor delighted us, like walking through a collage. There's a greenhouse area full of jungle plants, a pretty fountain, a collection of wall clocks, lanterns, lattice walls, antiques, photos, etc. Prettiness, interest and fun.
When it was time to head for the airport, our cab arrived promptly. Altogether, a fine experience.
My only suggestion would be to ensure the desk staff greet people warmly and offer every assistance. While they stored our luggage for 1/2 hour on arrival, which we appreciated, they did not suggest where we might sit to wait, or where we might go for a walk. We had to find our own way to the bar, after a brief attempt to go walking. When we booked our cab, we also found them efficient but a bit cool. Overall, professional rather than friendly.
But that's a small matter compared to all we liked about this hotel.
A last, happy memory of Costa Rica.

review_text: We splurged for a one-night stay here after a long day flying out of San Francisco. Since it was the start of our 30th wedding anniversary celebration, we opted for luxury and comfort. This converted Tropical Victorian mansion was a welcome respite. Too late for dinner, we had drinks at the bar, and was pleasantly surprised that the hotel bar offered Casinova di Neri, one of my favorite Brunellos, by the glass. They also had a great selection of ports, as well. We were treated to the best room suite at the top level of the hotel. Our room was well decorated with antiques, included a jetted spa tub, with a panaramic view of the city of San Jose. What a special treat and restive night before heading to La Fortuna and Arenal the next morning. Additonal descriptives are charming, elegant, romantic, and old world class. The staff was outstanding and welcoming. High recommend if staying in San Jose and willing to pay a little more.

review_title: Room with Private Patio & Amazing breakfast!
review_text: My awesome trip advisor natilizano.com / @CRTripDesign on IG booked us here for our first two night's in San Jose. The rest of the trip we spent with family in the outskirts of San Jose. It's the first time (in 40+ years coming to CR) I've stayed in a hotel in San Jose and I was incredibly impressed by the accommodations, the service, the rooftop jacuzzi's, rooftop gym and the incredible restaurant. Where to begin... the room was incredibly clean and comfortable. It included 2 robes, an outdoor private patio with fountain and plants, a great bathroom, Britt Coffee pods and maker... and not a single plastic bottle... because their motto is no plastic water bottles on premises... that is a great motto! The water from the faucet is filtered and a glass bottle of filtered water is provided in the room fridge, which also includes free snacks and free soft drinks. We had coffee each morning in our little sweet outdoor nook. We had an incredible breakfast our first day at the hotel restaurant, the Costa Rican breakfast (Tipico) was divine. The dinner that night in the hotel restaurant was equally amazing. Definitely have a couple meals at the hotel and definitely take advantage of the jacuzzi on the roof. This spot is fantastic. Enjoy!

Manger’s supervision urgently required to improve all these.

In short, stay away!

review_text:
My wife and I stayed 2 nights here (Nov 15-17, 2019). We arrived late (11pm) and were upgraded to a very nice deluxe room on check-in. Room wasn’t large but was clean and comfortable, with a nice outdoor deck area (completely private) including a water fountain and outdoor fan. Nicely renovated bathroom; very comfy (albeit slightly small) bed. Solid Wi-Fi and cable TV options. Complimentary non-alcoholic mini bar was re-stocked daily. Housekeeping was very good generally.
Parking is free and located directly out front, guarded by a 24/7 security guard. There are two nice clean hot tubs on the roof terrace which we used and enjoyed. The hotel itself is oozing with history and character, from its best incredibly well restored exterior to the abundance of artwork and antiques throughout the hallways.
People who dislike the location are crazy, in my opinion. Yes, Grano de Oro is on a quiet side street outside of the downtown core, but it’s just a 15-20 minute walk to the heart of downtown. Do you really want to be in the chaos of the downtown area anyway? Grab de Oro area feels very safe to walk around, and is just 15-20 mins from the airport.
The hotel restaurant is excellent, especially for breakfast. All the staff we encountered spoke great English and were friendly and helpful, including the restaurant staff.
Overall, this is a great boutique hotel. Highly recommended.

The food and wine are first class and the restaurant is just a great space.
A late check out was also offered as our pick up for return flight was 3pm.
I would highly recommend the s hotel for any stay in SAN José taxi ride to airport c 30 minutes.

review_title: Delightful Night at Grano de Oro
review_text: We were on our way to Manuel Antonio and the Arenas del Mar resort and needed to stay the night in San Jose to catch the hop flight the next morning. They recommended we stay at their sister hotel- Grano do Oro in San Jose. In an effort to save time and effort, I booked it and got great rate on top room as is low season. We were exhausted from travel when we got in but were greeted by lovely people at the front desk and fresh juice. Our room turned out to be truly fabulous- a Jacuzzi in room and a great view. We were in the Vista de Oro Suite The bed was wonderfully comfortable and there were delicious treats in the mini bar gratis. We also had an espresso maker in our room which was great for the next morning for quick and wonderful coffee. In addition, we had dinner in the restaurant that evening and even through our exhaustion, acknowledged that the meal was truly superb. Macadamia nut crusted sea bass was to die for. Finally, magnificent customer service-every single person we had contact with was wonderful and they arranged our transport to and from airport with ease. Should we find ourselves back in San Jose, we’d definitely stay here again without hesitation!

review_title: Inside of the rooms is the low point
review_text:
We stayed 2x within 4 nights. The first time, we checked in (exhausted) at 11.30pm and had to leave again at 6.15am. To be frank, I didn't like the hotel on that stay because all the negatives were accentuated, and none of the positives. I would have rated it a 3. The negatives:
- the rooms are OKish, but not >$250 standard. Shower curtains over a bath, toiletries in gym style dispensers, not particularly comfortable beds etc
- the immediate area looks menacing late at night. This is further emphasised by very visible security on the street (which is presumably necessary).
When we returned, it was another short stay but this time arriving at 5pm. Enough time to get a feel for the hotel, see it in daylight, and to have dinner at the restaurant. On this stay, I saw the positives of the hotel:
- lovely staff
- fabulous atmospheric old school dining room (loved it)
- nice (if limited) rooftop gym and jacuzzi
- a hotel with a lot of character inside. And outside, in daylight, you realise that the area is OK.
If I wasn't going to have any time to enjoy the hotel, I might pick somewhere that has a better room product. You can't really find anywhere that has a more expensive rate than the Grano del Oro, so you need to have some time to enjoy the hotel's vibe to get benefit from that. And if you have that time, it certainly seemed like a far more attractive and characterful hotel than anything else on offer in the city.
One thing that I would suggest the hotel thinks about is the bedding. They have 1 not particularly comfortable pillow, and then a large pillow covered in an elaborate pillowcase made from the same material as the bedspread. It is really unclear whether this pillow is decorative or functional. Are the pillow cases washed between uses? I assumed no (it's not clear) and anyway it was an uncomfortable fabric to have you head on.

review_title: Beautiful boutique hotel in the heart of San Jose
review_text:
This boutique hotel is located in a former family villa. Therefore, all the room are different and you will find yourself in a real maze with ancient photographs, objects, antiquities on the wall.
The place does not have a swimming pool but two nice jacuzzis on the top floor.
Our room was simply decorated but very confortable with a lovely private terrasse.
The hotel has got a parking in front of it and is ideally located in a residential area of San Jose.
We would definitely recommend to book a table at their restaurant which is know in the city as being a fine dining place with a very cozy atmosphere ! A perfect first or last stop in Costa Rica!

review_text:
The hotel was beautiful. Rooms were comfortable and attractive, with complimentary snacks, fruit and non-alcoholic drinks in the room fridge. Rooftop patio and hot tub was lovely. It was fun to explore the hotel and see the historical photos and charming courtyards with fountains.
All staff were professional and friendly. Restaurant food was good - we had light items and desserts and breakfast.
We were advised the neighborhood was not safe for tourists to explore after dark, so the next morning, we took an easy 15 min walk to the Mercado (central market) for souvenirs and food items. Wifi was free but slow in the rooms.
We had 2 rooms for the 2 couples in our group (1 king bed in each) and a large suite (2 bedroom suite with 1 bathroom, 2 queens and 2 single beds) for the 6 teens in our group. All were lovely and comfortable.

review_title: What a great place to relax after a long flight
review_text: This hotel was an overnight stop only after flying in to San Jose airport, check in was a pleasure, staff were great and we were given a free sours traditional drink on arrival, really good. The hotel is a converted Victorian mansion in downtown San Jose only 20 minutes or so from the airport. The building itself is a treat with plantings of tropical plants, huge flower arrangements and indoor fountains and we enjoyed exploring. The room was cozy and comfortable, we didn't use the air conditioning since the roof fan was quiet and kept the room nice and comfortable. Linking to the internet was quick and trouble-free. Our room had a small fountain just outside which we could turn on and off which was really relaxing. Since were leaving early the next morning the staff suggested a travelling breakfast which turned out to be a good option, ham and cheese croissant, apple, water and a few other items. Wake up call was on time. all in all a good overnight stay. One caution was not to walk the area after dark and I think this is probably good advice to tourists in any major city.

review_text:
Amazing! Fantastic!
From the moment we arrived at the hotel at 11pm, front desk was very pleasant and communicated perfectly. Welcome drink was mango nectar that was really good. The hotel is beautiful.
I highly recommend the rooms with garden patio which we got.
We had several questions to the front desk regarding our stay and about san jose and they were all so pleasant, friendly, and knowledgeable. They helped us out with our transfer transport and our tours. All of which worked great. The room amenities were good and the coffee/espresso machine was a blessing.
We had breakfast twice and really liked it. Thick mango juice (almost like a shake)!
We had a birthday dinner and we loved the tenderloin and lamb shank. The cheese platter was very good. We picked out a Bordeaux and the sommelier knew exactly what we were looking for and gave excellent input.
Highly recommend this hotel for anyone looking for a romantic and quiet stay in San Jose.
Overall this is excellent service and quality for good price I will definitely stay here again

review_title: Ideal for a night in San Jose
review_text:
We have been travelling around Costa Rica for our holiday this year and have stayed twice at the Grano de Oro as a one-night stopover en route to our next destination.
San Jose itself is unlikely to be the highlight of anybody’s trip to Costa Rica, but this hotel is a real plus point.
We found the rooms on both occasions comfortable, quiet and good value for money. During our second visit we decided to have dinner at the hotel’s restaurant - quite often hotel restaurants seem to be mediocre and overpriced, so this came as a real surprise. The food was excellent, there was an extensive wine list and the meal was sensibly priced.
If you’re heading to San Jose, this place is well worth your consideration.

review_text: We stayed at Grano de Oro on our first night in Costa Rica after landing at San Jose and moving on to Arenal, and then again halfway through our trip before heading to the south of the country. We stayed in a standard room on our first one night stay (room 34) and then on our way back we booked a standard room but were upgraded as we had stayed the week before and were in a deluxe king (room 10). The standard room didn’t have a window to the outside but instead patio doors to an indoor courtyard (actually a cornered off part of the hotel corridor) with a fountain, but this was fine. Room 10 was on the upper level and a larger room with windows out to the city. On both occasions we found the rooms well appointed, very clean, comfy beds and the staff were friendly. The terrace is a nice area to relax outside (didn’t try the jacuzzi). On our second visit we decided to try the restaurant for an evening meal and it was outstandingly good. I’d definitely recommend a meal here, and for the quality was very reasonably priced. San Jose itself isn’t a pretty city and I certainly wouldn’t be rushing to return to it, but for what we needed as a place to stay for a night before heading off to our main places to visit on our trip, Grano de Oro far exceeded our expectations.

review_title: lovely hotel in an old mansion
review_text: I stayed here for two nights before heading to the Osa peninsula. The hotel is a former colonial mansion and absolutely beautiful. There are older photographs on the wall and lovely decorations, with fountains, and almost twisting hallways so you might get a little lost your first time leaving your room. The staff is on top of everything. I had booked a standard room and was upgraded to the deluxe king, which was quite nice with everything I needed. The hotel is also in a good location to explore San Jose which I did on foot for one day. The rooftop deck was peaceful for reading towards the end of the day, and there are also two jacuzzis on the deck. The restaurant offers a delicious and classy, yet laid back restaurant I highly recommend!

review_title: Intimate Boutique Hotel with Cordial Staff
review_text: Hotel Oro de Grano is a beautiful former colonial mansion converted into a hotel. Boutique in feel, the intimate facility is staffed with helpful and gracious individuals. Check in/check out was quick. The rooms line an internal courtyard that provides a lovely al fresco dining option. The quarters are comfortably sized and the bed is appropriately firm. The room’s arrangement is unique. One wall opens into your personal mini-courtyard with plants and a fountain that can be turned on. It has a screen above to keep bugs out. This might be a nice place to relax in the evening, but we preferred the hotel’s courtyard. If you open the doors to access your room’s courtyard, warmth and humidity enter the room. Rooms are well insulated from noise (no disturbances). Toiletries were sufficient and of decent quality. The hotel also has a nice restaurant that is a magnet for locals wanting a special night out or wishing to celebrate an event. Attire is casual but the ambiance and service are special. It’s convenient not having to leave the facility for decent dining. Prices are reasonable and the wine list has a nice selection of options from around the world. When we departed early in the morning, we had to bring our own bags down via the elevator.

review_title: Very beautiful hotel, great decorations and atmosphere, very friendly staff
review_text:
We stayed here 2 nights, but not consecutively, because we took an overnight trip in between. We stayed in a room with a pateo each time, i think they were 38 and 39. 39 seemed slightly larger than the other, but both were very nice. The outside area is lovely to have and the little spring is a nice addition. The man that brought our bags showed us every feature in the room, the location of all the switches etc. There are complimentary soft drinks and snacks in the mini bar.
Reception and the guys in the gift shop were also very friendly each time and they stored most of our bags while we were away as well as sorted out transport to the airport for us. Communication with them prior to arrival was also very easy and they were very helpful.
We had dinner in her hotel restaurant one of the nights, which was extremely tasty. It is pricey, but worth it for the one time with the atmosphere there and the well prepared dishes.
The decoration throughout the hotel is absolutely lovely and there is great attention to detail (plans, lovely pictures, a book exchange..). Only thing I'd say is that the reception area does not really match the rest of the place and at the rooftop Jacuzzi area a bar might be nice. You do get free towels provided up there.
I found the area fine, it would be a bit of a walk to the centre, but not too far. There are shops, supermarkets, restaurants and bars close by.

review_title: Amazing hotel in a fantastic location
review_text:
This hotel is located 15 minutes from Sabana Park to the west and the pedestrianised area to the east which houses the Central Market and museums. It is also two streets away from the major car rental centres in San Jose.
The hotel is really beautiful and the staff are helpful and friendly - arrival drinks when you check in too! We booked a garden room and it was spacious and comfortable. Everything in the mini bar is free except alcohol. The hotel has two jacuzzis on the roof, which you should definitely find time to enjoy while you're staying. The food is delicious, if a little pricey, but the restaurant staff were really friendly.
We stayed for 3 nights at the start of our two week holiday in Costa Rica and then returned for the final night before flying home. The staff remembered us and gave us a lovely welcome - and a free upgrade.
I would definitely recommend this hotel.

There is free parking in a gated parking courtyard for clients a street away.
A wonderful stay.

review_title: What a hotel to finish our holiday in
review_text:
This hotel is just lovely, it has been beautifully and sensitively done up, and is perfectly maintained and is spotlessly clean. The rooms are lovely, and it has the most beautiful courtyards and fountains within the hotel.
The restaurant was stunning, and we had the best meal there from the whole fortnight.
The courtyard for breakfast and lunch is gorgeous and the restaurant area for dinner just lovely.
We had the pleasure of meeting the manager, purely by chance, and what a lovely man and a great story of his time at the hotel he has to share.
His/the hotels view that guests spend a lot to stay there, so should not be ripped off at all for food/wine is unique really, and we had been very surprised at the very reasonable prices for food/wine, for such a beautiful hotel.
Having been in the gift shop i can also say the prices there were about half of those in the airport, so full credit to the airport for this.
Do come here, you won't disappointed, i only hope we get to come back one day.

review_title: A Victorian Mansion in the heart of San Jose
review_text:
Everything about this hotel is exquisite, from the moment you walk in to their well appointed lobby to the interactions with the staff, delicious restaurant and the well thought out rooms.
The staff went above and beyond to make our stay perfect. We were struggling to book a rental car before we arrived but once we arrived Marco was there to take care of all the details. He arranged to have the rental car brought directly to the hotel so the process was seamless. Marco also arranged two tours for us, White Water Rafting and a Sights and Bites Walking Tour around San Jose. Both tours were excellent! Since the hotel is so central, we were met by our guide right in the lobby for The Sights and Bites Walking tour. It was exceptional, the perfect way to see San Jose and learn some of the history of San Jose and Costa Rica.
The hotel has thought of everything to make your stay the most pleasurable from the roof top gym and hot tubs to the in-room espresso machine, snacks and bath robes.
If you are looking for a central location with wonderful amenities and very attentive staff this elegant hotel is for you!

review_text: A delightful hotel with a very good upmarket restaurant which the locals book into. Our room was smallish but opened onto a lovely outside sitting area that was covered. Snacks and soft drinks in the fridge are free. The restaurant includes an inside seating area as well as a stunning courtyard. Beautiful plants and ornaments adorn the passageways and there is an interesting bar that takes you back in time. The hotel is set in a business area with no shops or restaurants that we could find in the near vicinity. So, this hotel may best be suited for overnight stays, especially if you plan to eat in their restaurant. We spent the first and last night here around a 12 days tour of Costa Rica. We returned for the last night stay, with a sandwich for lunch in a paper bag and waited in reception for our room to be ready. The gentleman on reception recognized us and asked us if we would like some coffee. He then escorted us to the restaurant, gave us a plate for our sandwich and brought us delicious coffee. No charge for any of this. We felt a bit embarrassed but very welcomed.

review_text:
We have just been for a break to Costa Rica. Our flight got in fairly late to San Jose so we decided to spend our first night there before flying on to the North East the next day.
We stayed at Grano da Oro and were not disappointed. It is a beautiful, boutique hotel situated within reasonable (40 mins) drive from the airport.
The hotel is well appointed. Very good sized rooms and free flowing common areas.
We ate in the classic restaurant that night and had excellent food. The following morning we breakfasted in the open atrium and enjoyed the bird calls and sunshine.
Grano da Oro is a lovely hotel and well worth a visit if you are in San Jose.

review_title: classy hotel in busy commercial district
review_text: Everything about this hotel was first class, the lobby, the courtyards, the restaurant and especially the staff at reception. We had room 17 in the courtyard area, which was very beautiful with a giant bromeliad. Dinner in the restaurant in the outside courtyard was outstanding. The food was more European than Costa Rican and featured excellent pasta. When we first arrived in Costa Rica, we stayed in a beautiful hotel on a hill outside Alajuela (Hotel Buena Vista) but we wanted to experience the capital city, so chose to stay at the Grano de Oro on our way back. Unfortunately, there was nothing to see in the area outside the hotel--I expected fine houses, parks, or shops, or restaurants. What I found mostly were businesses like small manufacturers or car repair or medical offices. It was not a pleasant area to walk around in---a lot of traffic. We did enjoy seeing the National Museum and the old Theatre, but these are a taxi ride away. It may be best to stay outside the city and just come in to see the sights.

review_text: This was a brief overnight stop at the start of a Costa Rica holiday. We arrived mid-afternoon and left very early the following morning. The initial welcome was very pleasant and we were efficiently checked in and shown to our comfortable room. We soon discovered the one downside of the hotel - it's slightly unhelpful location - when we went for a walk to stretch our legs after the long flight. The surroundings are not very picturesque and, after walking for some time towards the city centre, we decided that it was not really worthwhile and took a taxi back to the hotel. We then had a pleasant half hour on the roof terrace and a tasty meal in the restaurant, with attentive service. Needing to leave early in the morning, we found the availability of take-away coffee and a breakfast box very welcome. Overall, comfortable for an overnight stop but, had we been staying in San Jose any longer, we would have wanted something nearer the city centre.

review_text:
This hotel reminds of my beloved Imperial hotel in Mumbai ; an oasis in the middle of mayhem .
Unfortunately traffic in San Jose is now comparable to Mumbai’s ... the warm welcome st Grano de Oro was a respite to a tough day .
This place has been run by Canadians for decades and I am fascinated how it grew to become the national treasure it is now .
Been coming for the superb eggs Benedict at breakfast . Dinner was always good if not great , a bit generic .
This was my first time staying overnight and I was very impressed by the rooms . Thoughtfully and expertly decorated , joined to the building in a true arquitectural tour de force.The gym / jacuzzi area is outstanding.
I was happy to see the Aperol Spritz on the cocktail menu , a nod to the Italian GM .
The 4 course menu degustación that followed was truly inspired with a beautiful rabbit dish and terrific wine pairings . This one not only the best meal I have in Costa Rica but a top 10 anywhere in my lifetime. Expertly prepared , served and presented.
Unfortunately the next day’s breakfast was not up to par ; tiny dried crepe , too sweet juice made with concentrate , waiters bickering between each other , I even had to ask 4 times for toast ...
This blemish could not erase an otherwise extraordinary experience.
Highly recommended.
Also , close- by you will find la Casa del pie the best place for a pedicure anywhere.

review_text:
The Grano de Oro is a truly beautiful boutique hotel. Our room though was rather cramped and came with a welcome complimentary mini bar filled with snacks and soft drinks .
The lounge and restaurant just oozes character with its rich dark wood decor. Lovely for afternoon tea, complimentary throughout the day, or to curl up with a book. What surprised us though was, as we took a walk around a few blocks, the hotel stands out as completely grandiose set amongst very ramshackle dwellings and rough paving. We didn't know if this was normal for San Jose.
Our stay here was very brief as we had an extremely early morning pick up so, although we missed breakfast, a packed take-away breakfast was left for us. We wish we could have stayed here longer to fully experience what was a beautiful hotel.

review_title: Bathrooms need Updating, Dining Room is Very Good
review_text:
We expected a lot as this is the top rated hotel in San Jose and when we walked into the small, but beautiful lobby, we thought our expectations would be met. The check in went smoothly, the bellhop and front desk staff were efficient and welcoming. The room we were taken to, through a pretty outdoor courtyard, was small, though charming and well equipped but the bathroom... The bathroom may have had a new coat of paint in the last ten years but nothing else has been updated in quite a while. The bed was comfortable and the room was fine, but quite expensive compared to others in San Jose. Also, in terms of location, this hotel is kind of away from where the action is and there is not much in the area to stay for.
We would highly recommend dinner at this hotel. The menu offers a huge range of choices and we tried as many as we could manage. We did not expect an amuse bouche on the house, and as it happened, that was our least favourite part of the meal (see photo of cold fish on spoon with garlic foam). The salad was fresh and fine, though nothing special, but after that, it was all great! Delicious appetizer, delectable fish in Macadamia crust, sublime lamb shank, and an apple tart that was too much food but we simply had to eat it. Professional service in a beautiful room.

review_title: Elegant Affordable Luxury Oasis Close to Downtown San Jose
review_text: San Jose is a huge sprawling city so finding a hotel in a safe convenient neighborhood was a challenge. Hotel Grano de Oro is just such a place, a real oasis right on the fringe of the downtown area. The staff were friendly and helpful from the moment we arrived and made us feel welcome. Our room was elegantly appointed, quiet and a great plate of fresh fruit on the table when we first entered. On the last day we got a gift bottle of hot sauce to thank us. Our room also had a private garden with a fountain which not all of them do. Your experience here might vary a lot depending on the room, they have a jungle like courtyard with rooms facing it, hall facing rooms and city view rooms so be sure and investigate these locations to find the right one for your tastes. There is a great rooftop sun deck with two hot tubs and a small gym, you can see the cityscape from here. The bar and elegant dining room area is amazing, inner courtyard soaring several stories like a roman villa, very romantic especially at night. The drinks and food were excellent but not inexpensive as to be expected. Service top notch. The only drawback was the umbrellas at the inner courtyard tables, blocked the view up above a bit. The inner dining room area was warmer and no wind. Free coffee service in lobby each morning. We walked around the neighborhood but it is more commercial than anything but felt safe. Their location seems perfect for day tours, about ten minutes to downtown. There was some slight traffic noise from surrounding streets but not an annoyance and quiet at night. For me this hotel was the perfect place to stay in the city, I would definitely choose it again if ever there in the future. Well worth the cost in my opinion.

review_text:
We booked into the Grano de Oro for our first night in CostavRica. We arrived after a long flight and the customary 2 hours in SJ traffic somewhat jaded it has to be said. The building is unpretentious from the outside, but we could at least tell that it wasn’t the more usual modern tower or box, being an attractive low-rise colonial type of building instead.
The foyer is pretty impressive actually, with an enormous golden sun and some attractive use of bamboo too. Staff were all most helpful and we had a good first impression.
We had only booked the basest of rooms, working on the basis that we were due to leave at 6am for a transfer to the coast and would be no more than 10 hours in our room in any case, but the room was large and tastefully furnished, with a bath and quite traditional bathroom. The shower was not the world’s best, but no complaints and the bed was comfortable. We enjoyed a quiet night’s sleep and left the next morning very refreshed.
The restaurant and bar area are laid out around an open courtyard in the center of the property and this is a very pleasant feature. There is an array of heaters that ensure you are always warm and the restaurant is first rate.
It was a shame we were only here for such a. Short time as this is a first rate hotel, particularly when you look at what else is on offer in San Jose. It has class and character and is a great introduction to this beautiful country.

review_text:
Stayed here for a night at the start and a night at the end of my trip to Costa Rica. I was not very impressed on my first night. My room on the ground floor was quite small and basic and I didn’t make use of the restaurant because of a late arrival and early departure.
However on my second visit I had a much better room upstairs complete with “internal deck” though the bathroom was still basic for such a quality hotel. Breakfast was wonderful. The very traditional restaurant is a wonderful space, the service was good and it was a pleasure to have breakfast from a menu and not a buffet. I chose the “continental” with juice, fruit, yogurt and breads which was excellent.

review_title: Wonderful service, classic spaces, great location
review_text:
We are well traveled, and quite particular about where we stay. We loved the architecture, historic beauty, location, and warm, attentive service of the Gran Hotel. We used it as a first stop for our long weekend in Mexico City, before moving to Roma Norte.
Its Centro Histórico location- an easy 15-20 min. from the airport and within 5-10 min. walk of every major site (and top rated food and drink) in the area, was fantastic. It’s a bustling, intense, urban center- and Gran Hotel is a peaceful respite.
The room (a deluxe king) was clean, bright and comfortable. A bit dated in its decor compared with more contemporary lodging, but not in a musty, icky way- just older marble bath, carpets, etc. The
Room includes a credible coffee maker, wine cooler, nice flat screen TV, etc.
We were eager to explore recommended local food, but still had purchased the coffee and breakfast buffet - which was fresh and diverse: eggs, fresh fruit, cheese and meat, yogurts, more hearty Mexican specialities as well. Juices - a few types, including a green juice- and good coffee. When I requested espresso (to strengthen the coffee, I like it strong!), it was complimentary. Bottled water is plentiful and easy to access all over the hotel.
One evening, we had cocktails on the roof
Terrace- simple, tourist style drinks menu, but the view was lovely.
We interacted daily with lobby and reservations staff Javier, Jose Luis and Gabriella, as well as the breakfast and terrace teams- all were helpful and professional.
Overall, we would recommend Gran Hotel. We
covered most of Centro Histórico and might skip it next trip, but it’s a special place to stay in CDMX, and we recommend it highly.

review_title: Nice place to end our honeymoon
review_text: We booked the hotel as our final destination in Costa Rica and spent a single night. All in all, a lovely experience. For nearly $200 US, I would expect better water pressure in the shower, but the standard room was quite pleasant. We had an issue with noise at about 1AM when someone decided to drag their rollerboard up the stairs by our room step by step. Slowly. Very. Slowly. That, and the kids running around the halls detracted from the overall experience. Folks travel with kids all the time and there's just no reason to give them run of a hotel and have them pulling on the doors of other rooms. So, the nitty-gritty is the room was lovely. Be prepared from some noise if you book into a less expensive room. The rooms are well-designed and don't feel cramped at all. The minibar is complimentary, save alcohol, which is a nice bonus. But noise could be an issue and we found the breakfast in the restaurant to be much better than the dinner. Be sure to take in the jacuzzi deck -- it's quite pleasant. All in all, a 4-star experience.

review_title: Mediocre hotel with great restaurant and very nice doorcat
review_text:
We booked one night at this property because it looked neat and was reported to have a great restaurant.
First the good: the rooms and public areas are very clean, the bathrooms are nice, the lighting is excellent, and drinks/snacks in the minibar are free (except for alcoholic beverages, you pay for that). There is a very friendly black-and-white tuxedo cat who works out front with the bellman. And indeed, the restaurant is excellent (I will review that separately).
Now for the bad: upon checking in, the cat knew his job better than the bellman, who stood there looking puzzled as we removed luggage from our cab. He finally figured out that he was supposed to handle it, and took some of the bags (leaving the rest for us, not the proper "please go ahead, I'll handle everything).
We had a room (number 30) that opens into the interior courtyard. It has no exterior windows, and lacks privacy. We could close the windows (and curtains) to the courtyard, but still heard everything going on near by. If you stay, question what room you're going to get.
The deck with the Jacuzzis has a high fence with little sunlight. The two Jacuzzis themselves seemed to have some maintenance issues (one was soapy and the other looked stale).
There is no yard/garden or a place to sit outside and enjoy the weather except the Jacuzzi deck, which has a high fence with limited sunlight.

Hotel staff were very helpful so a great way to find your bearings before as we did - head out into the wilderness.

Used a handy car hire company just around the corner which we walked to and collected vehicle in the morning.
Would definitely book hotel again when we return.

review_title: One of the best hotels in San Jose
review_text: This hotel small and sits in a quieter area of the city 15 minutes walk away. The building is old, comprising painted wood panelling. There is a stunning reception that leads onto a bar, restaurant and courtyard with seating. The restaurant is very well regarded amongst locals for high end food. The bar has an abundance of drinks from liquors to cocktails and everything in between. The rooms are adequate size, the amenities are just what you need for a nights stay and the service is what you expect of a hotel of this quality. Fruit is made available in the rooms, there is a stocked mini bar and a hot tub on the roof. Please take registered taxis after dark as the side roads are quiet. We recommend this hotel for couples in particular and we advise no more than 2 nights as other areas of Costa Rica have a lot not to be missed ! #exploremore #travelhustle #hotelreviews

review_text:
The attention to detail at this family run restaurant really makes you appreciate the lovely qualities of independent run businesses. I've stayed here for business as well and as for pleasure and I wouldn't stay anywhere else in San José.
I always have found that the well-appointed suites are always super comfortable and set up in a savvy way (pro tip - all the snacks in the mini bar are complementary!).
Finally, the hotel restaurant is a special treat and is one of the best restaurants in town. I've often enjoyed their breakfast in the garden (a must!) and have returned back "home" to have a delightful, locally inspired meal.
Staff is always attentive and super pleasant.
Top Notch.

review_title: Perfect place to start or end your Costa Rica trip
review_text:

It's a beautiful hotel, I was updated to a superior room which had a lovely internal patio.
Staff was friendly and very helpful.
The restaurant is also beautiful and I had a very tasty and sofisticated meal.
I would highly recommend it to end your stay in Costa Rica or as a starting point.

review_text: We spent our first night in Costa Rica at the Grano de Oro Hotel. When we arrived we were greeted by friendly staff and juice, but our room wasn’t ready yet. The hotel checked our bags and asked if we wanted directions to someplace in town. We were tired and chose to wait in the lobby. We should have taken the opportunity to wonder around the hotel to view the many old hotel photographs that lined the hallways and take in some of the history of the building. This isn’t a standard cookie cutter hotel; it is a converted mansion with many nooks and niches that give it character and beauty. Once in our room, there was an abundant plate of fruit waiting for us, I don’t know if this is standard or something the travel agent booked for us. We had a “superior” room which opened to a small courtyard. The room was spacious and very comfortable. We decided to have dinner and breakfast at the hotel restaurant, which was described as the best restaurant in town. Check out was easy and quick.

review_text: We stayed at the Grano de Oro on our first night in Costa Rica before starting our tour of the country.The hotel staff were very welcoming, offering us a drink on arrival and dealing with check in very promptly. As we were being picked up the next day before breakfast the hotel provided a boxed breakfast of croissants, yogurt, fruit and juice to take with us, along with fresh coffee in the lobby. We loved our overnight stay here, a great start to our holiday and would definitely recommend this hotel if you are staying in San Jose.

review_text:
From our first encounter with the doorman to our last bite at the restaurant, I was totally satisfied we'd chosen the perfect hotel to experience a little bit of San Jose. We left our rental car out front to be picked up by that agency to find that there was a bit of confusion about our room. It seems a glitch in the system booked two rooms instead of one...which was treated as a simple, 'no problem.' The desk staff could not have been more welcoming and willing to make us happy.
Do not miss a meal in this restaurant! Although no one was formally dressed, I felt like a grand dame in pearls and black velvet because the wait staff was so gracious (and willing to go along with my restaurant quality Spanish). And the food was divine. At breakfast, I enjoyed the 'typical' Tico breakfast more than the other choices, but maybe that's just me.
Our standard room was fine (OK, wish we HAD splurged on the garden suite). I can't think of another big city hotel room where the windows were thrown open to catch the breeze. Take time to inspect all the vintage photographs displayed in the halls. And don't miss the hot tub veranda.
Downtown was an interesting walk away. We enjoyed the chaos of downtown the entire way and back.

review_text: I stayed here with my daughter on our first two nights in Costa Rica. We loved everything about this beautiful hotel: the organisation, room, food, hot tubs, location, atmosphere, courtyard breakfast, warm welcoming dining room, in-room facilities, fountains. I had requested a car to meet us at the airport via our booking agency, which was confirmed personally by a named member of the front office team. The driver was there to meet us exactly as promised. Our room was so lovely, with two large beds, bathrobes, spacious bathroom; the hot tubs on the roof were welcoming and relaxing; the food was delicious with charming service; and after a "hard" day walking into town (20minutes) we felt we were coming home.
