review_title: Loved this hotel and the staff!
review_text: I recently went back to San Jose to complete some dental work. I chose Grano de Oro because of its close proximity to my dentist. Upon my arrival I immediately felt at home in this former luxury tropical mansion turned hotel. I booked the standard room (which is very nice), but was upgraded to the deluxe patio room which was extremely pleasant with its own private garden and fountain. I was very impressed with the wood floors, tasteful decor, and cleanliness of the room and outdoor patio. The bed was also very comfortable with luxury linens. The staff was very friendly and the food in the restaurant superb! Having breakfast in the open air courtyard reminded me of sitting at a cafe in Europe. Should I go back to San Jose, I will stay again at this lovely hotel.

review_title: First and last time I stayed here
review_text:

review_text:
This hotel is so beautiful. It truly feels like an oasis in the city. Grano de Oro has an old plantation feel with lush, tropical greenery and fountains in the courtyards.The hotel is pristinely clean and the decor is simple and beautiful.
I enjoyed the touches of fresh juice upon arrival and the fact that beverages and snacks in the room (with the exception of alcohol) were gratis!
The beds are comfortable and the bathrooms quite large with soaking style tub which can be difficult to find in hotels. Great water pressure and abundant hot water. There is also a jacuzzi on site, but we did not take advantage of this trip.
Walter and David at the front desk/concierge were quite nice and helpful to us during our stay.
This is definitely a gringo hotel experience, which was a pretty nice introduction to what we are planning to be a more rustic/Tico style vacation.
Highly recommended!!!

review_title: Nice rooms, elegant restaurant, great food
review_text:
We were met by the hotel shuttle, straight off a flight from London and were glad we’d chosen to use the shuttle as it was spacious and cool, and we were in it for a long time because the late afternoon traffic was terrible!
The room was comfortable, much as you’d expect from a boutique hotel of this type. The hotel staff were extremely friendly, from the front desk, to the waiters, though to housekeeping. We were made to feel welcomed to the hotel and to Costa Rica.
We ate in the restaurant two evenings and while it isn’t cheap, it is a very elegant room and the cooking is good. It isn’t a typical tourist restaurant: we noticed that it was used by lots of local business people and had quite a dressed-up crowd of couples on the Friday evening.
You can walk to the city centre, though you may prefer to hop into a taxi: they’re cheap and plentiful. We liked San Jose more than we were expecting to: it’s definitely a ‘real’ city – not a tourist town – and is not especially picturesque, but the museums and galleries are interesting. We especially liked the Gold Museum.
If we were back in San Jose we’d definitely make the same choice again.

review_text:
My wife and I stayed only two days in Grano de Oro, one day at the beginning of our trip and one day at the end of our trip. We were very impressed with the hotel, the staff was very pleasant, warm and welcoming.
The first room in which we stayed was very comfortable with a/c, free WiFi and cable TV. We later went up to the roof terrace and enjoyed the jacuzzi.
On our second stay we were upgraded to the garden suite which was bigger with access to a small garden equipped with table, chairs and a sun umbrella. A small green corner if we had enough with our luxurious room. The bathroom had a Jacuzzi which unfortunately we did not take advantage of.
The hotel restaurant is amazing. The food is delicious and the kitchen is run by a French or French schooled chef. The decor is colonial with dark wood beams that gives the place an old class sophisticated atmosphere. Try the red snapper incased in salt and the pie Grano de Oro for desert, it's amazing.
Definitely recommended
Pura Vida

review_text: This delightful small hotel in an unassuming neighborhood in San Jose is just a short walking distance from the shopping district, museums and sports arena. We sat in the courtyard under an umbrella (against the possibility of a stray shower) after a drink at the bar inside (there are two sides to the bar, one inside and one out). They have a nice selection of local microbrews as well as the usual local cocktails and liquors.

review_text:
This was a planned celebratory trip for my two nieces college graduation. We bookended our coastal visit with our stay at Hotel Grano de Oro. We could not have been more pleased!! We fell in love with this carefully restored mansion, the beautiful greenery & landscaping, the interior courtyards, and the top notch professional & endearing staff. On our final stay, we upgraded to the king garden suite which was a real treat. It's worth the splurge!
Their restaurant is on premises and is superior for every meal, including room service.
Our only complaint was that we couldn't stay longer! For anyone flying into San Jose, we would MOST HIGHLY recommend a stay and a meal at Hotel Grano de Oro.
They truly provide 5 star service and amenities!

review_title: Best hotel in central San José
review_text:
Hotel Grano de Oro is a charming hotel in old colonial style. The hotel is one of the best hotels in central San José. It’s located a 10 minute walk from central avenue where “all” the main attractions are located.
There is not much to see or do in San José. Many of the guide books tells you to spend as little time as possible in San Jose, after staying there for two days we completely agree. We have travelled a lot, we usually find most places we visit interesting and appealing in their own way but that was hard in San José. I wouldn’t recommend people wasting their time visiting San José. There are too many other beautiful places in Costa Rica to visit. The best thing about San José was this hotel.
Our room was spacious and tastefully decorated. The room had a little private patio with a table and two chairs where we enjoyed a drink in the evenings. The bed was comfortable and batroom was equipped with a bathtub.
The hotel has a well-developed sustainability program with recycling, ecological cotton in bedsheets and towels, sustainability certified products etc.
The restaurant at the hotel is a French restaurant and it’s consider to be one of the best restaurants in San José. The restaurant serves a good a la carte breakfast.

review_text:
Spent one night here on arrival from London.
The courtyard rooms were off a small garden. Pleasant enough if a trifle basic but we were not in them long enough to worry about views etc. Clean and comfortable. I'm sure there are better in the main building and for a bigger price.
We enjoyed a nice dinner in the hotel restaurant. Smart, diligent and courteous waiting staff. The food was pretty good and reasonably priced at just over $100 for four including drinks.
Breakfast the next morning was a leisurely affair due to a big table getting in just ahead of us and a bunch of fellow travellers getting up even earlier than we did with some jet leg I guess. No problem though as the quality of the food and the lovely ambiance of the dining room made up for the wait.

review_text:
My wife and family (three children, ages 20, 26 and 28) returned to Costa Rica for two weeks for a second time to explore the country and visit with other friends who were also visiting. We used the Hotel Grano de Oro as a base, staying one night on arrival from the United States, staying again for one night a week later to greet the other arriving families, and a third time, for two days at the end to do a little exploring of San Jose before returning to the US. We picked Grano de Oro after enjoying it on our first visit six years earlier.
First the good news, and it almost entirely good new. The hotel is constructed from colonial Victorian mansions and has the very cool vibe of both modernity and turn-of-the-century colonial luxury. Every room bright and a little different. Spacious rooms and big beautiful white tile baths. Incredibly helpful and friendly staff. They helped us arrange dinner for 17 in the restaurant (more on that), held our excess luggage when we went out to the other parts of Costa Rica, handled all of the many transfers from and to the airport, etc. Couldn't be nicer or more professional. And the restaurant is one of the finest I've ever eaten in. Supposedly the best in Costa Rica, and I believe it without question. All this in a hotel at what I consider very modest prices, compared to the rest of the world.
Now the bad new, and there's very little. This is not a big, family resort with pools and the like. If you want the Hilton in Maui this isn't it. Realize that the hotel is smack in the middle of mostly uninteresting old San Jose. You'll wonder where you are when the cab pulls up to drop you off. Don't be dismayed. First, because the moment you set foot in the place you'll be delighted, and second, because if you give San Jose a day or two to explore you won't be disappointed. Now it's true that a day or two is all San Jose warrants, and Costa Rica has much else to entice outside the capital, but stay more than one night. Fact is, that if Grano de Oro was in any other city with attractions, you'd stay a month.

review_text:
My wife and I spent two weeks in Costa Rica at the end of May. The last two nights in the Hotel Grano de Oro in which we had stayed on our only other visit to Costa Rica 15 years ago.
Our stay, and the hotel, we just as wonderful as in our memory. The on premises restaurant is even better than before and has been relocated and enlarged since our last visit.
During the reservation process the General Manager, Marcos Montoya, got personally involved and arranged for us to stay in the room immediately next door to the one in which we had stayed last time. He would have seen to it that we got the exact same room had we wanted to, but we opted for a higher category room.
The room was immaculate and well appointed with a small but very private patio. It seemed to us that even though the room was immediately next to the other room in which we had stayed and backed onto the same street, the room was quieter. I'm convinced that they have replaced windows with double or triple pane but did not verify.
Arriving by car on a drizzly day, we really appreciated the valets with umbrellas on our arrival and were able to borrow umbrellas for our walks in the area.
We'll return on our next visit to Costa RIca which will hopefully be in far less than 15 years.
Only negative is that the traffic seems to have gotten two to three times worse than in 2000.

review_title: Above average charm below average service!
review_text:
Our trip started with a mix up regarding a transfer from the airport. We ended up just getting a taxi. The staff seemed in no hurry to step away from their desk to greet us. Not very warm or helpful. Our beefs: the free coffee in the lobby stops at 7:30..silly when you consider the price you pay. There is a little gift shop that is run by the front desk and is rarely open. It seems very unorganized. Our lunch was very good although it set us back $104 dollars with no alcohol and, again, coffee refills were not free! (we are in the Mecca of coffee..just pour it freely!)
If we would have stopped at this resort first then we wouldn't have been this underwhelmed but coming from Nayara Arenal the customer service at the Grano de Oro was lacking.

review_text: Only stayed the one night after a tour through Costa Rica. Wanted to get a little bit away from downtown. Arrived early. This hotel is a beautiful example of an old colonial estate. The house is built around a couple of small courtyards. It just reeks of charm. Beautiful wood and glass work everywhere. The front desk said we did not have to wait until check in and that we received an upgrade. First up, the bed is the best I have ever slept in. The room was beautifully decorated, without being overdone. The basics were there. Airco worked, the was bathroom spotless and well appointed, and after a couple of weeks of poor internet, the wifi here worked perfectly. What a relief. In hindsight, I wish we had booked dinner at the restaurant, supposedly one of the best in SJ. So much character to the place. Only down side, missed any cafes of shops in the area. Would certainly go back though.

review_text:
Located a 20- minute walk from downtown, this is one of the most serviceminded hotels we've stayed at. Front desk is quick and efficient, we were upgraded and sent mail wishing us welcome before arriving.
Parking is free, and should you need transport to the airport it will be arranged for 30 Usdollars and take around half an hour.
The restaurant is one of San Jose's finest, and serves international fare with local twist.
The beds are very comfy and the rooms spacious and spread out through this previously private home.
A nice touch is that tapwater is filtered and thus drinkable

review_title: Perfect end to our journey through Costa Rica
review_text:
After all the tents and tree houses and lodges we stayed in during our tour this was a welcome touch of luxury. Beautiful hotel with old world charme and modern amenities. Small courtyards with fountains and plants and rooms grouped around them. We had booked a standard room but were upgraded and even given a fruit platter (either because it is low season or because they knew we were on our holiday trip to celebrate our 25th wedding anniversary). Room had wooden floor and access to small tripcal courtyard. Bathroom and tub and lovely smelling lotions and potions. We had dinner and various coffees in the restaurant and bar area and the food is amazing. Staff very friendly and welcoming (everbody also spoke fluent English and soem even German).
Walk to town centre in 15 min. Parking is secure and just next door.

review_text:
My wife and I stayed in this hotel on the first night of our honeymoon. After a days worth of travelling from London via Miami this hotel was a short trip from the airport which was ideal. On arrival we were warmly welcomed by the staff and served a refreshing drink and cold towel, they also knew it was our Honeymoon so had upgraded us from our standard room which was a nice surprise.
We left the hotel early the next day as the main reason for choosing it was its convenient location.
All in all, we didn't stay long enough to really enjoy the hotel but the decor of the hotel is worth a visit on its own! We did have a look around the hotel at the facilities and can say that the rooftop jacuzzi's looked great, and the bar and restaurant was very posh (maybe too posh for us middle class British folk)
Overall, would recommend staying in this hotel for a short time if like us you are in transit to another part of Costa Rica. Enjoy!

review_text: Our flight arrived in San Jose around supper time, so we splurged and stayed in the Vista De Oro Suite before heading out for the rain forest the next morning. It was a very romantic setting in a very charming hotel. I don’t know the whole story, but they have done a great job converting a grand old estate into a beautifully detailed and comfortable hotel with a tropical ambiance. The courtyard restaurant was excellent. Sometimes restaurants in Latin America try to emulate a European style and fall short—but this was the real deal and a very good French restaurant in a tropical setting. The wine list was deep with great European and South American choices. If you have business to do in San Jose, or need a place to stay before or after a flight, or just want to see the city for a few days, this is a great place to stay. The same good French restaurant served us a wonderful Tico breakfast with gallo pinto and fresh fruit the next morning, which got our next day’s journey off to a perfect start.

review_text:
Beautiful hotel. We were tired & starving when we arrived so we just dined at the restaurant. The room we were assigned to is in the second floor. After staying at Nayara, the room seemed so minuscule. But it was just right for our last night in Costa Rica before heading back to the US. They serve this really wonderful truffle that I wanted to order & take home to the US. I inquired if they would sell me some in a box but instead they gave me complimentary 6 pieces. They don't make a lot & they serve it at the restaurant.
The hotel is a good walk around San Jose & not too far to the airport. We enjoyed our last night in Costa Rica & appreciate the hospitality. Stayed June 2015.

review_text: Clasic Hotel near downtown San Jose. The Hotel is built in a house from the 19th Century, which was adapted to be a Hotel. Rooms are not very large but nice and comfortable. I stayed in one with a small patio with a fountain and was very nice. Service is great, people is very friendly and helpfull. Its walking distance from downtown, and to the Sabana Park.The restaurant is beautiful, food is awesome, and service is great. If you want to stay near downtown this is the best choice, however I have to say that downtown San Jose was not such a nice experience. Not many things to do, crowded, and not very clean. Going in the opposite direction Sabana Park is much nicer. Costa Rica as a Country is beautiful, green all over, safe, and people very kind and nice.

A great hotel, We got given a lovely room with a tiny garden which had a nice little water feature. Room was tidy, clean and spacious. We visited the restaurant for breakfast as we heard really good things about it and it did not disappoint. Location wise everything was within walking distance the area felt safe and we ventured out at night quite a bit. One of the best things about this hotel were the staff they went out of their way to make sure our stay was perfect always greeting us with a smile and a hello and we felt we could ask them anything and they always seemed more than happy to help. Only disappointment would be the lack of pool and gym, the rooftop was nice as it was quiet and not busy but only had 2 Jacuzzis instead of a pool which could be understandable due to lack of space.
The building itself was beautiful and a must stay if you are in San Jose. Well worth the money.

This is one of my favorite hotels. It is a converted Victorian mansion that has been added on to and provided with all the amenities of a modern hote without losing its charm. It is small, only about 40 rooms along a maze of small corridors. The rooms are different.. However the all have wainscoting, wood floors, marble sink tops, air conditioning fine soaps, comfortable bedding and good linens. There is a rooftop garden with two jacuucis and some Lou he chairs. There is a beautiful central garden. And the best elegant restaurant in the city ( same name) is located on the precession. I reviewed the restaurant separately. Very helpful staff.
We stayed here on our last night in Costa Rica and it was the perfect way to end our vacation.

review_text:
We decided to stay for two nights in San Jose after arriving from the US to get acclimated and this hotel was prefect for that purpose. We look to stay in small unique hotels and this hotel was definitely that with its historic feel and dark wood ambieance.
We had a deluxe patio room which was on the second floor in the older section of the hotel. The room had extra high ceilings and dark wood floors and trim. There was a patio off the room in the back. The patio was actually a bit unnecessary-it was a small patio designed to feel like a garden that was totally enclosed with a skylight on top but since it was very hot when we visited, we relaxed in the room with the A/C going.
The hotel appears to be a bunch of different building which are connected with a maze of hallways which lead to rooms facing open air courtyard gardens.
We ate breakfast and dinner in the hotel restaurant which was very elegant and also had an open air courtyard where we had our breakfasts. The food was good and so was the service. San Jose is a gritty city and the hotel is about a half hour walk to the center of the city where the main museums and the historic theater are located.

review_title: Beautiful Rooms, Not So Great Location
review_text:
We stayed at Hotel Grano de Oro for one night on our way out of Costa Rica. We were looking for a luxurious hotel and restaurant for our last night and found it at this hotel.
The Hotel: A beautiful hotel and restaurant! We received a welcome drink when we arrived, and were told about the various services the hotel provides. We were also informed that we were upgraded to a Garden Suite upon arrival, so that was a nice surprise. There's a restaurant and a gift shop with a little something for everyone. Surprisingly, the hotel is not in the best part of town. We walked to the ATM and noticed that all hotels had armed security guards in front of them, and a lot of homes had barbed wire atop their fences surrounding the home. While the hotel is safe (it has security), the area is not one to venture too far out. There is a jacuzzi terrace, but it's not much to keep you entertained for long.
The Room: Our room, number 9, was a garden suite and was extremely luxurious and well appointed. The bed was super comfortable and the sitting area and patio were nice touches. The tub is large enough for a bath. WiFi was fairly good, although a little slow at times it was able to keep up with Face Time as needed. Mini bar and coffee maker in the room. If you can splurge for the garden suite, I highly recommend it!
The Restaurant: We read that we should dress nicely for dinner, but at lunch as well (we appeared to be under-dressed). Lunch was good, we had the beef tenderloin sandwich. For dinner we had steak and the red snapper, which were good but not the best we have had. Beautiful restaurant, though.
Overall: The hotel is too nice to pass up due to the area. I do recommend this hotel, but only if you plan to stay overnight only and not for more than a day or so.

review_text:
We were a family group of 6 and had reserved 2 rooms at the end of our holiday in Costa Rica. One of our rooms was upgraded from the Deluxe 2 Beds to a lovely Family Suite with 2 bedrooms! Our other room was a Superior Room. Both were decorated beautifully and the beds were very comfortable. We were greeted by friendly and extremely helpful staff at the reception desk. They helped book a tour for us to La Paz Waterfall Gardens and also printed off our boarding passes for our flights. The front desk kindly phoned our previous hotel as we had forgot to return an ornate room key. We were instructed to leave the key with them and someone would come pick it up when they came to town. That took the stress out of trying to mail it back ourselves!! We made good use of the (very hot!) rooftop hot tubs and loungers.
The Restaurante Grano de Oro was fine dining at its best and seating was full, so reservations are recommended! We were given a complimentary creamy soup with scallops bits in it. Everything we ordered was done to perfection and delicious! The breakfast was also great! Thank you for a memorable stay and welcoming us with such warmth!

review_text:
California to Costa Rica....
When researching flights to get in and out of Costa Rica, you will find that available flight times, price and convenience don't always go together, especially if you are traveling outside of the city San Jose. Therefore, you will require possible before, and after stays in San Jose, prior to catching a morning flight out.. With that being said:
Took the Red Eye out of California Wednesday night, cheaper and you arrive in San Jose at around 9:00 am the following day. We chose the Hotel Grano de San Jose to stay on our arrival portion.. WOW!!! what a great Hotel..
I had called them on making the reservation to see if we could get at least one of our three reserved rooms available on arrival, seeing as we just flew all night, and would possibly be needing food, and a little nap.. Technically, check-in is at 3:00 pm.. Paublo, made it happen!! when we arrived, we immediately were treated like VIP, and were greeted with a cold refreshing beverage in the lobby, and escorted to our rooms, and the rooms were wonderful. The beds were big, and so comfortable, and included all in room amenities you could ever require.
After changing clothes, we went to the Hotel restaurant, for an absolutely delicious breakfast. We had pre-scheduled appointments for a massage at their spa, so decided to hang out by their quaint terrace Hot Tubs, and just relax and enjoy the amazing hospitality that this Hotel offers.
Later, we decided to yet again go down to the Hotel Bar and Restaurant for cocktails, then appetizers, then Dinner...which was all so delicious, we just stayed and enjoyed..
When we booked this Hotel, the idea was to walk around town and enjoy San Jose before catching a flight out to Manual Antonio the next, but much to our surprise...We never found a reason to leave this Hotel..... It was absolutely perfect!!
Thank You Paublo, and all your staff, including the Spa and Restaurant for such a fantastic start to our unforgettable trip to Costa Rica..
Just on a side note, the Hotel while not far in distance from the Airport, does have some traffic getting to and from the Airport. Give yourself plenty of travel time. Paublo can help you with your transfer, and ensure your transfers go smooth.

review_title: A TRULY SPLENDID PLACE TO STAY IN SAN JOSE
review_text: We chose this hotel because it was reputed to be lovely and quiet, and both are absolutely true. It is about 2/3 mile from the city center, an easy walk, but avoids all of the hubbub of being in that area. The hotel itself is an inspired architectural feat of building a beautiful hotel within an old hacienda, preserving some interior patio spaces so that all rooms feel as though there is an outdoors close by. The rooms are nice, large, clean, and with good beds. The staff is absolutely the best you can imagine, fluent in English, kind and utterly helpful in every way. There is one of the finest restaurants in San Jose within, and a lovely gift shop as well. On the roof are two Jacuzzi tubs, and a fine massage therapist is available on short notice for brief stopovers between other destinations in Costa Rica. We came and went there three times, the staff remembered us and gave us the same room and put our friends next door, which we thought was unusually thoughtful. The food truly was amazing and we kept coming back for more of it. This is a hotel which we will use if we ever return to lovely Costa Rica.

review_title: An Experience not just a Hotel
review_text:
This is by far the best hotel option in San Jose, Costa Rica. It is a lovely hotel with history and elegance. There is no other hotel like this one in Costa Rica. The combination between the classic elements and the new modern design is just stunning. Even the outside area of the hotel, you just know right there, you have entered a great unique property. Customer service is over the top at Grano de Oro, the welcome cocktail was delicious and colorful. At our room, they had some fresh delicious tropical fruits waiting for us. What a nice gift. Perfectly placed on our cute little table in our room.
The rooms are just neat. Really, they are just neat and perfectly arranged for every guest to have a great time. I mean really, the rooms are just cozy, elegant, super comfortable beds, nice amenities. We just love sleeping in Grano de Oro. We took our time to enjoy the nice deck with jacuzzis. It is a great area to relax, enjoy the weather in Costa Rica, it was nice beautiful evening/ night weather. We had some wine as well there. What a treat. One of the highlights of the hotel is the restaurant, it is for sure the best one in the capital. Nobody can´t deny this part. It is amazing, over the top experience. The pejibaje soup it is worth trying. It´s just rich in flavor. You won't find anything like this anywhere else. Please, ask for the pejibaye soup. And the plate of cheeses is amazing as well. Very unique selection. The snock is to die for. A very fine selection for sure. Not to mention how adorable the scenary is. I just adored the restaurant. You can spend hours in there. It is magnificent. Eggs benedict in the morning are a must for breakfast. The best I´ve ever had in my life. There are many hotels in San Jose, but there is only one like Grano de Oro. This is a hotel for those looking to enjoy their stay in the best way possible, really! You just can´t go wrong with Grano de Oro hotel. This is hotel without an elevator, it is hotel with history, ambiance, romance, it is place that makes you feel comfortable and welcome like any other hotel.
Just over the top experience!

review_title: A jewel in an otherwise unremarkable town
review_text:
A great hotel. The room was first rate (we had #9, what used to be the library, apparently), reception was prompt and helpful with excellent English. We got there early and snagged parking right beside the hotel which was supervised by two guards 24 hours a day. Very convenient and very safe.
The restaurant was excellent, with a good range of choices and obviously also a popular place for locals. Prices were a bit on the high side, but nothing out of the ordinary for a very classy hotel.
A small boutique hotel, very popular, the only minor, but very understandable inconvenience as that the noon checkout time was rigidly adhered to - we had a 6 pm flight out so we were very early!
San Jose the town, however is itself an unremarkable commercial city with little to redeem it. If you need to stay somewhere, then this hotel is the place to be.

review_title: Cozy room in a charming building; good choice for a layover in San Jose
review_text:
I stayed here, traveling with husband and young son, for one night en route to the Nicoya Peninsula. We arrived very late on a Friday night and left at checkout time the next day. We enjoyed a tasty breakfast in the beautiful dining room, and the staff were helpful in accommodating our late arrival. They had some food and beverages that i had pre-ordered waiting for us in our room.
The hotel has an ingenious design, with most rooms facing an inner courtyard area, a good idea as the surrounding streets are fairly drab. A consequence of this design, however, is that rooms are somewhat dark and windows face into the corridors so you are more likely to hear noise from guests passing by than in a more typical hotel.
Our room was well-appointed, if somewhat small, with 2 very comfortable queen beds. The hotel is located near SJ's fruit and vegetable market. We appreciated the opportunity to stock up on fresh local produce on our way to our rental house in Nicoya.
The restaurant is beautiful. I would highly recommend eating at least one meal there if you are staying in the hotel.

review_text:
We stayed here twice on our trip. The front desk service is nice, with a fruit drink at arrival. The hotel was decorated for Christmas - very pretty. The rooms are nice, although on the smaller side (we had standard rooms). All hallways open to the outside, which we didn't realize in our second room. It turned out the window was open but we were using some A/C, and we heard noise from the hallway. it looks like a nice, inn hallway - no idea it was open air! Wish they would have mentioned that when we called about the noise.
Linens were very nice. The beds were on the hard side.
In being in the city, we did not walk around outside the hotel. Instead, we stayed in for dinner and breakfasts at the onsite restaurant, which is very high end. Dinner is expensive; breakfast reasonable. Both worth it.

review_text: The 'Golden Bean' - referring to the coffee bean which made so many Costa Ricans rich - has around 40 rooms, but you'd never know. It feels like a family home, exquisitely furnished and well maintained. Our standard room was one of four in a courtyard of lush tropical plants. It was comfortable and cool, with a large double bed. Toiletries were sparse, but there was a bath to sloth one's aching feet after a day trudging round the capital. Meals are taken in a charming courtyard, with very good food and lovely service. Check in was first class, and they will store your bags for you if you're going out before or after check in/check out. Breakfast was excellent, and included in our room rate. The house is located about 20 minutes walk from the centre of town, with the last 10 minutes being along a pedestrianised avenue. The city is rather a dump, like a giant Poundland. In daytime it felt sort of safe, but one carefully guarded one's possessions from a constant stream (on a busy Saturday afternoon) of some fairly sinister looking characters. We took dinner at the hotel, which was superb, and frequented by many locals. We visited the very interesting and well-designed Jade Museum, but ran out of time to try the Gold Museum. The much-touted major public buildings aren't up to much. Taxis are easily found in downtown - red and white - and will efficiently take you home for $5 (agree the rate in advance). Grano de Oro is not a luxury hotel, but top class and it's probably better to stay slightly out of the noisy and dilapidated town centre.

review_title: The number "1" full service hotel for a reason...
review_text:
I tried to book this 40 room boutique hotel for six nights during a ten day visit to Costa Rica. We were scheduled to be on a WindStar Pride cruise for ten nights. The ship ran aground in Panama in December and the cruise line cancelled the next few departures. We had non-refundable air that we booked independently so we decided to make the best of a bad situation and make a land tour out of the trip. The cruise was to have departed from Puntarenus on the Pacific coast and we had reservations at the Doubletree Resort by Hilton Central Pacific for two nights before the cruise. I extended that stay to four nights and planned on six nights in San Jose. You can see my review on the DoubleTree under their heading on TA. The Grano only had room for three nights so I took it.
We arrived via a private transfer at 13:30 and were immediately welcomed with a mango juice and a key to room 24, a lovely King room with two courtyard views. One view to the front of the room and the other 180 degrees away creating a great tropical cross breeze.
The place is an elegant conversion from its previous life as a mansion. No detail has been missed. Housekeeping always meets our requested time for the room to be serviced. The front desk arranges for tours, taxis and almost anything for which you could wish.
There is a gourmet restaurant on site which I will review under the restaurant heading on TA. We ate almost every meal at this great spot. It is open from 07:00 to 22:00 everyday.
They do not have a pool area, only two hot tubs and a small lounge area near the tubs on a terrace. It is not geared toward children.
It is on the expensive side, but well worth your colones if you can afford it. I highly recommend this property.

review_text: When we arrived at this hotel in our transfer car it looked unimpressive from the outside, also being in an area of non descript buildings didn't help. However as soon as we got out of the car we were greeted by the doorman who took us to reception through a very modern door access system. We booked a deluxe room which was on the ground floor bordering a lovely quadrangle reminiscent of somewhere in Andalucian Spain. We walked into the San Jose centre which only took 15 mins which is a bonus of the hotel's location. Previous Tripadvisor reports talked of the restaurant being a bit expensive but we didn't think so especially when compared to the Costa Rica hotels we'd stayed in. You feel special being in to eat in such a characterful restaurant and the food was superb. We had an excellent nights sleep and the breakfast the next morning we took outside in the restaurant's own patio area. Overall an great night's stay. I would recommend staying at least 2 night's in this hotel and fully taking in San Jose's sights. The location of the hotel is on the airport side of the city so you do not have to crawl through San Jose's traffic with airport transfers.

review_title: We love the old world charm of this hotel
review_text:
We have now stayed at Hotel Grano de Oro in San Jose 10 times.
It is a fully renovated rambling Victorian house, beautifully and tastefully decorated in period but with a modern feel.
The rooms are all built around inner courtyards and are very comfortable.
The staff are efficient, helpful and friendly.
The restaurant is superb. If you're in San Jose it's a must place to eat. The cuisine is a blend of Costa Rican food with a strong French flavor.

review_text:
Due to a wonky flight schedule we had to stay in San Jose for 1 night in the middle of our 2 week trip to CR. Hotel Grando de Oro was exactly what we needed.
The hotel arranged for a car service to and from the airport which was very helpful. The hotel was about 20 minutes from the airport, so it was nice and close. The property was gorgeous, it felt like a luxury hotel right away. Great customer service, everyone was very friendly.
The room was huge and clean. We had just been in a remote area for a week so a "normal" shower and large hotel room was just what the Doctor ordered. Comfy bed too! We felt safe the entire time.
We ate at the restaurant in the hotel which was very convenient considering we were tired, and also had an early flight the next morning. The food was pretty tasty, and we had good service. On the slightly expensive side for what you get.
The hotel was perfect for a 12 hour "layover" in San Jose. I left feeling relaxed and refreshed and ready to head back into the jungle!
The only cons: we were in a first floor room and we could hear the people above us walking around and talking. It wasn't horrible, but it would have been better if there was a better sound barrier. There was a hair in my food at the restaurant, I don't freak out about stuff like that so I simply didn't eat that portion of my dinner. I'm sure if I alerted someone they would have been great about it.

review_text: We loved staying at this hotel for two nights at the end of our trip. The building itself is incredible, with tons of winding hallways and interior courtyards. The restaurant on site was hands down the best food we had, albeit pretty expensive. The staff was friendly. All of the top attractions in San Jose are within walking distance. Our room was pretty small and didn't have an exterior facing window, but it was a great value for the price, and it really made for a great stay in San Jose. And we loved San Jose, contrary to a lot of the advice that we had heard before we went. It's definitely worth visiting for a day or two during your trip to Costa Rica.

review_title: Charming, upscale hotel with lots of character
review_text:
I've stayed here a couple of times and both have been great. It's best described as 'colonial jungle chic' with multiple courtyards with fountains and the jacuzzis on the roof. It's a real sanctuary from the city outside and feels very special.
The rooms are good sized, spotlessly clean and very comfortable, decorated in natural colours. The restaurant is in an amazing setting in a beautiful courtyard and the food delicious. I find it's a great place to transition between the peace of rural Costa Rica and 'back to reality'!
The location isn't fantastic, but San Jose isn't a city you want to spend a lot of time in, so it works fine as a self contained place for a one night stopover or a business trip, although it's definitely not a resort hotel.

review_title: We wanted to take our bed home with us
review_text:
We really enjoyed our night at the Grano de Oro hotel in San Jose. The service was very good, the food in the hotel at dinner and breakfast was really delicious and the bed was outstanding - one of the most comfortable we've slept in during our ten months on the road. We had Room 20 and really liked it - spacious and quiet with a nice view of the plants outside in the courtyard. A nice oasis in the hustle and bustle of San Jose.
We enjoyed an afternoon and then a morning wandering the Main Street of San Jose and mingling with the locals. Not much to see, but interesting to be part of the crowd.
This was a really nice place to stay on the last night of our wonderful long trip to Europe and Costa Rica.

review_title: Great spot for an overnight in San Jose with an incredible restaurant
review_text: We had an overnight on Dec 25 in San Jose and wanted to find a nice spot with a good restaurant. The Hotel Grano de Oro met the criteria! It was a bit further from the airport and did require some expensive transport for the area but it was worth it for our family. We emailed the hotel staff in advance to arrange the transport and dinner reservation which was very easy. Our arrival took forever due to extremely long lines in Immigrations- like 1.5hrs! The front desk staff were attentive and check-in was quite easy. Our rooms were very clean but small and the view was non-existent. Not sure there would be a view of much beyond the courtyard as the area is more urban hence the 4/5 stars. I would say it is probably one of the nicest hotels we would have found in San Jose. We walked into the city to cruise around and checkout the local markets and sites and felt safe. Our dinner was a treat! The selections and presentations were exquisite. They did handle our sons peanut allergy without issue as well. Truthfully a delightful experience for our family to spend Christmas day/night. Not sure that we will be back in San Jose other than to pass through but if we find ourselves there the Grano de Oro will be our first choice for our stay.

review_text:
We arrived at the hotel at midnight and had no idea what to expect when we arrived. Sure, we had looked at the website and read the reviews but after a long plane trip on Thanksgiving day and the 15 minute drive through San Jose things seemed a bit bleak.
The cab stopped at a stately set of wide stairs edged on each side with christmas trees of red lights leading to an elegant lobby. Of course a friendly porter was waiting at our door as soon as we stepped out of the cab. At the reception desk we were greeted with a smile and nice cold juice. The desk clerk was polite and professional and we were checked in and ushered to our room within 5 minutes.
The hotel layout is quaint as its obviously an old building that has been remodeled and added to over the years. Our room was on the ground floor with a door to the interior garden. I think each room must be different with its own particular charm. The room was small but tasteful and clean with a mini-bar, safe, coffeemaker and the other amenities one would expect at a hotel of this caliber in Central America.
The most important thing to my husband is having a quite room; he was so pleased. We stayed here one night before our diving trip and then, 10 days later we had another stay before our flight home the following day.
The restaurant in the hotel is old world elegance with with stained glass windows and tables in an interior garden court. Its hard to explain the layout but its breathtaking. We had a breakfast and dinner there and were very happy with the food and the service, both at the beginning of our trip and on our way home.
We highly recommend this hotel.

I do believe the nightly charge for the rooms is a bit high for what you get, but overall the hotel and staff are excellent.

We had a garden room but really didn't use the garden area, but loved the size of room. Definitely would recommend staying there.

review_title: Amazing hotel and staff...shame about restaurant quality
review_text: Great hotel. Room beautiful with outdoor terrace. Jacuzzis are dated and old but a nice touch. Staff really helpful. We booked to eat at the restaurant as it's number one place to eat in San Jose. Really disappointed with the service. We has to top up our own wine from the bottles we ordered. Food took ages. When the mains were served ours were cold. We asked the waiter to reheat considering it was meat and we were met with such hostility we felt really uncomfortable staying there to eat our mains due to his attitude. This was such a shame as the food when served hot was delicious! Air con, showers and complimentary toiletries were perfect...it's the little touches that make this hotel great! There's a little pizza place 2 mins walk from the hotel which is fab...check it out!

review_title: A grandiouos Victorian Mansion in a Latin Environment
review_text:
When I first looked at this hotel on line, I did not know what to make of a buttoned-up Victorian outfit in a Latin American environment. It all seemed a bit odd and out of place. Yet, thanks to the excellent reviews by so many Tripadvisor contributors, I decided to give it a try. Staying there was well worth it. We had arranged for a pick-up from the airport. Unfortunately nobody showed up and I had to call the hotel. The concierge on duty was very helpful and after a few minutes we saw a driver holding up a hotel sign with our names. When we arrived at the hotel we were immediately given an upgrade without asking for it. The room had its own small, outdoor patio.
Floors in the bed- as well as the bathroom were done in dark hardwood and were buffed like they were brand new.
Breakfast was served inside an open courtyard. Every color matched whatever other color sprung from your eyes while catching a glimpse of the beautiful setting around you. We found the truffled eggs benedict to be the signature breakfast dish. The presentation of the dish was again a feast for your eyes, not to mention the wonderful taste.
This place is very professionally run and can compete with any other 5-star hotel around the world.

review_title: Just what we needed after our adventures!
review_text:
My partner and I stayed at the Grano de Oro for our last night in Costa Rica before flying home, after two weeks of adventures throughout the country. It was just what we needed - a perfect night of luxury before flying home! We were happy to be surprised with drinks and a room upgrade when we checked in, and found the room to be beautiful and quiet. The bed was the best of the four hotels we stayed at during our trip, and we had a great night's sleep. Lots of little touches make the hotel a step above what you'll find elsewhere in San Jose - the robes, the wonderful hot shower, great bath and body products, beautiful architecture.
We had breakfast in the restaurant the next morning and we're happy with both the service and the food - very peaceful start to the day in the secluded courtyard! We had one last day tour before we headed to the airport at 10 PM, so the hotel staff held our luggage for us during the day. When we arrived back around six, they gave us restaurant suggestions and an umbrella, and guaranteed our airport pick-up would arrive at the requested time.
Truthfully, I don't think many tourists go to San Jose to see the city - it is not much of a tourist destination, and more of a interim stop on your way to the beaches and vacation towns of the Costa Rican countryside. That said, the experience we had at Hotel Grano de Oro was so wonderful that I would stay an extra day and night in San Jose just to spend more time there! Highly recommend.

review_text:
My wife and I spent a night at Hotel Grano de Oro in 2014 on the night prior to our flight return to the US. We were impressed enough to book two nights this year ( November, 2015)--one the night we arrived, and one prior to departure. I can't say enough about the helpfulness, service, and courtesy of the hotel staff: (Karen at the front desk, the person carrying our heavy bags <no name, sorry>) as well as the excellent dining and waiter attention at the restaurant. We thoroughly enjoyed both breakfast and dinner menus--excellent taste and visual appeal. We are already planning a 2016 trip to the country and will definitely be spending at least two nights, again, at this hotel. Oh, and the hotel itself, with clean, beautifully decorated public areas and rooms, the private patio/atrium. We did have a problem with internet connectivity during a heavy rainstorm that the technical staff was unable to solve, but their efforts in fixing were outstanding--they responded immediately to my call and kept working at it until I was online. In short, I whole heartedly recommend this establishment; everything I look for in a foreign stay was of the highest order. Regards,
Jim Geisler, Colorado, USA

review_text:
So, I was going to give this review a THREE rating, but when it comes down to it, the room was comfortable, the shower worked, it was a cozy clean room, nice outdoor space, and we slept very well - hence the FOUR.
Where it would have been a three is: Checking in was rather chaotic and sort of confusing (room was ready, not ready, gave us an upgrade that was also not ready, then found something else). We had made specific request to have a driver from the hotel to the airport as our flight was 6:00 am. We requested a pickup of 4:00 am. We go to check out, first no one there. 2nd, NO CAR, NO DRIVER...slightly annoyed, the guy who checked us apologized and after trying for a couple of minutes, was able to find us a driver to take us to the airport. Getting up and 3:30 for a flight, and having this hassle was not exactly a relaxing experience.
The other odd thing was the restaurant. We ate at 17:30, GOSH early, but we knew we had to get up early. We were sat at a nice table, but the waiter distribution was one then another then another LOL (Revolving Waiters). We ordered, and waited. Everyone around us was being served an Amuse Bush, but not us. We first corse came, and still no AB...so we asked, was just odd. But on another note, the meal was excellent as was the wine. Quality of the food was top drawer, and beautifully served.
So, while slightly mixed, I still think that it deserves a Four....better than average but most definitely not Excellent.

review_title: Luxury Hotel with the most amazing staff
review_text:
I don't know where to start, this hotel has been a shining light in San Jose for our family in the middle of a medical emergency. The short version, for those skimming, this hotel is luxurious, the staff is professional, caring, and their English is very good. The furnishings in our room are comfortable and inviting. Even with the superior ecologically friendly hotel, the showers have heat and pressure, and all the soaps smell so good.
The long version, we came into San Jose in an ambulance with my mother who was transferred to a local hospital. My father stayed with my mother, and my sister and I arrived to the hotel exhausted. We were greeted with warm smiles a fruity drink and a warm shower. The staff asked about our mother every morning while we waited for the cab to come to get us. The entire staff has shown compassion and care for our family. A special thank you to Marcos the hotel manager/owner who worked with our family to accommodate our housing needs, so we could focus on our mothers health.

review_text: My son and I stayed for one night at Hotel Gano de Oro on our way back from Santa Teresa to NY. We were greeted at the reception desk with mango juice in champagne glasses (the start to a lovely one night stay) We booked the Deluxe Room with a Patio through Expedia (for a great price) and received a very professional transfer to and from the San Jose airport (at an additional cost). The hotel and room were gorgeous and extremely clean! The bathrooms are updated and beautiful. We took a taxi to the Gold Museum and had dinner at the hotel restaurant (fabulous but be aware the hotel restaurant is quite fancy). I would definitely stay again and recommend to family and friends.

review_text:
Such an amazing stay. Perfect service, greeted with a cool drink after a horrific flight in. The place is designed in a colonial style, but with a matching room with a little patio garden with a fountain.
The service is amazing. Everyone in the hotel seems to be happy to be there, and will go above and beyond to help you out with whatever you need.
The food is really tasty - breakfast being the best as well as their banana coladas.
DEFINITE recommend staying there for your trip in Costa Rica.
The only downside is that the area is not that great. It's in the centre of San Jose, however if you're a bit anxious about a little bit of grime, not so great - but the whole city is kind of like that anyway, so I wouldn't be too worried. And in any case, the people there will help you get a taxi, tour, etc. whatever you need.
It's also right near to Budget car rental ;)
Anyway, definitely stay here, LOVED it!

review_text: My stay at Hotel Grano de Oro will forever live on in my memory. Beyond the immaculate hotel (excellent rooms, good dining, convenient location), the staff - led by the manager Marco Montoya were incredible. I encountered a serious medical condition and the staff were essential to saving my life. They ensured I got the best hospital expediently and provided support for me during my visit. review_title: Great Place to go after Grueling Costa Rican Roads
review_text: First, know that driving in Costa Rica can be challenging. Directions are easy and GPS accurate, but many named roads are not paved. Was surprised and our little Toyota Yaris struggled. Suggest knowing where you are going and if uncertain, upgrade to an SUV. So after a tough 6-7 hour day driving from Playas del Coco to Monteverde to San Jose before a noon flight the next day, the Hotel Grano de Oro was a sight for tired eyes. Beautiful old but nicely restored hotel with incredibly friendly staff and lovely environment. We loved the little courtyard outside our room, the large courtyard outside the restaurant, the nice bathroom/shower, comfortable beds, and effective WiFi. We spent the late afternoon having drinks and reading in the courtyard and enjoyed a nice dinner at the hotel. The hotel is an easy 20 minute drive to the rental car return. The Hotel was a great bookend to a fun trip. Anytime we are in San Jose, we certainly will stay there.

review_text:
When diamond in the rough is ever said again, I will always think of Hotel Grano de Oro. My husband and I spent one delightful day/night at this hotel before heading south on our Costa Rican vacation.
The property is beautiful with great respect paid to this historic treasure. The room we had was a king size with a patio - well worth the bit more money. We had dinner and breakfast in the restaurant, and the food and service were 5 stars.
Everyone spoke English, and at check out, when asked if they knew of a location where I could exchange my dollars for colones - the deskman said 'right here!' And best yet, charged me no fee!
It's a long schlep from SJO to any place exotic in CR (like Manuel Antonio, our destination) so this hotel is the perfect place to spend your first evening in this country before heading out of the city to points of travel.

I actually felt #9 out of the top 25 might not be where it should be rated, it must be within the top 5 in my opinion. If we return to Costa Rica we will add at least a day or two more to our trip to enjoy more of what this fine establishment has to offer.

review_title: Only stayed one night, wished it was more...
review_text:
We were greeted by an incredible hospitality staff and our bags taken care of. Although we were booked in the hotel through our tour company (CRS Tours), this hotel was our first stop after our flight in and trek around the country. Wainer, the gentleman working reception was incredibly gracious and kind, and even wish my husband and I a happy honeymoon - which was the purpose of our trip! Upon entrance to hotel had an incredible freshly squeezed juice, checkin process was incredibly easy and our bags brought to the room. The room (#9) was absolutely incredible!!!!!! Spacious, well decorated and well kept it was the perfect respite after a long day of travel. The bathroom was clean, the garden patio outside (private) was so absolutely beautiful and serene. Perhaps the only thing I was was the background noise of San Jose were absent.
We dined in the hotel restaurant and would recommend anyone to eat there. The only complaint I had was the salmon I ordered was a bit overcooked, and the mushrooms underneath were salted way too much! Breakfast the next day was included in our stay and the voucher allowed for anything on the menu. My husband had the huevos rancheros and I had the gallo tico. Both were absolutely incredible, fresh and well seasoned! Truly, we both wish we could have stayed a bit longer in this hotel...

Would definitely return to Grano de Oro if i were to ever visit Costa Rica again!

review_text:
My group of 9 travelers needed two separate overnight stays in San Jose 11 days apart. This was for the sake of conveniently book-ending a 10-day scuba trip with a nice hotel not far from the airport. Hotel Grano de Oro served this need perfectly. We all thoroughly enjoyed this beautiful boutique hotel where the staff and service are fantastic, the rooms spaciously comfortable plus the bonus of an excellent restaurant serving high-end Costa Rican cuisine located adjacent to the lobby. Lunch offered no problem with seating, but best to arrange a reservation for dinner through the front desk (particularly since ours was a larger group). Further, I was pleased to organize our airport transfers both inbound and returning. Inbound the cost for a transfer was $40 (4 persons) and outbound we needed two cars (for 9 persons), which cost $30 each. These transfers involved a perfectly hassle-free arrangement made through the reservation system or directly at the front desk.
Likewise, a front desk clerk (his name is Wainer, very pleasant) offered guidance and a map to local galleries and museums, one of which was called to transport us directly to their shop. Afterwards, their driver graciously transported us to another gallery in the Amon district (or he would've returned us to the hotel, either option), from which we walked back to the hotel. A brisk walking pace will have you back within 30 minutes or so versus the 20 minutes a taxi might have needed through heavy traffic and one-way streets. Last, one of our group wanted a massage to work out his scuba kinks and he described it as excellent, also booked through the front desk. Would we stay here again? Absolutely.

review_text:
The hotel is a charming, nicely restored Victorian mansion with unique rooms throughout. Some are quite basic, like ours was, while others offer private patios and gardens with fountains. The service is excellent, with very attendant and responsive staff, who kindly arranged in advance private transportation from our previous hotel (2.5 hrs away), and of course to the airport, all conveniently charged to our bill.
Things to keep in mind are the location, which feels a bit off the path in an area that, whether it is or not, doesn't feel safe, particularly after dark. Many travelers in other reviews have noted that the location outside downtown San Jose is a plus, as it is quieter with no riffraff. It felt a bit desolate for us, but in a city like San Jose I think you have to pick your poison. That said, there are some very good restaurants within walking distance. Machu Picchu, serving exquisite Peruvian food in massive portions, and Aqui Es, a cozy Argentinian bistro, are the two we visited and were well taken care of.
At this price-point, we were surprised at the lack of some amenities that make hotels like this, with a majority of patrons staying here as a respite after or before SJO, more self-contained and enjoyable. My assumption is that Grano de Oro finds itself frequently as the first and/or last few nights of travelers' Costa Rica itineraries, and expected two things specifically: bar service on the small but lovely jacuzzi terrace, and a simple gym on the premises (to help work off all those mojitos and delicious Tico breakfasts). Guests can use the gym at a hotel close by for $10, but having been spoiled for a week, the extra effort and cost was enough to discourage us from doing so.
The hotel restaurant is a top establishment in the city and indeed superb and worth enjoying for both breakfast and dinner while you are there.

review_title: Ok but be wary of room type you choose
review_text:
All I can say is be very careful about what room you select. We booked a superior room and based on pictures on the web site we expected a door opening to a courtyard. What we got was a bamboo screen closing off about half a meter of partitioned hallway, with light through a skylight above.
The website states "Windows that open to enjoy the beautiful San José climate". This is nonsense, as we saw a heap of rooms that only had windows out to the hallway. I'm guessing these were the standard rooms.
And now the bed. Good grief, two nights of sheer hell in a double bed. It was so narrow that the pillows were overlapping. But hold it, didn't the web site say the bed was a queen?
Why do they have to be so deceptive on the web site? There's no way I would have booked that room if I knew what it was going to be like.

review_title: Tropical paradise escape in the middle of San Jose, but not for light sleepers.
review_text: My family recently stayed at the Hotel Grano de Oro on the San Jose stretch of our vacation. We have visited San Jose several times before and this was by far my favorite hotel stay. The grounds of the hotel are beautiful with atriums filled with tropical foliage. There are rooms in the courtyard and with courtyard views from upstairs. There are also two jacuzzis on the terrance. We were a bit surprise because the jacuzzis were above ground models, but we enjoyed them just the same and met some cool fellow travelers during our soak. The rooms were clean and nicely decorated. Each room was a bit different. We had rooms 17, 21, and 25. Rooms 17 and 21 faced each other in the courtyard and Room 25 was upstairs; that being said the family members upstairs had a much better night sleep. The hotel doesn't have the best sound barriers and it was quite noisy for them on the first floor. Overall, we would definitely recommend this hotel because of it's excellent location, cleanliness, and overall atmosphere.

review_text: What an oasis of luxury and calm in San Jose! We arrived late at night to a beautiful reception with charming staff. A golden glow of yellow light beckoned us into the restaurant area, where diners were luxuriating at the end of their meals. The restaurant inner courtyard and rich woody velvety interiors will be for ever etched in my minds eye as one of the most delightful surprises I have ever encountered on checking in to a hotel. With morning light, birdsong, and lush exterior vegetation, the hotel took on a new level of delight in the morning. I loved this place and booked a friend in as a treat when she visited Costa Rica for her 40th birthday a few months later. Wish we hadn't tried to "diversify" by booking another high end San Jose hotel (Hotel Presidente) for the last night of our visit: with Hotel Grano de Oro, we had found the best on our first night. Book and enjoy.

review_title: Don't book unless you're ok with children's size bed.
review_text: The hotels looks nice. It's an older boutique hotel. Be prepared to be escorted to your room by a guard that will tell you your room comes with hangers and some free coffee filters. Will also show you the bathroom and will take about 5-7 minutes of your time. Also, this is a first hotel where I was given a full tour of my room. This, however, does not help the fact that the beds are for really short and small people. (Same guard will state that of anything our particular bed is larger than others in hotel) I'm 6 feet tall and my feet were hanging off their "queen"(somewhere between standard and twin but a lot shorter) size bed. Aside from the shortness only way two people can fit in this bed is if they are duct taped together and do not move, so they don't fall off. The room isn't big by any means. Windows are have a really antique feel to them, so you can be assured you and others will hear each other. Wifi or 3G did not work well in our room. Staff was not willing to assist with the bed problems and said all beds are the same in the hotel. Thankfully, Expedia refunded the booking. You might be ok with the hotel if you are one person and short, otherwise do not book.

review_text: We stayed our first night in Costa Rica. Our plane landed at 8:30 pm, so I wanted a place relatively close to the airport. Management was awesome. Security guards waited on the street awaiting our arrival (and they also kept watch over our car during our entire stay), they gave us fresh fruit juice upon arriving, and told us of some good local restaurants. The room was a King Deluxe, and was perfect for us (quaint and elegant, very well kept). The restaurant here is also amazing (we got the lamb- super delicious!) If we are able to make it back to C.R., we will for sure include Hotel Grano de Oro in our plans.

review_text: I can't say enough about how perfect this hotel was to kick-off our 10-day Costa Rican honeymoon experience. The class with which we were welcomed, the deliciousness of the pineapple welcome drink, the beautiful architecture of the hotel itself and the grandiose, comfortable rooms are all five-star. The rooftop jacuzzi is great, but the walk to the rooftop took our breaths away. The hotel is beautiful -and romantic!- and more than everything we could have imagined. We only had breakfast at the adjoining restaurant and it was good. The building itself is what wins it for me though. Awesome place.

review_text:
Booked this hotel on our last night in Costa Rica. My partner and I knew we wanted a very comfortable hotel with good food that where we can stay in and relax after a week of non-stop activities around the country. The bedroom was very nice-I love all the fine wooden furniture that was excellently crafted. The bed was very comfortable and the bathroom clean. The soaps and shampoos were also fragrant. The hotel grounds itself is beautiful, having been a former Victorian mansion. It is great to dine in the restaurant where there is an open area. It was quite romantic. Would definitely come here again.
One of the cons though is that it is far from the city center (Hotel Presidente was right smack in the center of everything), but it was perfect for our purposes as we wanted to be in a quiet and calm area. Anyway taxi fare to get to Avenida Central is quite cheap, so it was not really a big issue in the end.

review_title: A hotel with character and charm
review_text:
Hotel Grano de Oro is a beautiful renovation and expansion of a 1910 Victorian-style home originally associated with a coffee plantation. The surrounding neighborhood holds little of interest, but the hotel itself is classy and secure. The rooms tend toward small, but are comfortable and nicely arranged around a series of pleasant courtyards and gardens. The restaurant and its courtyard have a particularly appealing ambience, clearly a destination for romantic dinners, celebratory breakfasts and business lunches meant to impress. The food is excellent, though not cheap.
If you're looking to explore beyond San Jose and are interested in wildlife, check out my blog on Agami Herons in Costa Rica (http://www.kirstennaturetravel.com/agami-herons-in-costa-rica/).

review_title: Very relaxing retreat in the heart of San Jose
review_text:
Hotel de Oro is a very nice hotel near the heart of San Jose.
As for San Jose, I wouldn't recommend an extended stay in the city unless you are visiting Costa Rica for historical museums/a city experience--but, I usually stay one night in San Jose due to flights.
As for the hotel, it's a great hotel to spend your first or last night in Costa Rica (upon a late arrival/early departure). The hotel is very peaceful, beautiful, and comfortable--the beds won't disappoint--you'll get a great night sleep!
Please note that I'm giving Hotel de Oro only 3 stars for location--for San Jose alone, I'd give it 4 or 5 stars--but compared to everywhere else you could stay in Costa Rica, San Jose is only 2 or 3 stars for me.
Also, the hotel staff was extremely accommodating even though I only stayed one night--I was on a multi-destination trip and while my trip to Costa Rica was ending at the Hotel de Oro, I was off to Belize and wanted my clothes laundered before my next destination--the hotel staff very graciously laundered my clothes in less than 8hrs so that I could board my plane and fly to Belize with fresh clothes! Most hotels wouldn't go out of their way to do a special load of laundry for their guests!

review_title: Another great stay at Grano de Oro
review_text: My husband and I always stay at Grano de Oro when we fly through San Jose. It's a beautiful place with great staff. I'm almost hesitant to recommend it too highly, for fear that too many people will discover it and ruin it. With that in mind, I'll make one recommendation to travellers who decide to stay here: please, if you have dinner in the restaurant, dress appropriately. This is probably one of the best restaurants in the entire city. It's classy enough that they don't have a dress code (you're just supposed to be classy and dress appropriately without being told.) So unless your luggage got lost, it would be nice if fellow tourists could show a little respect.

review_title: The most beautiful hotel with the most amazing staff.
review_text:
The Grano de Oro is sophisticated, elegant, gracious and beautiful. The garden suite where I stayed is gorgeous, quiet and a true refuge. The food at the hotel restaurant is delicious. Do not even consider staying anywhere else in San Jose.
A special thank you to Marco, Omar and Ivannia from me. As I was checking out in the lovely lobby the morning of my departure, I heard a kitten meowing very loudly at the bottom of property's outside steps. The kitten/he had an injured paw and was limping. Being a person who is very involved in animal rescue, I was very torn as to whether to cancel my flight and stay make sure the kitten received medical and long term care - a home/adoption or to ask and trust the hotel to take care of same.
After much discussion, I was promised (for the 10th time) as the kitten was whisked away to stay in the separate hotel offices that he would be taken to the vet and that he would "never have to live on the streets again." Omar, who drove me to the airport, took the kitten to the vet the next day so that his paw could be repaired, Marco, the hotel manager, has keep me abreast of all events related to the kitten (Señor Pequito Gato -- I did not feel i should give him a real name) and, Ivannia, another hotel employee, and her husband have adopted Señor. From the photos I have received he is having a wonderful life.
Thank you so much to the Grano de Oro team. Not only do run a stunning facility in the most lovely way possible but, you also do so much to help the young mothers of San Jose and now the innocent animals of your city. I will see you again soon.

review_title: Best place to stay in San JOse
review_text:
Our stay at the hotel Grano De Or was simply amazing!!! To start, the food is amazing, and the restaurant and hotel staff were very attentive. It was my birthday, and they remembered both when we checked in, and also on the morning of (it's hard to say no to a breakfast desert)! The staff gave great recommendations, helped us with our day trips, and were very helpful. On top of their general wonderful nature, they were super helpful with our lost luggage. We had a missing bag, and they called the airline office very half hour until they got someone who could answer questions!
The room was perfect, clean, and the bed was very comfortable.
This is an amazing place to stay!!!!!!!

review_text:
Couldn't fault our stay. Staff was great; check-in was efficient. Although hotel is located away from the 'real' center, this makes it more quiet and safe, and it's a 20-minute walk or a cheap taxi ride ($3-$4) to the city center. Some restaurants and a supermarket are close by, and it's next to all the car rental companies (convenient for our car rental return). Hotel ordered us a taxi to the airport for $25 the next day.
We got upgraded to the family room, spacious with two separate rooms with comfy beds and TVs. Safe, mini-bar, decent bathroom.
Breakfast (a la carte, no buffet) was delicious, probably the best bagel with cream cheese I ever had. Dinner was delicious too (Chateaubriand!); sure, it is more expensive than surrounding regular restaurants in San Jose but worth it.

review_title: An oasis in a mad city....
review_text:
Having spent six weeks travelling through Central America and staying in some rather basic hotels, I was over the moon when I arrived at Hotel Grano de Ora.
It certainly is all a luxury hotel should be, and an oasis in the madness of San Jose.
My room was large, spotless and uber comfortable, and the bed was fabulous.
Generally, the staff were great and I'm pleased to say that having provided some negative (but valid and constructive) feedback to management about the restaurant, my issue was dealt with promptly and to my satisfaction.
I would definitely stay there again.

review_text:
I first stayed at The Grano de Oro shortly after it opened in 1992 and went back the next three years. I loved it and couldn't say enough about it. I went back in 2014 and again this year and I'm ready to try something else. Most travellers to Costa Rica fly in to either San Jose or Liberia and then go off on adventures in the country. This hotel well lovely doesn't have good food that matches in any way the delectable descriptions, the wine list is limited and very expensive. An overnight visit in a decent room with dinner will run you over $500 and that's a bit much for what you get. In addition on my last visit my small camera disappeared from my room... very disappointed in that.
I have been told of other lovely spots close to the airport for car rentals, etc. that are half the price and I'll be checking them out. This hotel has been too big for it's britches.

review_text:
We stayed in the hotel and ate in the restaurant. Perfect place to stay after traveling all day! The rooms are beautiful, tranquil and oasis-like. Upon our arrival we were offered passion fruit drinks which were great! Our room was in the back of the hotel, and there was a maze of beautifully kept covered patios to get through on the way, with fountains and local plants. When we entered the room we were treated to a surprise of our own little private garden just outside the french doors. It was very private with a bamboo wall separating our view from the neighbors garden.
We had some time to visit the rooftop jacuzzi and that was another treat. Towels were available and it felt super private as no one was there!
The restaurant was easily one of the most memorable meals of our trip. The food and service were unmatched and it truly deserves the number one rating that is has as San Jose's best restaurant. You should definitely have dinner there! We didn't have time to have breakfast at the hotel.

review_text:
This is a charming hotel, which offers fantastic service and excellent dining.
Our room was large and comfortable with a small private terrace - the perfect place to kick off one's shoes and relax after a long journey - and we slept incredibly well.
The communal areas are immaculately maintained and filled with little pieces of history in the forms of paintings, photographs and books, and well-considered to give the hotel a very relaxing feel.
We were particularly impressed by the attached restaurant. It looks stunning (dark wood-panelling, polished bar, heavy curtains, internal courtyard), serves incredible cocktails (the best Caipirinha I've ever tasted) and exquisite modern cuisine.
Our one quibble with the property was the almost complete lack of water pressure in the shower, which made washing one's hair in San Jose's soft water nearly impossible. However this wouldn't stop us booking again if we ever return to the area.

review_text:
We stayed twice at the Grano de Oro, once at the beginning and once at the end of our trip. It's really an exceptional place, about as far as you can get from the sterile corridors and wall-to-wall carpeting of your usual hotel. For the beginning of our trip we splurged on a room with an outdoor patio, but overall our second, more conventional room seemed just as nice. The hotel and restaurant surround an inner open-air courtyard with a fountain and stained glass windows. There was a second fountain by the entrance to our (balcony) room. Everything is paneled in dark wood. In short, you get to feel, briefly, what it would be like to have your own eighteenth-century mansion.
Other details: rooms were clean, staff friendly, beds not exceptional but not uncomfortable. The restaurant offers good but not amazing food; a solid choice if you're too tired or intimidated to go out.

review_text:
First, when you arrive the bellman is waiting at the curb to carry your bags and assist you in anyway he can. Then at the reception desk you are handed a refreshing glass of (passion fruit?) juice while you fill out your minimal paperwork.
We have stayed at Grano de Oro twice now. Both time were one night with flights the next day. The rooms are comfortable and clean. The atmosphere is very relaxing with jacuzzi on the roof and court yards throughout the hotel with fountains everywhere. The first time we stay it was in room 14 a few years ago, it felt very private and quiet. The second time we stayed it was in room 29 which in around a courtyard and steps up to the deck/jacuzzi area. It was louder in the morning then we anticipated with everyone getting up early for flights. The sound resinates through the courtyard. Next time we stay we will request a room away from the courtyards. Both rooms had A/C units.
The restaurant which we have dined at multiple times now for dinner and breakfast is just WONDERFUL from the atmosphere to the excellent service and cuisine! We are never disappointed. It is not overpriced for the quality of the meal!
Breakfast is not included, but reasonably priced and worth every penny! Hours: 7a-10p
We highly recommend this hotel.

review_title: Peace and quiet in the city
review_text:
As far as capital cities go, San Jose doesn't have a great deal going for it being somewhat shabby with lots of traffic, no exciting architecture ( although the theatre is worth visiting) and rather uninspiring shops and restaurants. Outstanding amidst all this though is the rather splendid Grano de Oro Hotel which offers an oasis of peace and quiet
in an elegant setting.
The rooms are of a decent size, spotlessly clean and contain all you would require to enjoy a comfortable stay. The hotel is set off the main thoroughfare in a quiet side road yet it is an easy 20 minute walk along the flat to the city centre. Staff were always pleasant and helpful and breakfast was excellent with hot food cooked to order.
Do make your way to the roof terrace if staying here. Even if you don't use the Jacuzzi it is a pleasant place to sit and enjoy the tranquillity, perhaps with a book, whilst surrounded by greenery from the plants and flowers.
Whether staying for just a night or several days you will be hard-pressed to find a better hotel in the city. Well recommended.
