review_text:
I'll preface this review in saying this was my first trip out of the US, and I traveled solo?!! Prior to arrival in San Jose, I contacted the Hotel Grano de Oro in San Jose, booked my stay (based on the many many positive Tripadvisor reviews) and I couldn't be happier with my decision. It was just a one night stay. The communication from the hotel staff prior to my arrival was excellent. I inquired about "things to do" when I arrived in San Jose, and they went out of their way trying to help me find a coffee plantation tour, and suggested other "popular" things to do, as an alternative. They also arranged for ground transportation, which I would HIGHLY recommend, as "navigating": through customs/immigration was a bit challenging. It was so comforting to exit the airport and see my transportation awaiting with a sign that had my name on it! Perfect!!
The courtyard off the lobby was perfect to enjoy an afternoon libation. Had breakfast there, and it was also nice.. not incredible, but very good.
The room was comfortable, and the staff was extremely pleasant.. offering restaurant suggestions. The room was just what I needed for one night.. comfortable beds.. clean (spotless) accomodations.. and so pretty decorated with Xmas "holiday flare!"
If I ever needed to stay in San Jose, I wouldn't think twice about staying at Hotel Grono de Oro, and you shouldn't either!

review_title: Excellent Hotel--Great Choice for Proximity to Estadio Nacional
review_text:
This is simply an excellent hotel, which I strongly recommend as an alternative to chain business hotels on the western side of San Jose. Some friends and I used this hotel as a home base in September for the US-Costa Rica World Cup qualifier. The hotel is an easy walk to the large urban park (La Sabana) where the new Estadio Nacional is located. The area around the hotel itself is not particularly scenic, but the hotel is a beautifully renovated old building with character. At midday, you will see local elites out for business lunches--not just tourists moving on to the beaches. Downstairs from the restaurant are interesting black-and-white photographs of old San Jose. Wonderful ambience.
The restaurant and bar are situated around an open courtyard, like many older Central American hotels. We ate both breakfast and dinner there, and they were very good. The restaurant is elegant and has a beautiful, old-fashioned bar with knowledgeable bartenders. In general, the staff were friendly and helpful.
This is the only hotel I have stayed in in San Jose, but frankly, I cannot imagine staying somewhere else, whether for a business trip, a stopover on the way to the coast, or a soccer game. This is a well conceived and executed boutique hotel.

review_text:
Like many other travellers we used this hotel as our first night stop after flying into San Jose. It is only 20 minutes from the airport so perfectly located. I had booked our hire car from the airport so it was frustrating to see that there are many companies just round the corner from the hotel which would have been a much better option!
We picked a garden courtyard suite which was another mistake as it gets dark pretty early so we couldn’t use the outside space and we were off fairly promptly in the morning so pointless really. I found the decor a bit oppressive - lots of dark wood and very traditional.
The restaurant was great. Lovely fine dining experience and clearly popular with locals enjoying special dinners. Beware if you are light eaters though the portions are huge.
A great option for one night arriving or departing from SJ. Not sure I would want to stay any longer.

review_text:
We were just looking for a place to spend the first night in Costa Rica before moving on. A quick trip to Trip Advisor brought us to the Hotel Grano de Oro in San Jose. It was an absolute gem. The staff was fantastic. It is not in the city center, but that's a small price to pay for the luxury of this hotel. Between a long day of travel and convenience of the hotel restaurant, we chose to eat there. The food was absolutely top notch! We were told the next day by our driver that it was considered one of the top restaurants in Costa Rica. I had no trouble at all believing it. There was a little sticker shock with the dinner bill from the restaurant but it wasn't what you'd think. The bill comes with gratuity included and was in Colons as well as Dollars. When it looked like the bill was 60000 dollars, I was headed for a heart attack. When it turned out to be under $120 with tip included, my cardiac problems were minimized.
Would I go back again? You betcha!

review_text: We stayed here two nights at the end of our trip, and it was absolutely wonderful. I don't have one negative thing to say. The staff was helpful at every turn and truly took care of us. The room's amenities included shampoo, conditioner, shower gel, lotion, soap, a blow dryer, a non-slip mat for inside the tub, two bathrobes, a coffee pot, extra pillows, a safe, a minibar, a TV, chairs and a table, and lovely french windows that opened and overlooked a small garden below. Surprisingly for San Jose, our room, a king deluxe, was also very quiet. Our room was toward the back of the hotel. And the restaurant was simply fabulous. We ate breakfast and dinner there on our full day at the hotel, and there were absolutely the best meals of the trip. Also, don't miss out on the jacuzzi area. There are two hot tubs with plenty of chairs for relaxing and reading. Also, this hotel is an easy walking distance to the largest park in San Jose, which is lovely in its own right. Would stay here again in a heartbeat.

review_title: Very cool boutique hotel, a bit further from central city than we'd hoped
review_text:
We stayed at Hotel Grano de Oro for the last few days of our honeymoon. Our room was one of several that was situated around a small garden courtyard that was beautiful. That made it feel much more like staying at home than in a hotel. The room itself was very nice, with hardwood floors, comfortable beds, and a nicely stocked mini-bar.
The hotel staff was very helpful, which I greatly appreciated because unlike the tourist areas where we'd spent the first part of our trip to Costa Rica, San Jose wasn't quite as easy to navigate for non-Spanish speakers. The hotel staff helped me arrange taxi service, book tours, and get to the airport smoothly.
We also enjoyed the food and beverage selections at the hotel's restaurant. Our only complaint with Grano de Oro is that it wasn't quite as close to the central city as we'd hoped, but that was just a minor inconvenience and I'm still very glad we stayed there.

We were given a welcoming fruit drink which was lovely and shown to our room by a friendly porter. We received a complimentary upgrade to a deluxe room rather than the standard one we had booked which was very nice indeed, especially after such a long trip. The room itself was gorgeous, massive bed and bathroom and the highlight was our own private terrace with fountain! Regrettably we were leaving for our next destination early the following morning so we didn't get to fully appreciate the hotel but in any case I would not hesitate in recommending it as the best hotel in San Jose!

review_text: We arrived in San Jose' at the start of our 46 days in Costa Rica and wanted to experience downtown San Jose'. One day in San Jose' is enough as you can see most of what it has to offer in the very busy place. The Hotel however is well worth the trip from the airport as an over night stay. The rooms are 1st class as are the beds and quality of the staff. Right from the reception the staff were incredibly happy and helpful! The restaurant is not to be missed as you will not find anything close to its quality anywhere within Costa Rica. Great start to our trip. Anytime we have an overnight stay in San Jose' we will definitely return to this hotel!

review_title: Beautiful, serene hotel in the middle of a busy city.
review_text: This hotel is incredible. It is beautiful inside and out. The staff was incredibly friendly and helpful. They were prompt with wake up calls and handled scheduling all of our transfers to and from the hotel. They recommended restaurants and shopping in San Jose, and warned us of areas to avoid. There was someone at the front desk all day and night. When we arrived at the beginning of our honeymoon, we were offered fresh, cool juice at check-in, someone took our bags to our room and showed us where everything was and how to work the safe, TV, etc., and there was fresh fruit waiting in our room. We had dinner in the restaurant that evening and the food was great. The area was nice, but you didn't have to wear black tie or even fancy clothes to eat there. We traveled to Nayara for the week and then came back to Grano de Oro for a night before flying home. When we came back, they automatically upgraded our room to a bigger, more secluded room without us asking, simply because we were return guests! It's very nice, very clean, and just an awesome experience.

review_text:
The group at Grano de Oro was extremely helpful at organizing a transfer from the airport to the hotel for a low price of $35 and made it seamless to get the transfer and find the driver at the airport.
Upon arriving we had a beautiful fruit plate in our room, a great drink from the front desk and the staff at the front desk, especially Wymar (spelling?). We got in late and wanted some quick but fresh (not chain) pizza. The corner (a block and a half away) had fabulous pizza and delivered to the hotel.
The hotel set up our day long tour of the coffee plantation, Poas volcanos, and Peace lodge and waterfalls. A highly recommended tour! It was a fabulous way to see the nature surrounding San Jose before we headed off to our resort.
The staff was courteous and accommodating during the entire stay. Breakfast is worth it at the restaurant, we felt that dinner was a bit over priced and not that great.... :/
A great stay in the city!

review_text:
I stayed at the Hotel Grano de Oro for 8 nights. The hotel is beautiful. I arrived in the evening and the foyer was illuminated with soft lights. It really creates a wonderful ambiance. When I arrived I was served fresh mango juice. The check in was smooth and fast.
My room was located near the garden towards the back of the hotel. I was led to my room by the doorman and my first impression of the hotel and garden was that this is a luxurious hotel. My room had a king size bed, an armoire with plenty of space for my clothes, and a table with two chairs. The bathroom was fantastic. It had marble counter tops and a nice deep tub. I had no trouble falling asleep here each night. It was extremely comfortable.
Many of the staff at the hotel speak English. I was able to communicate no problem. The front desk arranged for a morning taxi each day of my stay. They also arranged two excursions for me while I was there.
I made an appointment for a spa treatment and was not disappointed. The masseuse knows what she is doing! She wants you to feel comfortable and relaxed. The spa is a single room on the 2nd floor. Traffic from the street was distracting a bit though.
This hotel would have received 5 stars but I experienced an incident that left me uncomfortable. The doorman that helped me get a taxi one morning asked me out on a date! I was completely taken off guard and immediately felt sick to my stomach. The gentleman knew I was traveling alone and what room I was in. I wanted to report this to the owner but did not come in contact with him/her. San Jose is not a city that you should let your guard down in.

review_text: I stayed here recently for two separate nights on a trip to Costa Rica. It is a spectacular oasis in San Jose. It is a grand old residence that has been converted into a lovely and inviting hotel. The decor is charming, the rooms are spacious and have every modern convenience while maintaining Costa Rican charm. The beds were some of the most comfortable I have ever slept on! There is a beautiful courtyard in which you can eat, or a lovely dining room. The service and the food was nothing short of spectacular. The entire staff were very helpful and warm which certainly made the stay that much nicer. If you are staying in San Jose, even for one night, don't miss the opportunity to stay in this incredibly charming oasis in the city.

review_text:
My son and I stayed at Hotel Grano before and after going on a trip to the Monte Verdi cloud forest. We loved the way that there were beautiful trees and plants sprinkled throughout the hotel which is a beautiful old mansion. The focus on the environment was a great 'bridge' to the natural wonders of the cloud forest. We stayed there both before and after our trip to Monti Verdi. The highlights for us were
1. The restaurant that had great cocktails including one based on a local cane based moonshine called "guaro"
2. The Jacuzzi in a secluded rooftop garden. The many chirping birds and running water in a quiet setting made for a relaxing environment whether reclining on the chairs or sitting in the Jacuzzi.
3. On our second stay we were put in a room with a private rock garden containing a burbling brook water feature. We found it so relaxing that we left it on all night!
4. The friendly staff who made us feel welcome. In fact across Costa Rica we found everyone to be far more friendly than we have experienced in other tourist destinations south of the US.

review_text: Conveniently situated off the main thoroughfare, we began and ended our holiday at this beautiful hotel. The warm greeting at the end of a long and tiring journey was very welcome as was the refreshing cold drink. The bedroom was comfortable, well appointed and spacious, as was the bathroom with lovely walk in shower. The finishing touch was the little indoor courtyard garden, complete with table and chairs, fountain and tropical plants; cool and totally secluded. What a treat! Breakfast was a delightful experience in the open courtyard. The service was friendly and prompt and the food plentiful and delicious. The evening meal was our most expensive during our holiday, but was excellent. All the staff we met were friendly, courteous and helpful. This hotel gave us the ideal relaxing, gentle stay needed before embarking on our homeward journey.

review_title: Beautiful hotel in walking distance from city center
review_text:
This hotel was just gorgeous! The room was spacious and well-decorated (we booked a standard room and were given a free upgrade to superior). The hot tub was wonderful - very warm, with lovely plants around it to give it a very private feel.
The service was also very good and the location great! It was about a 25-30 minute walk to the city center, all downhill.
The restaurant, while very expensive, was pretty good. I loved the first dinner I had, didn't care for the second. Excellent service, gorgeous courtyard, inconsistent food.
My only complaint was that cigarette smoke came into our room. We had the windows open for air and some people below us (outside the building - no smoking allowed inside) were talking quite loudly and smoking rather late at night. Perhaps there should be a designated smoking area somewhere they can't bother anyone?

review_title: Wonderful stay...couldn't have asked for more.
review_text:
I was traveling to San Jose for business and decided to go a couple of days early for some leisure time. Given the great reviews here in Trip Advisor, I decided to stay at Hotel Grano de Oro for the vacation part of my trip. Before I booked the hotel, I sent like a million emails asking questions about the different options and day tours. All the emails were answered promptly and patiently. :)
My stay was amazing. I originally booked a superior room but when I arrived, they upgraded me to a deluxe room in the patio area. The room was lovely, with hardwood floors and a window looking out the patio - I could hear little birds chirping outside in the morning. The staff was so wonderful, very friendly and always willing to help. I had to work on Monday morning but my laptop was having issues connecting to Wi-Fi - as this is not a business hotel, there aren't Ethernet cables in the room - so they lend me an office so I could do some work. Not only that, they had somebody from the restaurant bring me a pitcher with water!
The restaurant was lovely as well. It's worth a visit just to sit in such a gorgeous place! The food was great too. :)
Completely recommended. Thanks Hotel Grano de Oro for such a great stay!

review_title: A little over priced, poor housekeeping service and bad location
review_text:
We stayed at this hotel for two nights on the way out of Costa Rica. The reception staff and bellboys are very helpful, and we were shown to our room and given help with all its features. However, that's about where the positives end.
I read a number reviews for this hotel praising its location; particularly its proximity to good quality Costa Rican restaurants. Unfortunately, aside from the good - if expensive - restaurant attached to this hotel, the other options nearby (within walking distance) are limited to fast food (McDonald's, Quiznos, Wendy's, KFC etc). Given the area, we also did not feel particularly safe walking to these options at night.
The hotel is a rabbit warren. Our room was well located, but others seemed to be deep in the bowels of the old house. I would hate to have been down in there in an emergency.
As we were only at the hotel for about 30 hours we left the next morning for our activities having not unpacked - we simply opened our bags to retrieve the necessary items. When we returned for the evening to pack for our early flight, we found cleaning cloths that had not been there before buried in and amongst our luggage. Some of my personal items which I had left on the bed side table for easy access had also been moved, altered, and relocated to other areas of the room. To its credit, when we raised this issue with the hotel's staff at reception they were very apologetic. I also received an email from the hotel's management explaining that it was necessary to move our things to clean the room. I do not agree - the cloths were buried so deep in our luggage that it suggests our luggage was in fact gone through by the housekeeping staff. Despite the speed with which we left in the morning, and the length of our stay in the hotel, our things were left in an orderly fashion when we left the room and not strewn around on the bed/floor/bathroom/in any way that would affect the ability of staff to clean the room. The staff had also closed my contact lens case which was specifically open to dry (as those of you who wear lenses know is important), as well as our ipads being moved, and balanced precariously on the side of the bed so a chocolate could be put in its place.
Not impressed.

We both got 90 minute massages in the hotel's spa and it was the best massage either of us have ever had!
The food is very delicious and reasonably priced if you are up for a fancier meal. Breakfast on the terrace was delicious and the atmosphere...so nice! Everyone who works there is very professional and very friendly!

review_text:
Stayed at the Grano de Oro for 2 days in August 2013 as a family with one toddler. The hotel, which is located about 20-25 minutes of a walk from the core downtown, is certainly very very nice. The staff is very attentive and immediately makes you feel welcome. The reception staff is fantastic, with one of the longest serving staff members (Pablo) making you feel welcome from the first moment you arrive. Rooms are also very good. We had the deluxe room with the patio. Excellent all around -- clean, airy, well lit, and with a nice if small patio where you can sit and read/eat (has a small table and 2-3 chairs).
The experience with reservations is also very good, with a very responsive email service to answer all your questions.
I would also highly recommend the restaurant, which has great food and service and a very impressive wine selection. It's a bit expensive for dinner, but then again, should be expected as CR generally is not as cheap as a tourist destination but also because the restaurant is very good with high end service, food quality, and ambiance. As an aside, we hired a babysitter through the hotel to watch our kid while we had dinner here, and she did a good job (albeit having to mainly watch over the sleeping baby).
The hotel set up a coffee plantation tour for us with Britt Coffee. A fun 2-3 hour tour with lunch.

review_text: Even though this hotel and restaurant were pricey we weren't disappointed at all. Our room was #4 which had windows that overlooked a small garden. Room was clean and well appointed and very relaxing. Dinner and breakfast were good. Staff were friendly and accommodated us on our early rush breakfast the next morning before we departed for our next destination. The hotel is a nice gem in the midst of a bustling big city. We did go for a rather long walk around San Jose and found it to be like any big city with it's traffic, exhaust fumes, smells, crowded sidewalks, etc. Contrary to what some people have mentioned here I didn't really feel that safe, even with my husband being with me, especially over near the city park area. I wouldn't want to walk around town at night.

Breakfast was taken in the open central courtyard. Lovely food, but you might struggle to find an option if you're not keen on eggs! We went away very happy and well-rested ahead of the 18-hour journey home.

review_title: Comfortable and elegant for the area, but I don't think you need it.
review_text: The hotel was beautiful, we had a family suite with excellent beds and opportunities for privacy. There are green places with water and fountains inside the winding hotel and you actually get breezes in the halls. We were told they had an excellent restaurant so we went for it the first night. The restaurant was a bit 'swank' for a vacation dinner for us and we felt the staff, menu and prices all a bit intimidating. It is elegant beauty on the edge of the city. We were able to walk into downtown and the market area and it's right near the national park with the stadium etc so the location's good. It just seems out of place in the location. a Victorian mansion in the middle of the working city seemed out of place and unnecessary for a place to stay. You can save money, get a similar location, and just not feel that you need to be dressed up to walk the halls.No real amenities beside the restaurant, hot tub and an expensive gift area.

review_text:
My husband and I stayed here for one night before catching an early morning flight. It's so much more beautiful in person- the pictures just do not do it justice!! It has the charm of a small bed and breakfast, but the amenities of a large hotel.
After traveling all day, we were exhausted. So, after grabbing some lunch a few blocks away, we retreated to our lovely room where we remained for the rest of the evening. We stayed in a Deluxe King, and while it was a tad on the small size, it was truly a great room. The air conditioning worked like a dream and is aimed at the bed, which rocked. Also the room has a nice large window that lets a lot of natural light in. The room comes equipped with a large flat screen tv that has lots of channels.
We initially had made reservations to eat at the restaurant for dinner, but were far too exhausted to go through the rhythms of a sit down meal, so we ordered some room service. It was certainly the fanciest room service we had ever had. We each had macadamia pesto and gorgonzola ravioli, a salad, and some delicious fresh bread and some sort of herb butter spread. It was really yummy.
I highly recommend this hotel to anyone who is passing through San Jose and doesn't want to actually deal with the city itself.

review_text:
Location: convenient to museums and restaurants in town, close to the airport.
Room: stayed in a room with two queen beds, sitting area, ample sized luxurious bathroom with coffee and tea, and option to go on to the shared outdoor terrace. Reliable wifi available. Cozy and cute, comfortable beds, perfect for a short stay en route to the airport.
Staff: friendly, helpful, commendable.
Food: Delicious! Loved the restaurant.
Grounds: very lovely grounds, flowering plants and trees, very old classic feel to the place. Quaint but not old, exceedingly lovely when lit up at night.

review_text:
In the heart of San Jose is a gem of a boutique hotel! The quaint hallways are lined with old photos of early life in Costa Rica - coffee plantations, textile mills, city streets, and an emerging nation.
You will find the rooms small, extraordinarily clean, linens fresh, large flat screen TV, simple amenities which make for a wonderful boutique experience - soap and shampoo in the shower by dispenser, lotions and hand soap in matching marble dispensers, nice coffee pot with small batch Costa Rican coffee, candy on the nightstand. Each room is a unique feel, shape, and layout. It's a signature boutique hotel.
Beautiful fountains, plants, indoor/outdoor gardens, 2 Jacuzzis, wood floors, a fresh gift shop, and stunning interior design will make you feel warm and welcome.
The highlight to this inviting property is the amazing staff and the first class customer service. The attentive staff - from the first person welcoming us at the curb (with umbrella due to rain), to the front desk staff offering a welcome juice drink, to manager on duty, to the bellman, to the bartender, to the restaurant manager - every person taking care of guest with high attention to detail. Truly made to feel welcome!
Only concern was internet. There are multiple routers on property and each with different name, so when moving about property changes in router require re-entering password to work with new router. Also, there were times when internet stopped working and routers went offline and internet was unavailable. For a hotel of this quality and exceptional service this is unacceptable. Friends staying with us had same experience. This needs to be address to move this property to an Excellent rating.
If you enjoy a boutique hotel experience with hight standards for guest attention - put this one on your list! You won't be disappointed!

...the gentle breeze from the ceiling fan... the indoor vegetation... breakfast in the courtyard... a heated outdoor jacuzzi... books on a bookshelf... accents from the past that give you a sense of well being. review_title: Beautiful hotel for the location but some the staff's customer service is lacking
review_text: Arrived at the Grande dr Oro on our last night of an amazing 10 day trip to Costa Rica. Everyone in this country has been so helpful, accomadating and friendly so I was so surprised at the lack of customer service on the morning of our checkout at this hotel. We stayed for one night before flying out of San Jose. We decided to have dinner at the Gran Oro because of the lack of choices in the area and because of their excellent reviews. The atmosphere and server staff was great but the food was overpriced for the quality. When we woke the next day we went for our "included" breakfast and found out after sitting down that we need a voucher which was never given to us. I had the printout from expedia with our reservation info showing that breakfast was indeed included. However the front desk reception refused to provide us with vouchers because they said "Expedia didn't give us a breakfast reservation for you" and "you should just pay for breakfast and call Expedia when you get home because its an international call and we can't call them for this". I was blown away! They are partners with a company as large as Expedia and all they can offer as help is for the customer to handle the problem when they get back to the US! Unacceptable. We just spent a good chunk of money on dinner for two at their hotel the night before (and I'm sorry we did) so it wasn't about the free breakfast but more about the lack of responsiblity the Gran de Oro had regarding their partnership with Expedia. I'm sure they would have no problem calling Expedia internationally if they didn't get paid for the room we just stayed in! Needless to say we didnt eat breakfast there. Overall the rooms were nice and the other staff were great.

review_title: For Us, this is one of the best
review_text:
We returned to the Grano de Oro after 9 years. It has been enlarged and even more beautiful. We reserved the same room as we had before, the Garden Suite. Very large room with a sitting alcove, which then opens onto a private patio with lush plants. A/C is more than adequate, Wifi is as good as home (fast) and service is excellent. Several locals told us that this hotel is the most respected restaurant in San Jose.
For $35 they met us at the airport with a private driver - very easy and smooth. Greeted with juice upon arrival, and we went straight to lunch. The restaurant offers a choice of indoor or patio seating and over the three days we have enjoyed both. We travel a lot, (28 weeks out of the last 40) for business and pleasure, but this hotel is easily in the top five. Understand that we don't like glass and chrome palaces, but prefer classics and if possible family run.
I agree with another reviewer, that San Jose itself does not merit a few days, but, for us, this hotel merits a trip to Costa Rica. Then when you add the things you can see on day trips from here, it is great.
The restaurant is wonderful. Elegant surroundings, excellent service, food is about as good as it gets. Dinner with no alcohol = $100 USD; breakfast $20. For us, better than the best in Aspen (where we travel frequently on business) at 1/3 the price.
We were here three nights, and hate to leave; wondering when we can return. Can't say enough good things.
Try the garden suite ($265)

review_title: Lovely little place and top notch service!
review_text:
Our stay was for four nights/five days in one of the deluxe room with a king size bed. Upon arrival it was pouring rain and the bell boy efficiently popped opened two umbrellas for us and helped us with our luggage up the entrance staircase. The front desk greeted us with flutes of champagne each and the check-in was simple. Room was clean and well appointed. There were some fresh fruits awaiting us in our room when we arrived. All the reps at the front desk have been very friendly and accommodating with helping us make phone calls and bookings for all the events/tours we had planned for our visit. (We found out that Sprint Cellular does not even have international roaming option-so my cell was useless for phone calls, and most of the tour's customer service only spoke spanish).
There is a souvenir shop conveniently located onsite. The items are very nice, unique, and of good quality. You have the option of postcards to pottery, mask to jewelry. The shop will help you with postage and getting your postcards out (Wonderful plus!)
There is the restaurant on site too, and it's just wonderful! (I will describe in detail in a different review). We had breakfast, brunch and dinner at this restaurant and would highly recommend it at least once if you're staying here.
As for location, the hotel is on the west side of San Jose and a few blocks off Central Avenue which goes straight into the heart of San Jose or downtown. Since the hotel is not in downtown itself it is quiet for the most part and relatively safe. ** Some returning visitors have warned us when we landed at the airport to avoid being out late in downtown San Jose as pickpockets and thieves are common. Speaking of Hotel Grano de Oro's location- it's close to other nice restaurants and even the Art Museum/ Park (walking distance).
Again, I can not praise the staff here enough for all they did for us to make our stay comfortable!

review_text: Stayed 2 nights at the Hotel Grano de Oro at the beginning and end of our trip to Costa Rica. The hotel is a beautiful Victorian-style mansion. Consequently, rooms and beds are on the small side. The property is very clean and the service is wonderful. The staff make you feel welcome and are very helpful. For instance, I left a pocket knife in the room the first night. When we checked back in 3 days later, they had it for me at the front desk - I didn't even have to ask! Everyone speaks English very well, but they were patient and helpful when I tried my rudimentary Spanish (Thanks, Ulises). The location is off the beaten track, but its only a $4 or $5 cab ride to the Museo Nacional and other attractions - and cabs are everywhere in San Jose. Would definitely stay there again.

review_text: I stayed here with my wife while I was on business in San Jose. This was my first trip to Costa Rica and we were both nervous about being in the city and not speaking any Spanish. We arranged for an airport transfer and were met upon our arrival and brought quickly to the hotel. The neighborhood of the hotel left a lot to be desired, but we were only there for two days and I figured my wife could stay within the hotel while I was working. We were able to check in early after a 10 minute wait to prepare our room (while drinking our welcoming juice). The rooms were small, but what we expected for a city hotel. We ran into a problems almost immediately with our AC unit leaking. We called the front desk and they responded immediately. We were given our choice of replacement rooms and everything was handled in a professional manner. My wife and I spend the next hour hanging out on our plant strewn patio enjoying the warm weather. That evening we had a wonderful meal at the restaurant (more to see in the restaurant review). The next day while I worked my wife arranged some spa services. They do not have a spa onsite but bring in a spa service. My wife was more than pleased with the price and service. The staff was very attentive even though we could not speak the local language. They were all very friendly making us feel more relaxed and at home. Overall, we had a great experience at this lovely hotel.

review_text:
I spent 2 nights at Grano de Oro. The first night I arrived before heading to the beach area in Costa Rica. San Jose isn't the most lovely area, but Grano de Oro was a nice retreat. Check-in was efficient. The first room I had was a double room to the right of reception and down a hall past a fountain. It opened into the courtyard. I appreciate unique features, so the courtyard was appealing to me. However, the room was basic, but comfortable. The bathroom was completely basic, but hot water was not an issue. Wifi was a nice touch too.
On the return from our vacation, our flight was cancelled and we chose to stay back at this hotel. We stayed in an upgraded room on a higher floor overlooking the restaurant. Again, the hotel is beautiful and has such unique architecture. The room was comfortable. The bed was fine and the bathroom was much brighter and had more water pressure. Also a newer tub/shower. We enjoyed room service and also the meals in the courtyard restaurant were just fine. The area around this hotel is not pretty by any means, but the courtyard areas within the hotel make it more of a retreat.
Staff were friendly. I will not hesitate to stay at this hotel the next time I am in San Jose. It is also convenient to the airport.

review_title: My Top Choice in San Jose
review_text:
For me, the magic of Costa Rica happens when you leave the capital and explore this amazing country. There are times when I have little other choice and need to stay in San Jose, when I do, Grano de Oro is my favorite. I have stayed in a couple of Marriott Hotels in San Jose and found them a bit too commercial and boring. Grano de Oro has great character do to it's history of being a Victorian mansion in the early 1900s. The amazing gardens and fountains quickly make you forget you're in a city. But one of the most important factors to consider is the quality of the rooms.
I stayed in a deluxe room that contained two queen size beds. They had very good quality pillow topped mattresses and very comfortable sheets. The pitched roof and trimming in the room was a nice change from the typically boxy commercial rooms found in chain hotels. Overall the size was fine for the three of us staying there. For about $200/night it wasn't too bad of a deal for th quality.
I also ate at the restaurant a couple of times and found it to be quite good. Nothing blew my mind away but my meals there were some of my favorite I had in Costa RIca. The wait staff were also very quick with their service. It's not bargain prices, $100+ for two people, but the average person will leave full and satisfied.
Hotel Grano de Oro is certainly my top choice when staying in San Jose. One criticism I have for the hotel is the poor WIFI. It's nice to have free internet, but only if it works. Three of us were constantly struggling to get a good signal. A few times we had to go to the lobby for service. Additionally, the staff could be a bit more friendly, energetic and engaged with the staff. You have the comfort to make you feel like you're in a home, you should have staff that make you feel like you're family. But overall I wouldn't hesitate to recommend this hotel to others.

review_text:
I stayed here initially as a one-night 'unavoidable' due to a late arrival from a long flight. The service and experience was so good I booked two further stays. One was an emergency stay after a flight cancellation where I just turned up; the reception staff immediately recognized me even though I had no booking and had only stayed with them for a few hours more than a week earlier. They pourede a drink, found me a room, upgraded it for free due to my flight disappointment and generally behaved like long-lost friends. Impressive. I have booked three more nights here at the end of my Costa Rica trip. Even though San Jose isn't much to write home about, this hotel makes it worthwhile.
Others have written well about the incredible restaurant, perfect service, great rooms and beautiful decor. Put simply, this hotel 'gets' service and style like few others I have stayed in. A true gem.

review_text:
I booked the Grano de Oro through Imagine Latin America as a start and finish point for a two week honeymoon. The building is very attractive from the outside and stands out from its surroundings in San Jose. It's walking distance from the city centre, but I got the impression there wasn't much to see in the immediate vicinity. We were greeted on arrival and kindly given an upgraded room (to deluxe patio) on both occasions we stayed as we'd only booked a standard room because we weren't staying long.
The hotel has real character as it is a warren of corridors but it's all very well decorated and maintained. The room was nicely presented and very clean on both occasions, however a little on the small side. There is a private walled patio which was nice to sit out on and had a small fountain, but this does mean you don't have a view out at all; not that I think there's a huge amount to see around the hotel! There was no bath in the bathroom but the shower was fine.
Although we didn't get time to use them, we went up for a look at the small jacuzzi area on the roof which seemed really nice although could have done with a bit of shade for the sun loungers. The hotel shop was, as you'd expect, fairly expensive ($1.50 for a postcard of the hotel - aren't they usually free?!).
One of the highlights of the hotel is its restaurant which served great breakfasts and absolutely fantastic dinners. The courtyard is really well designed and great to sit out in. The restaurant is definitely a place to dress up in the evenings although being the only place to eat in the hotel, they're quite relaxed about it. We ate dinner twice and weren't disappointed; the food was beautifully prepared and presented and tasted excellent. Wine and cocktails were also very good. The menu certainly isn't cheap, but then the restaurant would quite happily stand up against anything you'd find in major European or US cities so for a splash-out meal, it's worth it.
It would be good if the hotel had another bar area (maybe it did and we missed it?) which was a bit less formal but you can sit in some non-dining sections of the restaurant or at the bar itself.
I'd recommend the hotel as an excellent quality base to stay for a night as a San Jose base, although as even the most dedicated guidebooks tend to admit, there's not a vast amount to keep you entertained in the city as a tourist.

review_text: We only got to enjoy this lovely boutique hotel for one night on our way out of the country. We stayed in the Vista De Oro Suite, which was spacious and luxurious with a beautiful city lights view of the city from the large picture window wall. We also had a private Jacuzzi inside the suite and a private entrance to the suite on the top floor of the hotel. It was beautifully decorated with old world dark wood paneling and furnished with very comfortable and colonial style furniture. The bathroom was also spacious with luxurious linens and towels. The dinner in the hotel restaurant was the best we had in Costa Rica and of high standard for anywhere. I understand why it has been voted the finest restaurant in Costa Rica. The beautiful evening open air setting just added to the ambiance. Breakfast the next morning was also quite good. The public areas and check in check out experiences were all outstanding. The only concern I had was that some of the other rooms appeared quite small looking through the windows on our way to ours. Would we stay again? Absolutely!

review_text:
They say get in and out of San Jose ASAP. They're right, but we stayed here on 2 occassions both entering and leaving the SJ airport. This is a wonderful hotel! We stayed here twice so saw 4 different rooms and they were all unique and comfortable. Rooms here all had good beds, were clean and had roomy modern bathrooms.
Some of the rooms have outdoor patios with water features which were very relaxing. I'd ask for one of those rooms, although the other 2 rooms we had were also nice, just without the patios. Theres a rooftop hot tub (2 actually) set in a little garden which was quiet and nice. There's also a spa here but we didn't use it.
The restaurant here has to be one of the nicest in the city. It's an international menu and lacks in regional fare, but the setting is beautiful in a courtyard with fountain. The food quality was high and the prices were the highest we paid while in CR, but still in-line with American and European restaurants ($20-$30 entrees).
The staff was freindly and spoke perfect english. They have secure parking with overnight securty guard in gated parking lot. They upgraded our room one night which was nice, and they held our luggage between trips in and out of San Jose.
Overall a great place. Maybe the best place in San Jose, unless you're into cookie cutter American chain hotels.

review_text:
My husband and I stayed at this hotel on our honeymoon for one night. This is a beautiful hotel! The staff were all friendly and accommodating. One member in particular went out of his way to make sure we were taken care of - like getting us a bag full of ice for our beers! :)
The grounds are well maintained and there is a beautifully landscaped terrace upstairs with two hot-tubs that we took full advantage of after exploring the city!
Restaurant:
We dined at the hotel's main restaurant. The food was delicious! Dressing up a little wouldn't hurt as the atmosphere is very sophisticated and classy! The food was delicious! However... it's one of those places where it's a tad pricey and your very large plate only has a palmful of food on it! At least that's what we found when we ordered our $12 scallop appetizer - which we thought we would share - but it came with ONE scallop, that we ended up splitting in two. IT was delicious though - and we had a good laugh!
Even though this place is a little too 'posh' for us jeans and t-shirt kids, the hotel is really nice, staff is great, and we definitely enjoyed our stay here!!
Thank you for the great experience :)

review_title: Serenity and Romance in the middle of a noisy city!
review_text:
This environmentally sustained boutique hotel was a sheer delight. The design of the former manor makes every spacious room feel private and it gave us the sense we were the only ones there. Our room overlooked a small courtyard/garden that was the home to several unusual birds - delightful. The restaurant sat in the middle of the hotel and had a charming outdoor courtyard section. Our food was excellent and the tres leches cake was like a slice of heaven! The wait staff were friendly and courteous and very helpful.
The friendly personnel, combined with the design of the building made me feel as if I had stepped back in time to a gentler era. Their efforts to make a minimal impact on the planet made it even more enjoyable. I loved this place and highly recommend it!

review_title: Hotel Grano se Oro, San Jose
review_text:
This is a little boutique hotel haven in San Jose and highly recommended. It used to be the home of a noble family who now own a well known biscuit factory.
It is in typical Spanish colonial style with an inner courtyard used as a dining area when the weather allows.
The rooms are beautifully appointed and very clean.
There are 2 small Jacuzzis on the rooftop terrace.
The food is reported to be the best in San Jose. We found it very good and the waiter service up to scratch with any very good restaurant in Europe. The prices are good and the wine not too expensive.

review_title: Will Stay at No Other Hotel In San Jose
review_text: We spent 4 nights at this tastefully appointed boutique hotel. At check-in, Pablo greeted us with a flute of fresh fruit juice and a plate of fresh fruit awaited us in our room. Marco, the manager has done a great job of placing emphasis on customer service. Everyone was friendly and helpful. They all knew us by our names which added to our comfort. We felt at home. The rooms were small but tastefully decorated. The beds were very comfortable, with quality linens. The bathroom was small and only had one sink but the shower was oversized and very nice. We stayed in two different standard rooms but I would stay in a garden room for our next visit. They actually open on to a beautiful courtyard garden. We also enjoyed the outdoor hot tub on the roof level. It was luxury following a week in the rainforest. If I had a complaint, it would be that the wi-fi did not work in the second room that we had. The staff attempted to have it repaired but to no avail. Inspite of this, I would highly recommend this fine hotel and I would love the opportunity to return.

review_title: A return visit did not disappoint!
review_text:
My husband and I stayed at Grano de Oro seven years ago and found it a charming place. When we headed back to Costa Rica with our extended family, we knew we wanted to introduce them to this little slice of luxury.
The hotel has been remodeled since our last visit. The changes added to the beauty of the hotel, but I was disappointed to see the restaurant had been relocated. You still dine outdoors, but I missed the garden location. We were pleased to see Jose again. In the dining room, Jose is always ready to meet your every needs and make you feel welcome. The food was as delicious as we remembered it from the previous visit. The staff at the front desk was very accommodating.
We rented four rooms and were satisfied with each one. Our room was the Garden Suite. It was spacious and beautiful.
San Jose is not my favorite place to visit. We stop here before heading off to our main vacation stop. It is within walking distance of the market and downtown area. After touring the city, it is nice to return to an "ahhh" spot--relax in a beautiful room, enjoy a refreshing cocktail, and savor a delicious meal.

review_text: I selected this hotel to have dinner for Christmas Eve as it was my last night in Costa Rica and we needed to be closer to the airport. This hotel is nice enough, I would even say beautiful but it is not in a nice area of town. That being said, I do not think there is a nice part of San Jose, CR. However, I think that the person who trains this staff needs to teach a lesson in humility, as these are some of the most snobby staff I've ever had to deal with and I have traveled quite a bit. Yes, it's a nice restaurant, but not the nicest. Yes, the food is good, but it is not great and yes, it's a pretty hotel, but it's in the middle of San Jose, which is a very very depressed neighborhood. There is no need for the uppity attitude given because if it's one facet that makes a place stand out, it's great service and they do not have it here. The waiters are snobs, the bartender is a snob and they take forever in putting your bill together after dinner. I can't understand why there are so many friendly people in Costa Rica, but this place managed to hire all of the creeps.

I would like to see them during the day to see if they live up to other's reviews.

review_text:
My family and I stayed at the Grano de Oro for our last night in Costa Rica -- our guide recommended it because it is close to San Jose's airport. While convenient, it is also a very nice little hotel that helped us end our vacation on a high note.
Grano de Oro is a small hotel, actually converted from a Victorian-era mansion in San Jose. Our rooms were, you might say, "cozy." Still, they were very nice, each with a small outside patio area. We found the staff to be quite friendly and polite.
The restaurant in this hotel is its biggest selling point, I believe. It is outstanding. We had dinner and breakfast, and both meals were simply top notch.
Drawbacks? Its wireless internet was quirky -- on again, off again. That was no big deal for us, but it might be for business travelers. Also, its small size prevents it from offering much beyond comfortable rooms and a winning restaurant. There is a small jacuzzi upstairs, but it was occupied by a couple who obviously wanted some private time. Anyway, my young kids were a little bored.
I rated the hotel's location as poor simply because it is located in San Jose. Sadly, the capital city of beautiful Costa Rica is itself pretty wretched. I would not recommend walking in the area around the hotel.
I was quite pleased with Grano de Oro. I think it would work best for couples, but many business travelers and families will also enjoy it.

review_text:
We have stayed at Grano de Oro San Jose three times, for a total of five nights, at the beginning and end of two trips to other parts of Costa Rica. The hotel started with the restoration of one historically significant estate and has expanded to two adjacent properties. We could not tell where one property began or ended because they have integrated them so well. We stayed in deluxe rooms with adjoining courtyards. All have well cared for fountains or small ponds and luxurious tropical plants. The water features provide a soothing white noise that cancels out any city sounds. We stayed in a standard room one night and it was perfectly acceptable but without the ambiance of the courtyard.
The restaurant is rated as one of the top two in the city. I have not been to other outstanding restaurants in San Jose, so I can only say that the quality of this restaurant is superlative in my experience: lots of fresh, high quality fruit and veggies, and menu that meets the needs of omnivores and vegetarians.
Internet access is spotty. We had good signal in one room and almost none in another. But when we discovered the jacuzzi area on the top floor in with tropical courtyard had good signal, we were OK with going there a couple of times a day.
The staff in both the hotel and restaurant are knowledgeable appropriately attentive. They helped us streamline trips to local museums and to both the regional and international airports. review_text:
A really beautiful rambling building, with comfortable rooms, this is a fine way to begin to step into Costa Rica after arriving from elsewhere, if you are going to spend any time in San Jose itself.
We only spent one night in the Grano de Oro--we flew in in the afternoon, and were picked up at 6 a.m. to leave to river raft on to our next stop (the spectacular Pacuare Lodge). Others were clearly doing something similar, as the early morning lobby (with coffee ready for us all) was filled. You are welcomed on arrival with a glass of tropical juice.
It's a terrific place to stay, and would be for longer. A big rambling wooden building with interior courtyards, small fountains, conservatory area filled with labelled tropical plants, two small rooftop hot plunges side by side. The opposite of a corporate hotel in every way--shuttered windows and the feeling of a real place. Not a hyper-luxurious "boutique" hotel in feeling--except for the grandeur of the restaurante perhaps--but the sheets are great, the bathrooms very nice and very clean, and everything about it felt right. The staff, as everywhere in Costa Rica, was warm, friendly, and helpful.
Our room was good sized and comfortable, with a small desk, a coffee making set up, internet, tv if you wanted, everything you'd need. The restaurant is gorgeous--a destination in itself--and all the food was terrific. I recommend the seemingly simple Tres Leches Cake for dessert. This is "the dessert of the country," and a nice introduction to Tico cooking, unexpectedly interesting of texture and delicious.
This hotel is tucked a little away from the city center, and it's not a long walk to go to see the Vegetable and Fruit Market and Central Market--WELL worth doing, especially the vegetable and fruit market is a feast and a revelation for the eyes, and not a tourist attraction. You walk through a district of hospitals to get there, and that's kind of interesting too (Costa Rica has free health care for all).
So in sum: lovely, welcoming, a place you can breathe in the beginning of a new country.

review_title: Lovely hotel, great food, terrific atmosphere
review_text: We stayed here for two nights before taking a Windstar cruise. This hotel was as lovely and wonderful as the cruise. We stayed in one of the downstairs rooms, which must have been the servants' quarters or storage at one time. But that didn't matter--the room was quite spacious, the bed super comfortable, and we had a delightful private patio with a fountain and goldfish! Dinner and breakfast in the mansion's former living room and courtyard are not to be missed. The food is wonderful, but the ambience is worth even more than the price of the dinner. I absolutely recommend this hotel and would definitely stay here again given the opportuntiy.

review_text:
My initial reservation was broken into 2 parts. A standard room for 1 night and a deluxe for 3. They gave me a complimentary upgrade to a deluxe room the first night so I could stay in the same room all 4 nights. The front desk has been extremely helpful helping me get around San Jose--polite and professional without going over the top.
This place is calm and relaxing. Everything is clean, in order, meticulously cared for, and my room is absolutely gorgeous. I had plans to see a number of things around San Jose these 4 days and I did 1 of them. The allure of reading on the sun deck or relaxing in my room was too much, and since I'm on vacation I get to do whatever I want.
My favorite part of my room are the windows that open up into a central garden. It's so quiet and the air is cool. I can't say enough about the atmosphere of this place. It's been restorative and I would make a trip to San Jose for a weekend getaway just to stay here.
I can't recommend this place enough. Any traveler passing through should soak in a few days here.

review_text: My husband and I enjoyed a one night stay at the start of our recent CR trip. It was our first time in San Jose, but our 5 th in the country. I rate this hotel 4 stars for it's overall atmosphere, spacious rooms, good bed and clean bathroom. The restaurant was also excellent, though the food is quite rich! We also had a nice lunch at a family run restaurant just a short walk away (Maria Bonita). For me, the service at this hotel was just not up to par. Check in was smooth and professional but it went downhill after that. We tried three times to have ice delivered, finally giving up and getting our own. Getting information was a challenge ( not language related), no o e offered to help with our bags when we checked out...a search for a spoon seemed like an impossible task. None of these are deal breakers, but I had read such good things about the service and had been impressed with my email correspondence, so perhaps was a bit let down with the reality. I'd stay again if in San Jose, but maybe lower my expectations a touch!

review_title: Grano de Oro San Jose Costa Rica
review_text:
This hotel is just a gem sitting in San Jose. We enjoyed a deluxe room overlooking the garden.
The room was spacious and nicely appointed. Other rooms on the same floor were standard and smaller. The hotel is a terrific restaurant, arguably the 1st or 2nd rated restaurant in all of San Jose. The service was excellent as was the ambiance. You had the choice of eating in the courtyard or inside with windows and doors opening onto the courtyard. The food was excellent and beautifully presented. For breakfast you had many choices but you could only get whole grain toast and even though bagels were on the menu one could not switch the toast for the bagel which was rather inflexible. But that was our only complaint of an otherwise very well-run restaurant and hotel.. The hotel has free wi-fi which was very good and cable TV which got a few US channels. The hotel is in town but that does not mean you can walk easily to downtown attractions. It is best ot use a cab to get about.

review_text:
Sure the hotel staff was very friendly and helpful, but good service isn't everything. The hotel is located in an ugly neighborhood. I took a walk around the block, and all I saw was iron fences and barbed wire. The hotel looks very out of place. The inside is very charming, and has a B&B feel to it. My room was adequate, but had paper-thin walls. I could hear every word my neighbor was saying. The bathtub/shower has an enormous soap dispenser on the wall with sharp corners. I got a gash on my elbow from banging it on the soap dispenser.
The restaurant is very classy, with a great menu. The food and wine were delicious, but for some reason my waitress ignored me.
I had planned to begin and end my Costa Rican trip at this hotel, but after the first night, I dreaded the thought of spending another night there. Fortunately, the hotel staff was accommodating, and canceled my reservation without any late cancellation fee.

review_text:
My husband and I spent 2 nights in the "Vista de Oro Suite" at the Hotel Grano d’ Oro in late December 2012. The room was lovely, at the top of the hotel, with many windows and views over the city to the mountains beyond. The hotel is in a suburb of San Jose and is a handsome, beautifully decorated former coffee finca (ranch) headquarters with an outstandingly competent front desk staff. They arranged transfers for us to the Saverge River Valley, as well as dinner reservations at the Park Café Restaurant, a culinary gem owned by Richard Neat of Michelin 2 star fame.
Meals themselves at the hotel’s highly rated restaurant were a mixed bag. The ambience of the restaurant is great due to its location in an atmospheric courtyard. Breakfast and lunch there were superb…well served and quite tasty. Our dinner there was less of a success, overly dry fish as an entree and a novice (or just inept) waiter who disappeared after taking our order with only the busboy to pour our wine, bring us dessert menus and respond to our other needs. A very odd experience in what was otherwise a fine hotel.

review_text:
The area surrounding the hotel is "authentic" San Jose showing the city's gritty character but the Hotel Grano de Oro is a welcome oasis. There is a lot to recommend about this place: the inviting lobby, a beautifully appointed restaurant serving good food, the tropical-plant filled corridors and hot-tub area, the charming and clean rooms, and even a quaint little gift store.
But the best thing is the service. We had a number of special requests, like handling a third-party pickup of some specialty items, keeping our tab open while we were away, and turning in our rental car so we could make our flight. These were definitely above and beyond normal hotel service requests, and the staff there went out of their way to not only handle our unusual requests, but to do so with confidence and a smile. (We were particularly fond and appreciate of David at the front desk without whom our trip could have ended poorly.)
We will definitely be back here on our return to Costa Rica.

review_title: Yes - it is as wonderful as the reviews all say
review_text: We just spent 2 nights in San Jose at the Grano de Oro, after flying in on a late flight. Thru prior emails with the hotel, we had arranged pick up at the airport and we were met right at the gate and had received detail instructions from the hotel (cost $35.) Upon check in they confirmed the reservation we had also made via email for dinner the following night and they assisted us the day we were leaving with phoning the car rental company (Economy Rental) which again went off without a hitch. The hotel is within easy walking distance to the downtown sites and the hot tub deck is a treat. Wifi works well, and the air conditioner is efficient and very quiet. The rooms are quaint and the beds are great. Explore the hotel, especially the 2nd floor above the open courtyard, enjoy the historical photographs and by all means visit their restaurant (we ate all our meals there and enjoyed each one of them). It was this hotel which brought us into San Jose for the start of our 2 week vacation and it was well worth it.

review_title: Very good choice for San Jose
review_text:
We stayed at Hotel Grano de Oro two nights, on our arrival and before departure from the San Jose airport.
The desk staff at this hotel are among the best in the industry - very attentive, helpful, and fluent in Spanish and English.
The hotel (we are told) was the home of the Pozuelo family, famous for their cookies which you'll find in most any grocery store in Costa Rica. So, as another writer said, the rooms are similar to a B&B. There is no swimming pool, though there are the two roof-top jacuzzis. The back garden area is heavily planted, so you don't feel like you are in the city. Rooms are very nice and well-kept, though they are a bit small (think large guest bedroom in a friend's house). Everything is very clean, and it was very quiet in our room, though you might hear the facilities from another room at times (not bothersome though).
The restaurant has a nice ambiance, and the outdoor dining area is wonderful for breakfast (it's a central court within the hotel). The food at the restaurant was excellent. We ate there three times, and two of the times the wait staff was exceptional. On one occasion, the waiter was hard to get hold of for any reason, and even when we did, he delayed coming over (this was a different waiter than we'd had previously). Food was always excellent, though...
When you are in this hotel, it feels a bit like you are contained in a small oasis within a not-so-nice area of the city. You can quickly access any sights in town via taxi from here (e.g. National Theatre, the museums), so it's a good location if you want to stay somewhere local and not be in a generic chain hotel.
Accessibility is pretty good if you get a first floor room - just the entry stairs to deal with.

review_text:
Aside from what has been said again and again about this being a beautiful hotel (which it is,) I wanted to write to let you know that it is also a hotel with heart.
Last week I developed a severe allergy and was told that I could leave the hospital but must stay somewhere nearby and we chose Hotel Grano de Oro. About 15 minutes after checking in, my allergy returned and I had to rush immediately back to the hospital, where I was admitted and told I could not leave that night. We knew that it was a lot to ask to refund our stay, especially because all of our belongings were in the room and they could have used it for someone else.
When I was finally released the next afternoon, the staff graciously let us know that would not be charging us for that last night. It literally brought tears to my eyes, especially after already having had to pay for the hospital stay.
We ended up spending the next night there and it was the perfect place to relax and recover.
We would definitely recommend them, not only for the beauty and character of the hotel but for the kindness and empathy that they show their guests. Muchas gracias por todo!!

review_title: Stunning hotel BUT Camera stolen from room
review_text:
If you are lucky enough to stay at this beautiful hotel; use the room safe, don't leave your hotel room unlocked EVEN upon checkout, take valuables with you, because there is no loyal housekeeper there! Only opportunists!
My boyfriend and I stayed here on Christmas eve for a couple of nights and the hotel is a dream! Decor, food, ambience, quality, all was everything you could wish for. And i so wish i could leave the review at that.
On our date of checkout, our camera was stolen by housekeeping. There was very little sympathy from the reception staff who were extremely slow to react, making us feel as though we had made up the story of the lost camera! Extremely frustrating.
We stayed with friends in San Jose for the following nights and called the hotel each day to see if anyone had 'found' (handed in the camera or camera card) which we now offered a cash reward for, being that all of our photo's of a month of travelling through Panama were on the card.
The woman at reception was rude and un-helpful, even telling me that 'we (the hotel) don't trust or believe you, you could have left the camera somewhere outside of the hotel'. I was brought to tears each time i spoke with her!
Eventually we returned to the hotel at one last attempt to plea to the housekeeper who took the camera to let us keep the photo's. The hotel owner met with us instead and although he was extremely gracious and sympathetic, he was unable to help, baffled that his loyal staff of 20yrs would steal anything.
We had been travelling for one month, staying in hostels, hotels, guest houses of varying standards, dorms, private rooms etc and not one item had been stolen. We came to Costa Rica, treated ourselves and stayed in the best hotel in San Jose for Christmas and our camera was stolen by housekeeping.
The mistake of leaving our room door open on checkout is one that we wont be making again as it enticed housekeeping to take the camera, and gave them the get out clause that it was our mistake to leave the door open and another guest must have walked in and taken the camera.
Not the case due to a number of other factors which i won't bore you with. The camera was stolen, by staff at the Grand de Oro. I wish i could upload photo's of the hotel for you as it is beautiful - but they are long gone!

review_text: We stayed at Grano de Oro for a one night lay over before we started touring the rest of the country. We were greeted with a warm welcome from the hotel staff. Our room was very unique. They even called our room to let us know we were being picked up ten minutes later than our scheduled arrival time. All in all it was a great experience!!

review_text:
Hotel Grano de Oro is a little oasis in a bustling Central American city. After a day of business and/or sightseeing, it is a pleasure to arrive at this beautiful quiet, luxurious hotel. The bar and restaurant are both excellent, and the service is very good.
We stayed in a garden Suite, and it was very spacious and refined.
Our only concern was that there is no dedicated concierge.The front desk staff are helpful, but not very knowledgeable. We were directed in the opposite direction of a restaurant towards which we were planning on walking! The manager, Marco, actually jogged to our assistance, when we called to tell them we were lost, so we can't be too upset!
Overall, this place is a little gem.

When we checked in the desk person made cab arrangements for the next morning having us pre-pay to avoid early morning problems. We had a fresh fruit basket in our clean beautiful room with birthday greetings. After our extensive tour of Costa Rica relaxing in one of the hot tubs on the roof was very welcome and relaxing. The restaurant atmosphere was elegant, but also unpretentious and friendly. My wife and I are both chefs and we enjoyed a superb dining experience. The next morning at 6am our cab was warmed up and waiting. All in all a wonderful way to end our vacation. Thank you

review_text: I kept fantasizing that Teddy Roosevelt had to have come to this place when it was a plantation house. It is truly a beautiful hotel, immaculately clean, with wonderful staff across the board. My husband and I stayed here our first night in Costa Rica, arriving too late to begin our planned excursion north. And then from our second excursion on the Caribbean coast, we returned to the Grano de Oro to stay the night before we were to fly back home to NY. This time we could avail ourselves of the restaurant for dinner. We tried small plates and everything was superbly prepared as well as impeccably flavored. Our waiter, Carlos Castro, was charming as ever and even though we didn't order dessert, gave us a couple of amazingly delicious bonbons to complete our meal. It was a truly splendid way to end our trip.

review_title: Wow! *This* is where to stay in San Jose
review_text:
My fiance and I stayed here for one night on the tail end of our journey to Costa Rica. The grounds were a former plantation house converted to a hotel, and if you take a look at the collages they have posted, you can see what an amazing transformation the hotel has undergone in the last 20 years. Our room was wonderful, complete with a little grotto and fountain. The rooftop lounge area was very nice- we were happy to utilize the hot tub after all our Costa Rican adventures.
We ate dinner at the restaurant on premises, and it was a very classy, delicious way to end our trip.
Definitely recommend this hotel (and restaurant) if you're going to be in San Jose. Wonderful!

review_title: Great restaurant, OK hotel, mediocre staff and services
review_text:
We stayed at Grano de Oro for 2 nights on the tail end of our trip to Costa Rica. First of all, there's not that much to do or see in San Jose and we were there Dec 30 and 31 so all the museums were closed. Grano de Oro is a beautiful renovated hotel, and it's very nicely decorated. It's in town with absolutely nothing nice within walking distance but cabs are easy to get. The restaurant is gorgeous and the best food we had in Costa Rica but very expensive. As for the hotel, our room was very small but cute and comfortable. The jacuzzi on the roof had no view, was tiny and not hot enough. My biggest complaint was the customer service. Throughout our trip in Costa Rica, we had the best service in all hotels, people were so nice and helpful. Not at Grano de Oro. We asked them to book a white water rafting tour for us. In all the hotels we stayed, we always had the hotels book our tours (zip lining, ATV, etc) because they know the companies. Grano de Oro booked us with the WORST company: completely unacceptable (late, horrible food, no water, no toilet paper in bathrooms, dangerous, the list goes on and on). The hotel really should have done their research on this or told me they had no idea and I would have picked a company from my guidebook. When I spoke with hotel manager about it, he was sorry but didn't do anything about it (could have perhaps at least offered to buy us a drink or bottle of wine as an apology?) AFter all, the tour they booked for us was $100 per person.
Bottom line: there's not much going on in San Jose so unless you need to be there, get in and get out. If you want to do some touring of the area (to visit volcanos or national parks or museums in San Jose) , better to stay outside of the city -- we stayed in Alajuelo at a place called Buena Vista which I loved and which is about 20 minutes from the airport and 40 minutes to Volcano Poas.

review_title: Luxury in the heart of San Jose
review_text:
On our trips to Costa Rica, this is the hotel we have stayed for the first and last nights. The hotel is beautiful and centrally located in a rather unassuming neighborhood...but the rooms are very comfortable and the staff is very friendly. One of my favorite aspects of this hotel is the restaurant: fantastic food! I could eat there all the time! What I liked about it too was that the restaurant appeared to be filled with older, high class 'ticos'....but my brother and I (20 & 15 at the time) were treated well. Even though we look younger than that, the servers were still very friendly and didn't treat us differently (which has happened at certain luxury establishments in the US).
It is also right around the corner from a great park to watch (or play) soccer in a beautiful park. San Jose isn't exactly scenic compared to the rest of the country, but this hotel takes your mind off of it.
The staff is very helpful with whatever you need and especially when we arrived on our first day with SO MANY bags. The guy who was driving us for our vacation and the people at the hotel must have been shocked...but they wouldn't allow us to help them. They just seem to go out of the way to make things easier for you and yet aren't intrusive.
A beautiful hotel that's centrally located close to the city and the airport and a fantastic first stop on your excursion to this beautiful nation!
I would stay nowhere else in San Jose. Our family was there in Costa Rica for I believe 17 days and we had a guy drive us around to the different places because we didn't want to rent a car. The hotel coordinated everything with the driver from check in to check out....it all worked out perfectly.
Great hotel!

review_title: Depending on your room, it's wonderful or unacceptable!
review_text: My husband, daughter and I stayed here on either end of an action filled trip to CR. we spent no time in San Jose, so we really only required a night's comfortable lodging. The hotel is a former mansion, very charming and homey. but beware that the rooms are wildly distinct. On our arrival night we had a sweet-2 lovely rooms connected through a bathroom. Very very nice. Even nicer than we needed, as the queen plus single bed in the main room could have sufficed. But on our departure night, we were given a room that had only one window which opened onto the corridor of the hotel (in it's day, this was likely a staff room facing the courtyard of the original mansion). There was a screen and rock garden to separate us from the guests walking down the hall, but clearly we could not keep this window open to hear and be heard. We were told there was no other room available with two beds. For one night it was okay to shut the window and make do. But if we had been staying longer, this would have been unacceptable lodging. Not sure what we paid since it was part of a package our travel agent assembled, but my guess is we paid much more than this particular room was worth.

review_text:
What a gorgeous hotel! Sadly, I was only there for one night, arriving late and leaving early to catch my flight home from Costa Rica. Since I had been staying in more rural Montezuma for the past two weeks, I was really looking forward to a clean, quiet, bug-free accommodation, and that's exactly what I got.
Since I was traveling alone, I booked their Standard room, which was exactly as the picture shows. Room enough for a big, comfortable bed, a chair and table, an armoire, and a lovely black and white tiled bathroom with a divine shower. I can't tell you how relaxing it was to go into this beautiful little oasis, shut the door, and revel in the peace and quiet.
After changing out of my jungle-y clothes and enjoying the fabulous shower I went down to the restaurant for a solo dinner. The food was amazing, the restaurant absolutely gorgeous, and the staff attentive. I felt as though I were truly back in time-- the mansion has been beautifully maintained, and really has a sense of magic about it.
In the morning, my taxi to the airport was ready and waiting at the early time that I had requested. Hotel Grano de Oro really made my last night in Costa Rica pleasant, memorable, and perfect. Highly recommend it!

review_title: Good choice close to center of San Jose
review_text:
Our first stop on a 2 week vacation to Costa Rica was in San Jose. We were only here for 2 nights and 1 full day so wanted to stay somewhere centrally located. Hotel Grano de Oro was very central to the center of San Jose and we were able to walk to see the area which made it very convenient. The hotel itself is very nice. Our room was on the 2nd floor, well appointed, nice hardwood floors and wood trim, high ceilings and large bathroom. It was one of our favorite rooms on our trip. The staff was very helpful overall. I think it would make a good business hotel if you were in San Jose for business purposes, and it did appear that they had several small but nice priviate dining rooms for private/group dinners. The restaurant, including the courtyard area was very well appointed as well and we wish the weather had been warmer so we could have enjoyed the courtyard area.
There were several minor disappointments - 1) our room was on a side of the hotel that faces a very, very busy street (with cars, trucks and buses) during the day. The traffic starts very early in the morning and street noise makes it hard to sleep in past 6:30/7:00 AM. Would have been nice to have double paned glass in the windows to help with noise reduction. 2) Even though it's located near the center of San Jose, there really aren't any restaurants within walking distance, especially at night. We arrived late in the evening, the hotel restaurant was closing and would only allow us to grab a glass of wine (no food since kitchen was closed) and we would have had to take a taxi anywhere to eat - not something you really want to do after 8 hours of flying and arriving in a new and unknown city/environment.
Overall, I think it's a good choice if you want to be close to the center of San Jose.
