I stayed here for a night. It is a gorgeous oasis in a busy city. Our room was well appointed (2 flat screen tvs in less than 200 square feet!), very comfortable beds, great shower and lovely view of a garden. The restaurant (we had lunch and breakfast there) is fantastic, with updated twists on local food. The portions were huge, but it was too good to stop eating.
The front desk staff is really horrible, though, which is why I can't give the hotel more stars. They were so unwelcoming and unaccommodating that even though I loved the hotel itself, I don't know that I'd recommend it. We asked them to help us with an early morning tour to Poaz before our flight. After going around and around with us about the timing, they agreed to call one local guide for a personal tour. He didn't answer and they promised to keep calling until they got a response and would get back to us either way. We're still waiting for that call almost a week later (i.e., they never followed up with us). Having missed that opportunity, we asked for some recommendations for walking around before our flight. They basically said, there's nothing to see, you're out of luck, you should have booked a tour. Really? Four people were sitting behind the desk chatting with each other while we checked out, and all were really rude and distracted. They got annoyed when we asked for a cab to the airport and really couldn't have cared less if we were pleased or not.
Booking tours and getting in and out of San Jose (places to go/places to avoid) needs a bit of help, so it's disappointing that such a beautiful place would have such unhelpful staff. Just keep it in mind if you decide to stay there and do your homework on tours ahead of time.

review_text:
This hotel is fantastic - we stayed for our first night after arriving late in San Jose, and then again our last night before leaving Costa Rica. Grano de Oro is a great base if you're arriving or leaving the country, but we wished we had stayed longer and used it for day-trips out of San Jose. Staying at Grano de Oro was really enjoyable, I wish we had had more nights!
The service is unprecedented and probably the best we've received anywhere we've ever travelled. The staff were so friendly and so helpful - from the moment I contacted them to ask about availability, to welcoming us in reception, even to the point where they were kind enough to call the airline on my behalf when we were in an area without any telephone signal. Everybody at the hotel was really friendly, even the porter who took us to our room, showed us how the air-conditioning works and asked us to double check the bathroom to make sure it was pristine clean!
We booked a Deluxe room with two double beds, which was large and had a large bathroom. On one of our nights we got upgraded to a Family Suite, which was fantastic, with two separate rooms. The beds are really comfortable, which was just perfect after a long international flight.
We had breakfast at the hotel court-yard, the food was delicious - they had a range from pancakes to the traditional Costa Rican breakfast of gallo pinto. We loved their fresh-fruit juices. We also tried lunch and dinner there, both excellent, the food at dinner was a work of art! Again the service in the restaurant was first-class, the waiters always there just when you need them. A lot of local people come to the restaurant and, especially during dinner time, most people dress up - men in suits, ladies in high heels. You can dress as you want but we felt more comfortable in a summer dress/ shirt for my husband.
The atmosphere at the hotel is relaxed, nothing is too much trouble. All staff speak very good English. We arranged airport transfers through the hotel, everything worked perfectly. It took about half an hour to get from the airport to the hotel.
We loved our stay at Grano de Oro and would definitely recommend it.

review_text:
We had the pleasure of staying here for one night. I wish there had been more to keep us in San Jose so we could have extended the experience.
Grano de Oro hits all the right notes. The property is gorgeous and the staff is incredibly efficient and friendly. Everything is comfortable, even when it's formal.
They have done a phenomenal job updating this beautiful, historic property to the modern age. If I had to find a complaint it would be that you can hear some noise from the hallway if other guests are talking outside your room. This is because of the way the building was constructed so many years ago. This is a tiny quibble, though.
The restaurant was also delicious and the setting couldn't be more lovely.
If you have the chance, stay here. Really. I can't wait to go back.

review_title: Old world charm in San Jose
review_text: We spent 2 nights (1 night at the beginning, 1 night at the end of our trip) at the Hotel Grano de Oro. Everything about this hotel is top notch! The moment we arrived the hotel staff directed us to a parking spot (parking is free!), and helped us carry our luggage into the lobby. In the lobby we were greeted with warm smiles and hellos, and delicious glass of fresh fruit juice! The hotel itself is stunning...an old mansion that is beautifully decorated with dark hardwood, artwork and black & white pictures on the walls, chandeliers hanging in the halls, and lush courtyard's tucked within the grounds. The rooms are lovely, with comfortable beds and white linens, and a gleaming bathrooms! We also enjoyed taking a relaxing dip in the hot tubs on the roof. The restaurant in the hotel was also fantastic! The only downside was the WiFi -- although free, it was a bit spotty at times and we had trouble getting it to work. Other than that we LOVED this place! If you're coming San Jose this is the place to stay!

review_title: A Classic Hideaway in the Heart of the City!
review_text: We spent a short night here on our way from the coast to the airport the next morning, but what a memorable and enjoyable experience! I've not travelled much of the world, but this hotel reminded me of classic hotel you might find in the French Quarter in New Orleans, and I could just as easily imagine it in Paris. A beautiful, quiet, spotless hotel split into sections giving you a quaint, private feel. Our room faced a covered but open outdoor courtyard full of local fauna and giving you a very private feel. Our room was spotless with georgeous hardwood floors, wonderful beds, modern but classic bathroom and lovely ceiling fans. The restaurant and bar were wonderful just to be in and relax, let alone the outstanding food. Lots of warm, beautiful wood, relaxed quiet atmosphere, natural gas flame lighting put you at ease immediately. A wonderful staff that was extremely helpful yet very unobtrusive. I will definetely be back on my next trip to Costa Rica! Pura Vida!!

Great value, sweet location for wandering to a few of San Jose's hot spots plus an incredible on site restaurant to boot. Perfection!
We loved that the hotel had historical character... Lots of winding stairways and paths. Our room was on the ground floor and was more spacious than we expected, immaculately clean with WiFi, solitude and genuine good karma!
After check in we explored the area by foot before dusk. We then took advantage of the roof top hot tubs. Bliss! We were the only ones there! We tidied up and made our way to the glorious restaurant for dinner.
One word about our dinner at Grano de Oro: WOW! Seriously, if you stay here, do yourself a favor and enjoy dinner here. I imagine breakfast would be incredible too! We decided to explore a bit and walked to Soda Tapia for breakfast and were glad we did. Hotel staff delightfully pointed us in the right direction. I want to stay two nights next time to enjoy both Soda Tapia AND Grano de Oro breakfasts! :)
A quick side note about the restaurant: While there did not seem to be a dress code, we tried to be respectful and stepped it up a notch a bit due to the restaurant's classy elegant decor. My husband wore khakis and a light shirt while I wore a sundress and my signature gold "Costa Rica" flip flops. :) Meanwhile, we observed a couple wearing sweat pants and hoodies! While this is normally acceptable attire for adventure travel in Costa Rica, I must say they looked REALLY out of place at the restaurant. Please, pack at least a sun dress / smart casual shirt if you're visiting here! No heels/dress shoes required! Just step it up a wee bit before going on your adventure! I mean, c'mon, the servers were in ties! Give THEM some respect! :)
I digress...
There's just simply something special about Grano de Oro that one can't describe unless you've been. Is it a big chain 5 star resort? Absolutely not. Grano de Oro is 5 star in its own Central American boutique way. Please keep it a secret!
I can't image staying elsewhere when in need of a San Jose stay. We will be back. Hopefully soon. Gracias!

review_title: Really nice hotel, really lovely dining
review_text:
We stayed here on the first and last nights of our trip to Costa Rica. It is twenty minutes from the airport, so convenient for late night arrival and early morning departures.
This was our anniversary trip and I had mentioned this when booking and upon arrival, there was a fruit tray and a note wishing us a happy anniversary; it was a nice touch. When you arrive at reception, they great you with a "welcome drink" which was passion fruit (with maybe another fruit mixed in?) - it was delicious.
We had booked a standard that they upgraded to a deluxe king for our first night, we had booked a deluxe king for our second stay. Both nights were spent in the same room - 23. It is a nice room with its own private garden located on the first floor in a hallway tucked away in the back. It was very quiet and relaxing. The bed was perfect - not too firm, not too soft.
San Jose is definitely a busy city, but we did not feel that the area around the hotel nor the downtown area itself was intimidating or sketchy in anyway. We live in a city, so are used to the noise, energy and fast-pace of a bustling city. We walked into downtown and had no worries about safety.
We ate breakfast and dinner here - both were excellent. The restaurant is very pretty. The cappuccino was so good, and they had decaf which was great for me. We ate dinner here as well on our last night before leaving Costa Rica and it was perfect, a really great meal. It is formal dining, so the prices reflect a nicer restaurant in a major city. They offered us an amuse bouche of english pea soup with goat cheese - it was seriously good. I could have ate a bowl of it. I had spinach salad with avocado and other things, it was fresh and good. My husband had a caprese salad he loved. I had the rabbit with wine and black cherry sauce, my husband had the pork tenderloin with tamarind and mango, both came with veg and a side of mashed potatoes - all of it was gloriously good. We had a dessert of bailey's ice cream and a cake with a raspberry coulis - so tasty. The whole meal from start to end was so good, a great anniversary celebration dinner.
The staff are so accommodating, professional and welcoming. At our return check in, they welcomed us back, the one staff member remembered us and asked how our trip had been.
Coming back to Cosat Rica (which we will do sooner rather than later) I would definitely stay here and eat here again. We really liked it.

review_title: Best Hotel of San José, Costa Rica
review_text:
Restaurant serves very good food, but the Hotel-staff (reception) always try to put you in a room you didn't book (and payed for): rooms & bathroom OK, but 1 Queensbed per room, instead of 2 at each room (we are a family of four) on arrival from Amsterdam. We accepted due to our delay and missing baggage, we were overtired and just wanted to sleep. When we came back after our travel for 3 weeks through Costa Rica, we got 1 big double room with 2 Queen beds for the kids, as ordered and payed for, for us, as parents, we could get a big room with 1 Queen size bed. As we did not accept this, they offered us a really small room, sort of shoe-box, with a Kingsize bed.
Not according to what we ordered and payed for this hotel.
Nevertheless, it seems to be the best hotel in San José, but they have a lot to learn, like don't cheat your clients. The restaurant is superb, the only High Cuisine in Costa Rica. The hotelrooms in the "Old part, the original building" are the nicest rooms with a view over the restaurant.

review_text:
Costa Ricans are generally friendly and hospitable, but this charming little hotel takes it to new heights. Not only is the accommodation spotless, modern yet elegant in colonial style, but the staff really do everything they can to help, with a smile. I stayed a couple of nights, then went around the country with a small bag: they kept my luggage safe at no charge. I had trouble with the internet connection: they sent someone to my room three times with various solutions until it was sorted out.
The restaurant is reputed and many locals dine there. It's rather expensive, but the food is excellent and includes Costa Rican specialities. Breakfast in the lush courtyard is another expensive pleasure, a luxury to treat oneself to after days of plain gallo pinto and coffee in mountain villages.
They will arrange airport pick-ups and excursions on request.

review_title: The perfect spot if you are visiting San Jose
review_text:
The place is beautiful but here were my complaints:
There were two jacuzzis and only one was in use due to maintenance. The one that was usable was colder than bath water and it would have been nice to be able to relax before our long flight the next day
The room on the second floor shakes intermittently, almost like a small earthquake.
The room was extremely noisy from the outside street noise which kept us from our sleep
Other than that, the rooms are spacious and the staff are the most professional of the ones we experienced on a two week trip through 5 cities.

review_text:
I decided to drive back to San Jose and stay the night before I flew out the next afternoon. It's a long drive fro Dominical to SJO and I didn't want to have to wake up super early or stress out on my last day there. And then....
I'm going to assume that my experience in getting to/finding this hotel was a fluke. I don't know what happened to its location on Google Maps on in the GPS but it was wrong. So so wrong. The direction they have on the website are correct but the coordinates are wrong. If you get lost, it's difficult to find your way back because there are 3 different areas where "Calle 30 between Ave 2 and 4" could be. Literally same street names. They don't use addresses in CR, just markers. So just be careful, I got lost for 2 hours in another part of town and then I got stuck in traffic. So much for not stressing.
That said, the hotel staff did their best to try to guide me there. They were courteous and did what they could. Once I *finally* arrived at the hotel, I was so happy. Possibly because I had just spent 7 hours in a car (4 driving from Dominical and then 3 trying to find this place). haha. The hotel is lovely, the restaurant has delicious food, the staff is kind and helpful, the rooms are clean.
Keep in mind that when they say you get a "terrace" it means an enclosed area with doors separating it from the main bedroom that looks like a garden. This upset me at first as there were no windows in my room but then remembered that San Jose isn't very pretty outside. It's the city. So I enjoyed my terrace. The stress was gone. The bed is sooo comfortable. After hiking and riding and all kinds of physical activity on my trip, that bed was heaven.
The breakfast was tasty and obviously the coffee was good. The pressure in the shower was GREAT. A nice change as I was shifting back into my reality.
I do recommend this place to stay if you're looking to spurge on your first & last nights in Costa Rica. I would stay here again and this is what I would do:
* Fly to SJO - take hotel shuttle from airport to hotel.
* Book a car from Budget rental (in advance) - they are 2 blocks from the hotel. You can pick up your car after your 1 night, load up the car and be on your way to see the rest of the country.
* At the end of your trip, stay your last night here. Drive to the hotel (now that you know where it is) unload the car and drive it 2 blocks back to Budget. Have a lovely dinner.
* Order your breakfast as room service. Take a shuttle from the hotel to SJO the next morning.
Hope this helps! Pura Vida!

review_title: A Perfect Beginning to a Costa Rica Getaway
review_text:
My girlfriend and I had the pleasure of staying at Hotel Grano de Oro for a single night prior to hopping on a morning flight out of Pavas. I can’t speak for the surrounding neighborhood, as we didn’t have much time to venture off the property. But I can say that every moment spent on the hotel premises was perfect in every respect. And how many hotels can you say that about?
Our deluxe room was the kind you could literally spend all day in – lots of colonial charm, extremely quiet, with great wireless reception when we needed to “plug in.” What’s more the property was operated by a super friendly and highly attentive staff who quickly made us feel welcome. And last but not least, there is a lovely restaurant on site that offers a sophisticated yet diverse menu. Truthfully, dinner wasn’t a knockout, but breakfast the next morning in the courtyard more than made up for it.
If I ever make it back to San Jose, this is where I’ll be staying again.

review_title: Gracious and attentive service and elegant establishment
review_text: We stayed at this hotel the first night of our vacation in Costa Rica, and it was a great initial exposure for the Costa Rican experience! "Attention to detail" best describes this establishment, which also houses a most exquisite restaurant. The food was excellent, and on Saturday evening they had live music and dancing too. The room was exceptionally clean, with a focus on all of the little details. The room we stayed in had an outdoor patio with a fountain and a little pond, which actually contained live fish! The beds were very comfortable and the room was elegantly furnished, bathroom was super clean and stylish, and the service was very gracious and accommodating. We will definitely return to this establishment on our next visit to San Jose.

review_text:
We stayed here on 2 separate nights in July. This is an oasis of a hotel situated in downtown San Jose. On the first night we had the family room which was very good for a family of 4. On the second we shared a room with 2 double beds, which had plenty of room. The rooms are very comfortable. The building is beautiful with great charm. The staff are always helpful and organised our transfer to the airport ($30 for 4 people) which is around 20-30 minutes away. We also had an evening meal in the restaurant. This is a stunning setting. It is about a 15 minute walk to the centre of San Jose and the cab cost ~$5.
This hotel has real quality and is worth staying in, if in San Jose

review_title: Nice little oasis in the city
review_text:
We stayed here while traveling through Costa Rica and Panama from 6/30 to 7/15. We were at the Gran de Oro for two nights 7/4 and 7/6. The staff at the hotel was great and very accommodating. We left most of our luggage with the staff while we traveled for overnight rafting, which turned out to be very helpful. The rooms are beautifully designed, both our rooms contained a fountain in it. It's about a $3 to $4 cab ride into the heart of the city from the hotel.
Best attributes:
- Helpful and courteous staff
- Every room is unique
- Beautiful outdoor restaurant (Great Wine Selection)
Dislikes:
- No pool. One of the jacuzzis was not working when we were there (But really who goes to San Jose to swim in a pool)

This is a lovely hotel on the west side of town, close to the park called La Sabana. It has restaurants in walking distance, and a wonderful, wonderful staff. We stayed here twice, and both times were very happy. We also left our luggage here between stays, and they were very accommodating. There is a beautiful courtyard restaurant (pricy), that serves breakfast and dinner.
We walked to La Sabana, which has the new soccer stadium and one museum. A few restaurants in walking distance. Most of the action is more toward the center of town, requiring a cab, car or bus ride.

review_title: A must when visiting San José
review_text:
I think there are no real five star hotels in Costa Rica. Basically big chain hotels can be found like Marriot or Intercontinental, but of course, no flavor can be found in those. Luckily for tourist, Grano de Oro can enhance the experience of San José City. Although San José is the simplest part of magnificent Costa Rica, is a mandatory stop at arrival and for many, at depature. Also, is the best to try local food, as many of the places are flooded with restaurants to please the ones who look for American or Tex-Mex food.
Grano de Oro, then, is a boutique four star hotel with local flavor and attentive staff. Lobby is small but calmed, with computers for guests to use. At arrival we were greeted with a delicious juice fruit. Our room wasn’t ready, but it was more a fault of our tour operator than the hotel. As we had to leave early next day, we requested breakfast the they before and were willing to help us. It was not that early for a box lunch, but early enough to have it ready at 7:05 (restaurant opens at 7:00am). Actually it was delicious.
The room has personality and convenient facilities. I think that the shower could benefit for more water pressure and improve with better amenities. However, a dispenser in the bathroom seems a common practice in Costa Rica. The Bed is comfortable and linens are good. The décor is unique. I suggest checking noise isolation, as sometimes some things from the corridors can be heard. They have Britt coffee (good) for the morning.
When we go back to San José I would like to stay at Grano de Oro again.

review_text: I was planning a trip for my husband and I - and we needed to spend one night in San Jose before starting our vacation at Arenas del Mar in Quepos area...I emailed Grano de Oro and they were so easy to correspond with...and they even helped me with a transfer from the airport to the hotel...when we got off of our flight from the US....and entered the San Jose airport...there was a person holding a sign with our name waiting for us! The hotel was beautiful and classy though! We had a really nice room with a patio area...and we did have a late dinner at the restaurant...I would say it was just "good" food...not extraordinary. But the comfort of having the beautiful hotel and that we didn't have to venture out to try and find a late night dinner in a city that we aren't familiar with...made this a great stay. The hotel staff was very nice too...I would recommend!

review_text:
I have had the good fortune of staying here on several occasions. From the door man, to the hotel and restaurant staff, the service is top notch. The hotel grounds and rooms are impeccably clean and the setting, amidst the hustle bustle of busy San Jose, is sublime. All rooms have a ceiling fan, WiFi, TV. and air conditioning.
The hotel was converted from a coffee plantation and is lovely. There is a full bar and restaurant where tasty, high quality food is served to late night travelers.
A travel tour bus was scheduled to pick us up by 6:00a.m. the following morning and the kind wait staff made sure we had freshly brewed coffee before our early departure.
Hotel Grano de Oro offers five star service at very reasonable prices.
Pura Vida!

review_title: I'm sad we only stayed one night!
review_text: We spent our first night in CR at the Grano de Oro before going to Arenal. There are not enough words of praise for this hotel. It was actually a house that was converted into a very nice, elegant, Victoria style hotel. We stayed in a superior room with two beds which was great for us that were traveling with our 9 year old son. I loved the decor, the wood floors, the space and every touch in the room and bathroom. It had a very good size! We were lucky to have breakfast in the restaurant because service and the ambience in the open patio were perfect. They offer complimentary wifi too. Owners of this hotel should buy more hotels all over the world and take their very nice taste and high standards everywhere. Services was also very good.

review_title: Excellent hotel if you want close to downtown San Jose.
review_text:
We stayed here for 4 nights as we wanted to explore San Jose. We are a family of 5 and got the family room, that has 1q and 1sgl in the main room with a separate queen in the separate bedroom. There is a shared bathroom. Beds are excellent for comfort. Excellent for families for 5 !. The hotel is really beautiful. The staff are very friendly. I could go to lobby and get hot water forntea any time if day or Night. 2 computers in lobby to use for research, check mail, of leave your teen to play on for a while. There are 2 hot tubs on the roof, ( our room overlooked thru the trees). They are warm, not hot, and one was broken while we were here.. But we used the one several nights and it was enjoyable. Banos out there as well, so you don't have to run to your room, if you need to go !
. If you want to rent car for a day or 2 there are several places 2 short blocks walk.

review_text: Overall,this is a good place to stay in San Jose. We stayed in a superior room which was in a small back garden area and the room was fairly nice ( one would expect for the $180.00 price). The staff was very accomodating and would help with anything if asked to do so. There were a few drawbacks - the hotel is located about a 15 minute walk from downtown and there are not a lot of attractions close by. The restaurant located on site is fairly good but is seriously overpriced compared to other restaurants of the same quality. Other than this, the hotel is top notch and i would recommend at least one night to check it out.

review_text: The hotel is a welcome retreat that will make you forget how unappealing San Jose is once you're inside. The rooms were nothing special from a functionality stand point, but were decorated in the style of a what you'd expect in a Central American mansion. There's a great little terrace with a jacuzzi and the interior is all open air with fountains and plants. The real star of this place is the restaurant. It has amazing dark wood molding and ornate staircases that are original to the building. The food was classic French, that was presented a very 1980 way, but absolutely deliciousness nonetheless. I would probably never bother to stay in San Jose again, but I'd definitely come back here if I did.

This is definetly the hotel to consider in San Jose.

review_text:
What an experience!
This is a superb hotel, probably the best you can book in San Jose. Upon arrival we were given a fruit cocktail while we checked in, setting the tone for the rest of the stay.
Our room was a good size, with a small courtyard containing a fountain and plants. The bathroom was plushly decorated with ample space.
I'd recommend having a stroll around the hotel - it contains a tropical garden courtyard, library and roof terrace with amazing city views.
The restaurant has an outside area as well as a well-apointed inside dining area. The menu is large and reasonably priced for a hotel of this calibre. The only downside for me was the presence of Foie Gras on the menu (a totally unnecessary act of culinary pretention and cruelty in my opinion).
Over all, this hotel is a haven of luxury and tranquility in what can be a hectic city. Staying here would be highly recommended.

review_title: Victorian spendor in San Jose Costa Rica
review_text:
Wow this place is a magnificent restored mansion with ice cold rooms and great beds at a fair price . They really try super hard to take care of you and the WI-FI is the best ever in a hotel .
Now when I go to a restaurant in another country you have to take the culture and flavors under consideration . Why isn't this restaurant area packed out ? Certainly the dining area is superb but for the price of the food wholly molly its just not up to par . You need reservations because its not very filled so they keep staff as needed . Everything gets doused in a not so original gravy although my corvina (fish everything is corvina down here for some reason ) and later fajitas was a 10 . Gordon Ramsay really needs to pop in because the culinary aspects of such a fine looking place are not better really than a Fridays and that is sad because this fine place deserves "fine dining" . The service does magnificent with what they have to work with . You will pay a fortune for your dinning experience here by the way . My advice , stay here , use the Jacuzzi , relax . Have a drink at the bar , but definitely eat elsewhere .

review_text: We stayed here for two nights at the beginning of our trip in Costa Rica. It is well priced and located only about a mile from the central walk in town and tourist attractions. We walked everywhere and had no problems at all. The staff was very helpful and the food in the restaurant was delicious. We arrived too late for dinner the first night--but had a lovely basket of fruit and a bottle of wine awaiting us (we had upgraded to a suite) and we stowed our stuff and kicked back and relaxed overlooking the city. The second night we had dinner in the dining room and it was delicious! Breakfast was included in our room rate and it was excellent as well. I loved the Gallo Pinto there--lots of different flavors. We will book this hotel again!

review_text: We will absolutely come back to this hotel! I don't normally write reviews about hotels but in this case I have to make an exception. Our family visited San Jose in February 2012. We stayed for 2 weeks venturing out on day trips seeing as much of Costa Rica as we could. It was always a highlight returning to the peaceful sanctuary of the Hotel Grano de Oro. Service was always first class and the staff treated us as if we were family. The restaurant is amazing! It was nice to be able to have the choice to either sit inside their beautiful Victorian era dining room or in their outdoor centre courtyard which felt like you were sitting in a tropical garden! I think during our stay we tried almost everything on their dinner menu, never being disappointed, favorites going to either the roast duck or the beef tenderloin! It also seemed like we had our own personal waiter catering to our every need, very impressed. The rooms are very tastefully decorated and seemed like staying in a Victorian mansion which apparently it was before it was renovated into a hotel. We highly recommend this hotel to anyone without any hesitation!

review_title: Off to a rocky start, but recovered nicely
review_text:
We stayed here 2+1 nights on our way into and out of Costa Rica. The hotel is located in a neighborhood that looks iffy when you land from North America, but you get accustomed to most houses and shops in San Jose fortified with chain link fences and barbed wire after a while. We weren't sure the GPS was working correctly right up until we got to the intersection that the hotel is at.
We had a standard room the first two nights. The room was located in the ground floor courtyard area. The room itself was immaculately clean and comfortable, even tastefully finished. The next morning we were woken up by birds outside our window, which, even though sounds delightful, is a bit of a pain when it's 5 am and tired after a long flight, all we wanted was to sleep in. There are also plenty of guests leaving early in the morning for day trips from San Jose, and it was noisy beginning at 6 am.
The restaurant is very well reviewed, but frankly, I don't see what the fuss is about over the food. Dinner the night of our arrival was very average. The decor is wonderful, very appealing visually, and the desserts are good if overpriced.
The hotel does not have a pool, but the two rooftop hot tubs are inviting. The staff is pleasant enough, with a sort of detachment that comes with bigger hotels.
The final night of our visit, we had the family suite which cost about $50 more, but was completely worth it. The noise level was much more acceptable in this upstairs suite. It comfortably sleeps 5 in two rooms. On the eve of our departure from CR, we ate at Kalu's - a sandwich and pasta kind of place where the yuppies hang out- about a 10 minute drive from the hotel. Delicious!
The hotel is definitely not within walking distance of the central downtown area, especially if traveling with kids. However, the roads are easily navigable with a GPS and a hotel map.

review_text:
This hotel belongs to a small organization of "Distinctive small hotels" which would be the exact contrary of the plastic luxury. The old house, with old photographs on the walls, really tells what this organization is all about.
We usually don't stay in expensive hotels and, given the wide variety of hotels, B&B, etc. available in San José we wouldn't have picked Grano de Oro, except for a bit of extravaganza and interest generated by comments. Expensive it is, but worth every dime.
To begin with, the personalized welcome was warm, flawless and friendly (as is usually the case with "ticos"), though we walked in and after 10 days on the beach, in the jungle, what not, and a 6 hours drive, rain, fog, etc., we didn't look like we belonged in there. Service continued to be like this throughout.
We got the "luxury" room #5, 3rd. from the cheaper rooms. Impecable, every day. In the morning you can see why: 3 people go about fixing the rooms and checking every corner.
We didn't have meals at the restaurant because the menu was too "international" and expensive, but in any case, we walked through it. You absolutely must too. Ticos use wood in a manner that is fascinating in general, but the way it's used here is beyond description. A real pleasure to look at. We did have breakfast with local friends there, in one of those glorious morning of San José in the lovely patio. I paid $40 for 4 full breakfasts, con todo!
My 2 comments: Courtesy coffe in the loby disappears at 7:30... but there is coffe and coffee maker in the rooms and I guess you could get more coffe bags if you used it the evening before.
I would also suggest to include at least a continental breakfast in the price of the rooms. Anyway, if we want to splurge in San José next time, nothing will convince us to go anywhere else.

review_title: Simply elegant with very good food
review_text: Stayed one night at this hotel before heading home after a few days on Costa Rica. Service at reception was lovely and even before you see them, the hotel seems to warm up the area it is in. The room we stayed in was simple with afloat screen tv, immaculate bathroom and comfy bed. The room had VERY well functioning air conditioning and a very homey feel. The hotel is not a big chain or fancy in any way but you will enjoy it (take it from a picky traveller). The Resturant has the feel of among the more elegant places you may find in andalusia Spain. The food was very good - something admittedly I found lacking at other places we tried in Costa Rica. The drinks are excellent and wine listing fairly comprehensive. In a nutshell, try the hotel for a comfy feel and hit the Resturant for an elegant, romantic good tasting meal.

review_text: A georgeous hotel with friendly and attentive staff that look after your every need. A little away from the hustle and bustle of downtown which adds to the peaceful ambiance of the place. All the main attractions of San Jose are a short (and cheap) taxi ride away. We stayed 2 nights, the room was excellent, very clean and a lovely view oer the central garden. I would highly recommend the hotel restaurant. The court yard is a superb environment for breakfast (try the passion fruit juice) and lunch, great food and very attentive staff. Prices are reasonable for this level of elegance. Dinner was another level above in both food and sevice. Hotel staff was always immediately available for any need including taxis and finding suitable transporation for an early trip to the airport for 4 adults and lots of luggage.

review_text:
This hotel is lovely. Driving through San Jose at night, we were getting a little nervous about finding the place, but GPS pulled through and the wonderful staff was amazing. The overnight parking is gated. I thought I had lost my passport at this point, and when the desk clerk saw how tired and frustrated I was, she upgraded our room. We were offered fruit juice in champaign flutes while she checked us in and everyone was so kind and helpful. The room was spacious and lovely and had an indoor patio with a fountain. Very romantic. We wished we had been able to stay for two nights, but our flight was canceled and we missed our first night. I would have given this place 5 stars if they had been able to give us any discount on the night we missed, but they charged us full price for two nights even though we only stayed one. The upgrade helped, and we would probably stay again if we flew a different airline. For the luxury, the price is fine.
I feel compelled to add, to my embarrassment, that I mis-set my alarm. Knowing we were concerned about getting our car returned in the morning and still making our flight, the desk actually called the room to make sure we were up and saved us from missing our flight, . I felt like an individual at Grano d'Oro, which is not always the case.

review_text:
We spent our last night of a 3 week trip to, Costa Rica here. During our trip we had stayed in mainly wonderfully rustic type accomodation, and so decided to treat ourselves to a bit of luxury for our final night. We were not dissapointed! We were a party of 4 (two couples) and booked a family suite with 2 bedrooms. The main room was very nice and plush and complete with everything you would expect,2 beds (1 double and 1 single) , ceiling fans, A/C, mini bar TV, telephone, wardrobe complete with 2 robes, coffee making facility with 2 cups. The smaller room had 1 double bed, A/C and TV. Considering that this suite had the potential to sleep 5, I thought it was a bit poor that we only had robes and coffee cups for 2, a minor point, I know, we didnt wear the robes and we got extra cups, but perhaps still worth a mention. The 2 rooms had an adjoining door. The bathroom which was between both rooms, (again accessible from both rooms), was a delight, without a doubt the best lit room in the whole of Costa Rica! complete with lots of towels, soap, shower gel, body lotion etc, hair dryer and big bath. If we found ourselves in the same situation again we would book 2 seperate rooms, the power of hindsight!
The hotel building is a lovely old converted house, complete with jacuzzi on the roof. The restaurant was lovely (pre book!) we ate our evening meal in the courtyard, being waited on by very attentive staff, glorious meal worth every colone! All the staff we had dealings with were cheerful and helpful a credit to the hotel. review_title: Impeccable hotel; a must visit in San Jose
review_text:
Outstanding hotel with charm, amenities, service, security, and professional staff. The airport cab service - arranged through the hotel for the "going rate" of $30. US dollars - was EXCELLENT, and Omar, deserves special recognition! The transition from the airport, associated immigration and customs into the city couldn't have been any smoother. Welcoming staff had smiles, social and linguistic skills, and an ambassadorial demeanor that far surpassed many hotels in the U.S. and made check-in efficient and seamless. The associated gift shop is certainly stocked with a variety of Costa Rica souvenirs as well as international postage stamps. The room itself was immaculate, incredibly comfortable, and spacious, and the bath/shower was delightful and exceeded expectations. The restaurant within the facility offered a wide-range of entrees with an interesting flair (for example, conger eel and calamari risotto) and the bar service was adequate. And the wine selection is good. It is important in the restaurant to make certain that one speaks slowly and distinctly; it is wise to remember that English is not the native language. The ambience and furnishings suggest a very judicious decorator, and the courtyard provides a backdrop steeping in romance, charm, and local flora. Breakfast in the courtyard is exceptional.
You will regret should you not choose this property for your overnight accommodations. I WILL go back to this property when visiting San Jose again.

review_text:
Generally San Jose is simply a stop over on your way somewhere else in the lovely country of Costa Rica. Hotel Grano de Oro is a wonderful oasis in this gritty city. You are welcomed with a a cool cloth and a tropical drink and immediately feel the stress of travel disappear. The hotel is lovely and impeccably maintained. There are little out of the way gardens and fountains as you wind your way to your room. We stayed 3 nights total on our way in and out of Costa Rica, so had two different rooms. Both were extremely comfortable with white tiled baths, crisp sheets, comfortable beds...rather than feeling like you are in an impersonal hotel you feel as if you are staying in an upscale home. However, that doesn't mean a B&B atmosphere, it's certainly a hotel with all the privacy of a hotel. The restaurant is elegant and the food delicious. There is both an inner courtyard open to the sky for al fresco dining and an interior restaurant with huge windows that can be open or closed depending on the weather.
The only negative is that the area around Hotel Grano de Oro is not attractive. Most of the properties are behind razor wire and high walls, though that is the case pretty much everywhere in the city, which is too bad. We did feel it was OK to walk to the local market and city center, but be careful of the uneven side walks and pot holes that are everywhere.
When we returned to Hotel Grano de Ora after our week long stay in the country it felt like coming home.

review_title: An elegant oasis in downtown San Jose
review_text:
My husband and I stayed here the first and last nights of our 2-week vacation. We had two different Standard rooms, which are the smallest, but they had plenty of space for us and our luggage. The bath in the first room had a large glass shower stall, while the second had a shower/tub combo; water pressure was great. The bedrooms had flat screen tv, mini bar (which we didn’t use), robes in the wardrobe, coffee maker, and comfortable beds with extra pillows. Everything was sparkling clean. There was free wi-fi available in the rooms, as well as two computers for guest use near the lobby. At check-in, we were given a welcome drink and a complimentary map, and staff service was warm and friendly, even on our 3:30 a.m. checkout for an early flight home. The hotel packed us a nice breakfast to take to the airport (our travel agency included breakfast in our arrangements).
We ate two dinners, one breakfast and one lunch in the hotel restaurant, and spent some time at the bar. Restaurant prices are somewhat expensive, but everything was delicious and beautifully presented.
I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone planning a stay in San Jose.

review_title: Sophisticated, refined with a very good restaurant
review_text:
This is probably one of the most refined hotels you will find in Costa Rica. This has become one of our must stay at hotels in Costa Rica. This was our fifth stay at this hotel.
The hotel is in a quiet area very near to down town San Jose. The gold museum is within walking distance. We have felt very safe walking around this area over day. I have no idea how safe it is in the evening but like many cities (like in Rotterdam, NL) we tend not to walk around cities at night anyway!
San Jose for those who haven’t been is not one of the prettiest cities to visit and the highlight of San Jose is the Grano de Oro hotel and its superb restaurant.
The hotel is a revamp colonial mansion and is beautifully furnished. Some rooms can be slightly noisy due to creaky floorboards but this is part of the charm for those of us who don’t like the characterless chain hotels.
The best thing about this hotel is its restaurant. Even if you are planning only to go bird watching or Zip lining in the jungle, pack some nice clothes and book this restaurant for an upscale dinner. The food and wine are refined and beautifully served. The crystal wine glasses and fine china will make you feel like a movie star from the back and white period.
No its not cheap but this quality of food in the Netherlands or Frans would cost you at least twice the price. Costa Rica is not known for refined cuisine but this would get at least one Michelin star if not two in Europe.
We would also like to thank the management of the hotel for the lovely fruit plate and note they left in our room thanking us for our returning visits. A special note also to one of the bellmen who was very helpful.
We love this hotel and restaurant!

review_title: Great building, location, service, atmosphere and restaurant!
review_text:
Victorian charm hotel (former family house) offers amazing service (love the coffee at 5 am!) and beautifully decorated rooms. We loved the hidden gardens! The only inconvenience was the lack of ventilation in the bathroom. And the water in the roof-located jacuzzi was just warm, not hot - so I did not use it in the breezy March night.
I love the location - in a walking distance from the museums and the national theater. Remember they are closed Monday - if you plan to stay in the capitol only one day, make sure it is not Monday.
The restaurant is as awesome as the hotel and has a great chef - MUST GO!

review_title: Beautiful spot for an overnight stay
review_text:
We stayed in San Jose overnight. Grano de Oro was the perfect spot. It was quiet and out of the way of the incredible traffic in San Jose, yet close enough if you want to get into town. I love historic hotels, and this is the home of a former coffee plantation owner. In the restaurant/bar area you can see the lovingly preserved details of the original home. The courtyard and fountain were very inviting, but it was too cold for us to dine there. We found the menu a bit heavy and pricey, but the food was delicious and there was a nice wine selection. Our room was spacious and well appointed. We had a deluxe room with 2 queen beds and 2 (!) TVs, which we never used, and free wifi.
We really liked the hotel's sustainability efforts. A nice blend of luxury and eco consciousness!

review_text: We arrived in San Jose from Denver, CO at 6:05am. After clearing immigration and customs, we were met by our driver and headed straight to Hotel Grano de Oro. We did not expect our room to be ready because of our early arrival and planned to check in, have breakfast and then go for a very long walk exploring San Jose. Breakfast was excellent and we were told that our room would actually be ready about an hour later. After flying all night we decided that if we even sat on the bed we would fall asleep so we went for our long walk and didn't return until 4 pm. Our room was immaculate and very comfortable. We ate dinner in the restaurant and were not disappointed at all. The food was superb, the presentation was very nice and the service was friendly and attentive without being overbearing. It was an excellent beginning to a truly memorable first time visit to Costa Rica. If you want to stay in downtown San Jose and want have good food, there just isn't any other place to stay.

review_title: Excellent location to see downtown San Jose
review_text:

Surprised that we could leave our windows opened (no a/c) all day and night without any "city" noise. Excellent sleep and good meals. Nice to be able to get out and see the city (within walking distance) and did feel safe walking around.
Would recommend this hotel, especially if you want to see and do something quite different than just sit on a beach. A very eye opening opportunity to see a different side of the country. Bought a lot of our souvenirs, snacks and beverages for our trip while in the city.

review_title: the perfect way to end our vacation
review_text: I wish we could have stayed here our first night in CR. Our travel agent had put us at Xandari for more money and quite honestly,,,, there was no comparison. The Grano de Oro is one of the finest hotels we have ever stayed in, and we are world wide travelers. Service was incredible and the people who worked there all spoke English and were lovely to talk to. Our room was on the second level and faced a tree with a birds nest. It was spacous enough, had a large flat screen TV, and a ceiling fan and AC that cooled us off at night. We ate breakfast in the courtyard on a beautiful sunny morning and it was great way to end our trip to CR. The only comment i have is that they do promse free WIFI in the rooms and neither rmy husband nor i could ever get the internet from our room; we had to go into the lobby area. But other than that, i would stay here again and highly recommend it.

review_title: Lovely boutique hotel for a brief stay in San Jose
review_text:
Lovely colonial building beautifully converted into a small hotel. The hotel about 20min walk to down town in an area that is not so great. There isn't that much around and we didn't feel that safe at night going out. That said I wouldn't go to San Jose for the location more for a stop over. We went downtown and didn't like it that much.
The hotel itself was lovely. We stayed there 2 nights at the start of the holiday and one night on returning to San Jose which we looked forward to throughout the holiday. The staff are really friendly and tried their best to help us with our Spanish! We stayed in two rooms, the first was much bigger than the second. The rooms are all different and the first one we had was beautiful with a lovely small private garden.
The food in the restaurant is very good and we ate there all 3 nights. The cocktails were also delicious and the bar area and outside courtyard are delightful.
The only reason I wouldn't give it give is because the service for one of our breakfasts was poor with a long wait and us having to ask again for things. This was out of character with the other days.
Overall a fantastic place which I would recommend and would come back to if I needed to stay in San Jose again.

Our rooms were beautiful--each opening out onto courtyards with fountains and amazing plants. We took advantage of the jacuzzi under the stars to wash off our traveller's tiredness from our long journey The beds are so comfortable.And the bathrooms are extremely well appointed. There are hardwood floors throughout. Breakfast was amazing, and the staff so accommodating. On our return stay at the end of our vacation, the staff at the desk were particularly efficient checking on our flight reservations for our return trip. I highly recommend this hotel..

review_text:
The Hotel Grano de Oro was a fabulous, unique property. Our room (the deluxe room) was wonderfully decorated with a king bed and didn't seem small at all.
We stayed two nights- one at the beginning of our honeymoon and one at the end, so we really were just there to sleep, not to see San Jose.
The staff was very professional and very helpful- we were greeted with a glass of fruit juice and a quick check in which was most appreciated given all the traveling we'd done that day.
The rooftop jacuzzi is very nice, although not very warm- more lukewarm than a true hot tub, but we still enjoyed it.
My only complaint is that the area doesn't feel very safe to me- it was dark when we arrived and we wanted dinner. After looking at the hotel menu, we thought it was pricy and thought we'd wander to see what else was nearby. After walking less than two blocks and noticing barbed wire coiled on top of each fence, we did not feel secure walking and returned to the hotel. I don't know that it was dangerous, but the barbed wire just didn't feel right.
We ended up eating at the hotel and the food was very good, though, as mentioned, a little on the pricy side.

review_title: Lovely and Unique in San Jose
review_text: My husband and I stayed at Hotel Grano de Oro on New Year’s Eve, in between our Windstar cruise and trip to the Osa peninsula. What a great place to stay for the holiday! Our room was comfortable, sparkling clean, and very cute. Dinner at the hotel restaurant (see separate review) was a lovely treat. The hotel was beautifully decorated for the holidays, and the staff was warm and helpful. The only disappointment is that breakfast is not included in the price of the room. Although this was not a surprise to us when we booked, once we got to Costa Rica it did start to seem odd, as every other place we stayed, even those very much less expensive, did have breakfast included. Still, we recommend this hotel for the restaurant, the hotel's ambience, and its originality. Each room is different, and as such, cthe hotel ompetes favorably against the many cookie cutter chains found in San Jose.

review_title: Our First Night in Costa Rica
review_text:
I do concur that this was a great hotel. We stayed 2 nights. The first afternoon we walked into the city center and were back in the hotel by dark. I was not concerned for safety, but had left all my jewelry stateside. As others have said, there is not much to see of San Jose. We enjoyed the hot tub on the roof three times, after returning from our walk downtown, and the next day before and after our city tour. It was nice that we were completely alone and only 1 other couple even came up to check it out.
There are a few things I wished I would have known before our visit. 1.) We really did not need to exchange money. Every place we went accepted dollars at the same rate we received at the bank in the airport. 2.) The hotel's water is treat and perfectly safe to drink. No need for bottled water. 3.) Asked for a "to go" breakfast from the hotel as we were leaving at 6:30 as the restaurant did not open till 7. Oh My Gosh...what a treat.

review_title: The best place to begin and end your Costa Rican adventure.
review_text:
The Grano de Oro is a beautiful converted mansion. We have stayed there upon our arrival to Costa Rica and after we vacation across the country we return to have one last elegant night before we return home. We first stayed in their standard room which is very nice but a little small. Since then we have found their room upgrades have given us a good deal more space and comfort.
The service cannot be beat. Everything from airport transfers to the helpful staff is always taken care of for you. One time our tour company forgot to pick us up and the Grano de Oro staff was able to contact the bus to stop on the outskirts of town and wait for us while the Grano de Oro driver whisked us there.
The restaurant has to be one of the finest in San Jose. You can choose indoor or courtyard seating. The food and selection is wonderful with many little special Grano de Oro touches of elegance. The service there is second to none. Just as you are thinking you might want or need something else, like magic they appear to take care of you. Be sure to try the bar. The drink menu has some special Costa Rican cocktails or you can ask the bartender to make you something special as to your own tastes at that time. In the morning you can have an American or Costa Rican breakfast in the restaurant. Another nice service is if you have an early morning departure you can preorder a sacked lunch/breakfast to be waiting for you to go.

The Hotel Grano de Oro is a beautiful building and although our room was a bit small, it had its own private patio with foutain that was wonderful! It was clean, the shower was good sized and the service was excellent!
No breakfast offered. I enjoyed my dinner but my husband was disappointed with his sea bass. Still, it was a lovely restaurant and we both really liked our time spent there.
San Jose was very much like any big foreign city - people everywhere, crazy traffic and many vendors selling average-ish souvenirs but we had fun walking around the central market taking in the local culture and got some good souvenirs from a store recommended to us by the front desk. I would definitely stop and ask the front desk for recommendations/directions if you aren't interested in "exploring" as San Jose can be difficult to navigate since not all the streets are labeled.

review_text: The great thing about the Hotel Grano de Oro is that most of us have heard not to spend that much time in San Jose, that there isn't much to see, etc. So when you pull up to HGO, you feel that you found a gem because it's such a wonderful hotel with tons of character. We stayed one night before we left for Tabacon and it was such a wonderful first night. We had a cute room facing an outdoor courtyard. There are multiple rooms scattered about the hotel with tons of winding hallways! The manager left us a tropical fruit plate since it was our honeymoon which was nice. The room was moderate sized and the bathroom spacious. Everything was extremely clean. The front desk was extremely helpful. We ate dinner the first night at the hotel which was delicious and then the next day, we had breakfast in the courtyard which was lovely!! We took the advice of the front desk and did a 3 hour walk through downtown which was great to just experience the city. We walked back to HGO and used their hot tub which was really nice (although not that hot). If there was more to do in San Jose or the hotel was closer to the airport, we would have stayed longer. The hotel does offer pickup from the San Jose airport to their hotel for $30 which was reasonable and our driver was super nice!

review_title: Charming ambiance and a superb restaurant on premises
review_text: This hotel was recommended to us by the company which designed our tour package. It is located in downtown San Jose and it is certainly the hotel of choice for the downtown of San Jose itself, although there may be other hotels in the suburbs of San Jose which may have advantages lacking in the Grano de Oro, specifically spacious grounds and/or outdoor recreation opportunities. The Grano do Oro has no swimming pool or tennis court, for example. However, it is a very charming hotel. The original hotel was located in a Victorian house which has been progressively expanded in a manner which is very tasteful and was cleverly done. The result is a maze like structure which permits the illusion of great privacy in each room. There are several courtyards upon which the rooms look out so that guests feel that they are in a little village of their own. The rooms are spacious and the bathrooms are very well appointed, with full bath tubs as well as showers. In spite of being downtown, the rooms are quiet. The restaurant associated with the hotel is touted as the best restaurant in San Jose. I have no way of knowing if this is true, but the hotel's restaurant is very good indeed. I highly recommend the Hotel Grano de Oro to anyone staying in Costa Rica's capital.

review_text:
We arrived at Grano de Oro after a very long day. We had been told that San Jose was not the safest city so we did not want to stay in the downtown area. I found this hotel online and saw that it had great reviews and I could not be happier that we chose this hotel. This was our last night in San Jose and we just came through to fly out of Costa Rica.
On our way to the hotel, we passed many sketchy neighborhoods and my husband even made a comment of, "Where is this hotel again?" and then all of a sudden the beautiful hotel appears out of nowhere. We arrived at night and realized that the area was much better during the day and there are actually a few other similar styled boutique hotels.
Our room could not have been more beautiful. We had hardwood floors, a comfy bed, impeccably clean and nice bathrooms. When you walked out of our room, it opened into a jungle styled courtyard that had birds and plants. It was very beautiful and peaceful.
The hotel was quiet and the restaurant was delicious. Even if you do not go to the hotel to stay, I believe food and the ambiance in the restaurant are worth the visit alone.
This hotel was one of the Costa Rica Small Distinctive Hotels and I would most definitely go back to this hotel or try one of the others that have earned this classification.
Friendly, helpful staff and absolutely beautiful hotel. Highly Recommended

review_title: Exquisite Boutique Hotel in San Jose
review_text:
We fell in love with this hotel at first sight of the foyer!
It is an eclectic mix which somehow works to give it an unique charm and style.
Obviously an amalgam of different buildings, its corridors meander at unlikely points while stairways sprout unexpectedly to take you to what should by logic be a downstairs room. Getting hopelessly lost in such a small hotel is part of the fun.
The decor is period, and there are period pieces of furniture and other decorations scattered throughout the buildings and the rooms, adding marvellously to the charm. This could have been overdone, but someone knew when to say "when."
There is a nicely appointed dining room with a mouth-watering menu, and a coffee shop that fills a partly covered courtyard and that serves breakfast and then snacks throughout the day.
Reception, along with the rest of the staff are extremely welcoming and make checking in as smooth as possible. Any queries or requests are dealt with expeditiously and with a smile.
This seems to be a Costa Rican trait, particularly in evidence here - nothing ever seems to be a problem, and whatever it is they do it with a smile!
The rooms are wonderful, again period style with large double beds and bathrooms. Seats and coffee table with coffee maker. TV. We had an upgrade and our room had an exquisite water feature in a little annexe which was extraordinary.
I would strongly recommend this hotel. It is a welcome antidote to the ersatz style dished out by the big chains.
I would highly recommend this hotel -

review_title: A Piece of Gold in San Jose
review_text:
My husband and I stayed at Grano de Oro for one night (Chrismas day). We were pleasantly welcomed and had a quick check-in. We stayed in room 14- first floor. It was a small, well-appointed, and clean room. The window looked out to the side of the house, but didn't make the room feel closed in. Note: The hotel was previously a private home. You can hear people shuffling about above and around. You may want to book a room on the 2nd floor.
The hotel has three or four parking spaces in the front, but also has a big parking lot just across the street. The hotel and parking lot are under camera surveillance for security's sake. It is also complimentary. There are also security guards outside of the hotel 24/7.
The hotel is located just two blocks from Paseo Colon (main street). You can walk down from there to the pedestrian only shopping area.
It has two small hot tubs on the upper floor- private and well-maintained.
We had Christmas dinner in the hotel restaurant- excellent cuisine and great, friendly service. We had a table facing the courtyard- added to the ambiviance of the evening. We also had breakfast at the hotel in the morning- delicious and again, friendly service. They have a great selection of local juices, like cas. Try it!
San Jose is good to stay for a night to start your journey to other more scenic and active locations. So, when you need to have that night- stay at Grano de Oro!

review_text:
We stayed at the Grano de Oro for the last day of our 3 week trip to Costa Rica in December 2011. I was dubious as to what to expect as service standards we had experienced in our travels around the country were marginal at best. But my fears quickly dissipated.
The service was great - starting with the welcome drinks, to the owner personally helping us with our luggage, to sharing the birthday cake the hotel baked for all guests and staff to celebrate the hotel's 25th anniversary. We had the two bedroom family suite, which faced the garden. The room was immaculately clean, well appointed and spacious. With the exception of some very noisy guests coming in late at night into the room next to ours (all the noise stopped once they entered their room), if was quiet and we had a great sleep. In the very early morning when we checked out, a complimentary coffee station was set up so that we could have fresh coffee on the way to the airport. Awesome.
The arrangements made by the hotel for our airport transport were also flawless. And the gift shop attached to the hotel was one of the best we had seen in our travels through Costa Rica - it was small but had a very, very good selection of items and was reasonably priced.
But the highlight of our stay was dinner in the hotel's restaurant - in the centre courtyard under the stars. It was a fabulous gourmet meal - complemented by the beautiful setting.
The owners - fellow Canadians - have done a great job refurbishing this original coffee plantation mansion over the years into the elegant boutique hotel it is today. We would definitely stay here again.

review_title: Nice hotel, iffy location, great service
review_text: We stayed at the Grano on three different nights in December and it was a good experience. The property is really well done and the rooms are nice. Lots of hot water. The only thing I would watch out for is the exchange rate and transactions at the attached restaurant. The bills we received upon check out were not what I signed for in the restaurant and the exchange rate was 520 Col. per dollar which was higher than anywhere else we went in Costa Rica (two weeks). I was told the exchange rate had changed but if I added a 1000 Col tip one night it should not be 1008 Col the next day. Just a bad way to do business for such a nice place.

review_text: I have to tell you. I never ever take the time to write reviews of any Hotel, however I was inclined to write one now. My wife and I just returned from an 8 night trip to Costa Rica. I hated Costa Rica as it is an overpriced over rated country and would rather spend my money in Hawaii or some other Caribbean Island, however the only bright spot of our entire vacation was our layover in this wonderful Hotel Grano de Oro. I must say that I have stayed in some of the finest hotels in the world, Four Seasons, Ritz Carlton, St.Regis, etc. Our stay at this little hotel was up to par with some of those larger hotel chains. Although Costa Rica as a whole was disappointing, this Hotel was the best part of my trip. The service, the rooms, the staff, and the food was incredible. We stayed two nights when we first arrived and another night on Christmas Eve. The restaurant was excellent and we thoroughly enjoyed a dinner with the family. I want to thank everyone at this Hotel for making our stay as pleasant as it could be. Please don't change anything as you are a perfect Hotel. For those planning on going to Puerto Viejo, Cahuita, or any other part of the Caribbean side of Costa Rica....DON'T! That area is full of crooks looking to screw you out of your money and it is a drug infested crap hole. The only bright spot of our trip was this great Hotel. So thank you for making my vacation half way decent while we stayed at your Hotel.

review_text: We capped off a weeklong trip to Costa Rica with a one-night stay here before flying out the next morning. Our travel agent had tried to put us up in a Holiday Inn, but my high-end daughter searched the internet and found this place which cost only a tiny amount more. All the places we stayed previously were supposed to be superlative but weren't. This place really was a Holy Cow! experience. It was aboslutely gorgeous, the food was incredible and the service even more so. I was beginning to despair about nice hotels in a third world country (actuallly Costa Rica seemed second world, if there is such a thing.) The hotel surroundings weren't especially gorgeous, bu they weren't bad to walk around and I am very nervous in cities. There was no city noise in the hotel, the beds were super-comfortable and the entire experience was an absolute delight and huge sigh of relief. Thank you Grano de Oro!

review_text:
We had one night to kill in San Jose, at the end of our Costa Rican vacation. The Hotel Grano de Oro was the perfect hotel for this purpose. The rooms are clean and luxurious (perhaps the beds are a bit too soft, but they ARE luxurious). The staff is friendly and helpful, the food at the restaurant is absolutely delicious, the hotel facility is beautiful and well-appointed. Everything was decorated up for Christmas, and it was beautiful! We also really enjoyed the beautiful music coming from the next-door convent (?), orphanage (?)..... while they held their religious services Saturday night.
The only downside to this hotel is its location. It is close to downtown San Jose, which, it turns out, has very little to offer to the tourist. It is truly the downtown of a large city, where the shops are mostly discount shoes and clothing, aimed at residents of the inner city. We spent a morning walking around, hoping to find some last minute souvenirs. We had been directed to the downtown area, but truly found nothing. We did eventually find an artisan craft area at the far end of town. It is telling that two different hotel front desk people warned us to be careful while walking around. One told us that the area is safe, as long is there is daylight. The other told my daughter that she should remove her little necklace and earrings before going out.
The Grano de Oro itself is fantastic! It definitely rates 5 stars, if it could be picked up and moved to an better location.

review_text:
Beware, and know what you are reserving before it's too late. Hotel Grano de Oro is located within walking distance of downtown San Jose.... but its is a long walk in a very questionable area. If you are looking to feel safe or comfortable walk.... think again. Our first morning as we were leaving I was stopped by the doorman and asked where we were going. When I said downtown I was told to remove my little gold necklace. Seriously?? I have traveled the world and have never had to worry about a thin gold necklace. Just to be clear, although downtown San Jose is a "one time" must visit, it is on the rough side, a huge fist fight broke out right in front of us - not a comfortable experience!
OK, back to Grano de Oro, for the price point, you can do much, much better. We reserved the family suite as my husband I were traveling with two of our adult children. We got two double beds and one twin, and one bathroom. Personally, I don't define a double bed and a shared bathroom as vacation! Also note, there is no breakfast included making it even a worse value.
Lastly, before you reserve, note the cancellation policy - they are not willing to make any changes! They didn't care that we were unhappy. I think Hotel Grano de Oro has survived on its restaurant. We made a strategic decision not to eat in their there as we didn't want to hand them any more money. I'm sure it's very good, so my strong suggestion would be to skip the hotel (you will do much better anywhere else) and rather just go for a meal and check out the restaurant.

review_text: My husband, oldest son and I recently traveled to San Jose, Costa Rica to visit another son who is traveling abroad for a semester. We stayed at the Hotel Grano de Oro in San Jose' and it was PERFECT! The room was large and spotless. The bathroom had all that we needed. The bedding and the linens were just right. The decor of the lobby, the restaurant and the hotel was just beautiful, yet very relaxing! But, the thing that made the hotel so wonderful was the staff. We were there for 7 days and spent a lot of time at the hotel as it rained all day, every day for the entire trip. Thank goodness all the staff spoke very good English as we don't speak any Spanish. The staff was kind, helpful and just plain old fun. This hotel is truly an oasis in the middle of a developing country/city. I would definitely stay at the Hotel Grano de Oro again AND highly recommend it to anyone who is thinking of traveling there. One minor point however, don't expect to walk to anything. Anything and everything is either a taxi ride or bus ride away. That said, don't let that deter you from staying at this hotel. The staff totally took care of us in all aspects of getting to and from the hotel. The restaurant in the hotel is not to be missed. Everytime we ate there we just wanted to come back for more. This includes breakfast, lunch and dinner. The decor of the restaurant was just gorgeous, the food was exquisite, the presentation of all the food was extremely creative and the service was awesome. I would have loved this restaurant just as much if it were in London, Paris or Rome!

review_title: Like a trip back in time to an era of elegance, class and sophistication.
review_text: This was our third visit to Costs Rica but our first to San Jose. Regrettably, unlike so much of this beautiful and wonderful country - my favourite in all the world - the capital city has little to offer. Nevertheless, I would always be happy to start and end my trips there in the future and to return to this simply lovely hotel, which is one of the best I have stayed at anywhere. It is beautifully presented, the rooms are immaculate (with the most comfortable beds ever!) and the staff friendly, helpful and efficient. The restaurant is sheer elegance and sophistication, and makes the dining experience a real pleasure. The food is also extremely good - certainly no more expensive than good hotel restaurants in Panama City, Lima or Cusco. Whilst it is tempting to keep such a gem to oneself, i would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone visiting San Jose, and I wouldn't want to stay anywhere else in the city.

review_title: Good option for business travellers too
review_text:
I regularly stay at this hotel, as I need to visit San Jose on a monthly basis. Being a boutique hotel has it's advantages and disadvantages, of course. The rooms vary from one to the other, and you don't accumulate points in a loyalty program. But then again, loyalty programs are meant to replicate the kind of service that small hotels like this one can provide.
The daytime staff are very friendly, and remember you from one stay to the next. I usually get the same room every time I visit, and once, accompanied by my wife, I got a free upgrade to a grand suite.
It is true that the difference in friendliness between daytime and nighttime staff is surprising, and there is street noise to contend with. To that I would add that the table and chairs in the rooms are not the most comfortable for working.
On the other hand, the location is very good if your business takes you downtown, and the hotel is near the Sabana Grande park, which is a good option for exercising.
A highlight is the restaurant, which is well known in San José in it's own right.
Overall, a hotel worth becoming a regular at.

review_title: Loved the hotel, the architechure, atmosphere, food, ....
review_text:
An old mansion turned into hotel, Hotel Grano do Oro is an excellent place to stay, It is charming and peaceful (it was great that you were in a very nice hotel without long hall ways, large halls, elevators, ....) Very tastefully decorated. We stayed there for 3 night. The restaurant was excellent: the food was great, the atmosphere was very formal, but the waiters were so warm and friendly and would do everything to make you happy. It is beautiful, with gorgeous stained glasses, a large courtyard in the middle. Definitely go there if you are in San Jose.
One other thing: they have a nice gift shop.

review_text:
We arrived at this beautiful hotel directly from the airport and were upgraded from a Standard room to a Superior room free of charge. The room was lovely and the bed was the most comfortable and the shower had the most pressure of all of our hotels in Costa Rica. We didn't get a chance to use the rooftop hot tub as we were only here one night, but the view from the roof was pretty neat.
At check in they provided us with a city map and once we settled in, we decided to explore downtown San Jose a bit. Since it looked rainy, the hotel provided an umbrella for us to take just in case. We ended up needing it on our way back!
The hotel provided a laptop with free internet access so we could email our family and let them know we had arrived safely. The only thing I wish they would have offered was a free phone to call internationally, as my parents don't have internet and we had to wait until we got to our next hotel to call and let them know we had made it.
We ended up eating dinner here and the food was good, but not great, and a little overpriced in my opinion. However, the tres leches cake was the best that we had in all of Costa Rica. Amazing!!! We also had breakfast here in the morning in the courtyard and my mango creme french toast was wonderful. The best breakfast of our trip! My husband's omlete was good he said, but nothing special like my french toast!
Overall we had a great stay and left with fond memories of San Jose and the Grano de Oro.

review_title: A classically beautiful hotel with great service
review_text: Ten years ago, on my first trip to Costa Rica, I noticed a beautiful old house being renovated as we were driving to the airport. I asked the driver and he said it was being made into a boutique hotel. I made a mental note that if I returned, that would be where we would stay. Voila! This last June, we had a wonderful return trip to visit relatives and spent our first (and only ) night at the Grano de Oro. Dining in the exquisite restaurant, my husband remarked that this was a super way to start the trip! We loved everything about the place: service was friendly and excellent; our room was upgraded and we were able to have a room opening to a lovely garden patio. Whenever I emailed with a question, they responded quickly. Indeed, it was a great way to start the trip.

review_text: Staying here was the only thing that made our visit to San Jose worthwhile. The hotel and rooms are beautiful. The hot tubs on the roof make a beautiful respite from what is a hectic and dirty city. Despite being outside, they were surprisingly quiet. The staff are incredibly friendly and helpful, and they gave us detailed directions to our next stop as well as great recommendations on local restaurants. The parking area has a locked gate, and there is security outside the hotel at all times. We were able to walk to the main part of the city from the hotel, although it may be a bit far for some people. However, cabs are readily available. Also, the restaurant easily had the best food we ate in Costa Rica. It had a beautiful setting with very professional and formal waitstaff. It was so good that we ate dinner and breakfast there even though we stayed only one night. For such a nice restaurant, it was surprisingly affordable, too. Overall, we were underwhelmed by the city, but our stay at the hotel made it worth it.
